Sebagaimana diketahui, but now the u. government is taking control of a huge portion of Venezuela’s oil. S. And, pressed by economic need, long-held nationalist convictions about oil, starting with the need for sovereign control, are giving way to a more complex web of perspectives.

#529. Estonia bans Russian athletes as backlash intensifies

📅 13 Nov 2026

Estonia bans Russian athletes as backlash intensifies

Tanggal: 13 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/articles/cm4gn9lvlgy2o?at_medium=RSS&at_campaign=rss

Estonia has become the latest country to say it will not allow Russian or Belarusian athletes to compete on its territory as a result of the ongoing war in Ukraine.

It comes after Norway, Finland and Canada made similar announcements.

The moves come amid a mounting backlash over the reinstatement of athletes from Russia and Belarus.

In September, the International Ski Federation (FIS) relaxed its rules, saying competitors from the two countries would be granted access to its events "provided that they sign a declaration of neutrality".

They had previously faced more stringent background checks on any voluntary link or paid duty with the military.

Participation remains limited to individual events, with athletes banned from displaying national symbols such as flags, anthems or uniforms.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, however, it has now emerged that estonia's government has written to the fis, claiming that allowing entry to competitors from russia and belarus would undermine the country's support of ukraine, and present an opportunity for propaganda. It said a ban issued in 2022 will be maintained.

In a statement issued to BBC Sport, the FIS said it "is committed to offering full support to athletes, national ski associations and local organisers - with most of which we have a long-standing relationship - in the process of navigating what we know to be a very complex situation.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, "with that said, the individual neutral athlete policy is clear in stating that notwithstanding eligibility, the host country visa and entry policies remain in place and are determined solely by the host country. FIS bears no responsibility for denial of visas or entry to any person granted eligibility under the FIS Individual Neutral Athlete Policy. ".

On Thursday, Scandinavian neighbours Norway and Finland both said they would also block visas for Russian athletes because of the war in Ukraine.

Sebagaimana diketahui, norway is preparing to host the cross-country skiing world cup next month, while finland is due to stage the figure skating world championships in march. The International Skating Union (ISU) has said it "believes that athletes should not be punished for the actions of their governments in a world where, sadly, many conflicts are ongoing", and that it was "seeking clarifications" from officials in Finland.

This comes in the wake of last month's decision by the Court of Arbitration for Sport (Cas) to overturn a ban of Russia by the International Ice Hockey Federation (IIHF), a move condemned by the British, German, Finnish and Czech federations.

Diungkapkan bahwa russia have been suspended from competing in iihf events since the country invaded ukraine in february 2022, but the russian ice hockey federation (rihf) then successfully appealed that decision at cas. The court said that IIHF arguments citing safety and security were "not supported by sufficient evidence", but the Hockey Federation of Ukraine said the ruling caused "special outrage".

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the canadian government has since informed its hockey authorities that it will not issue visas for russians to play in next month's world junior championship, including those who currently play for teams in canada, as long as the war continues. A number of countries had said they would refuse to play against Russia, if they were allowed to take part.

Despite the controversy, the return of Russia and Belarus to international sport has been gathering pace this year.

In March, several athletes from the two countries were allowed to compete under their national flags at the Winter Paralympics after partial suspensions by the International Paralympic Committee were lifted.

In July, the International Olympic Committee (IOC) provisionally reinstated Russia to its competitions, stating a ban introduced in 2023 after the invasion of Ukraine was "no longer applicable".

Diungkapkan bahwa however, sports federations can still enforce their own eligibility criteria. While World Gymnastics, World Aquatics and World Boxing have all removed restrictions on Russian athletes competing, a total ban has been maintained by World Athletics.

Last month, it was announced that Moscow will host the 2030 World Weightlifting Championships - the first time an Olympic federation has chosen to stage a global event in Russia since the 2022 invasion of Ukraine.

‘We have further to go,’ says Huw Pill after increase to 4% last month as Bank seeks to tackle rising inflation.

The Bank of England will probably need to raise interest rates next month and again in early 2027 to combat rising inflation, its chief economist has said.

Sebagaimana diketahui, signalling a sharp rise in mortgage payments for an estimated 2. 3 million homeowners who will have to refinance their loans next year, Huw Pill said that while the decision to nudge interest rates from 3. 75% to 4% earlier this month was a “significant step” towards getting monetary policy into a better place, “we ⁠have further to go”.

Pill told the Financial Times: “My view would be, we will see evidence that motivates further rises,” adding that the central bank would “do ‌what is necessary to get inflation back to 2% through time”.

The chief economist is one of a number of the Bank’s policymakers who believe the UK economy has gained in strength over the last year, handing workers the power to bid up wages.

Sebagaimana diketahui, recent figures showed the economy grew by 0. 7% in the third quarter, to give an annual rate of growth that was only surpassed by the US among the G7 group of wealthy countries.

With inflation expected to rise to 5% in spring next year, driven by high oil and gas prices as a result of the Iran war, Pill expects public and private sector workers to demand substantial pay rises, which would keep inflation high for a longer period.

Pill said he considered an end to the US-Israeli ‌conflict with Iran and a fall in energy prices to be a “very low probability”, signalling to the newspaper that he was poised to vote for another ​quarter-point increase next month.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, “my bias, for what it’s worth, is that i worry about the inflationary impact being magnified by second-round effects,” he said, adding that he believed the central bank should have acted sooner to combat inflation. “In my ⁠view, we waited too long. ”.

While the Bank has not seen evidence of wage increases or companies being able to pass on higher costs to consumers, Pill said the absence of evidence was not evidence of absence.

Sebagaimana diketahui, “as we go into next year, we will begin to see some evidence, and it could play out in one direction or another – we’ll see. ”.

Berdasarkan laporan, financial markets expect uk interest rates to rise to almost 5% in 2027. Pill said these expectations were “not outrageous”, hinting that he could vote for more substantial increases in the cost of borrowing at the next meetings of the Bank’s monetary policy committee (MPC) because the “ability to be ​modest [in the scale ​of rate rises] has diminished”.

Diungkapkan bahwa city analysts have interpreted the increasingly hawkish comments of pill and other mpc members as making an interest rate rise in december almost inevitable. #533. Microsoft says services fully restored after global outage hits governments

Tanggal: 14 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.theguardian.com/technology/2026/nov/14/microsoft-says-services-fully-restored-after-global-outage

Tech company says operations restored to all customers and regions affected by one of worst IT failures in years.

Microsoft has said its service has been fully restored after a massive outage that saw widespread disruption to governments, businesses and public services around the world.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the technology company said on saturday morning it had restored service to the remaining customers affected by one of the worst it failures in years. On its Microsoft 365 status page, the US-based firm said: “We have completed our efforts to address the underlying issue of the incident and restored service to the remaining impacted customers and regions.

Diungkapkan bahwa “further updates can be found at mo1550821 in the microsoft 365 admin center. ”.

Diungkapkan bahwa the outage, which began on thursday, affected governments, courts, healthcare services, businesses, airlines and banks. Governments including those of Japan, Singapore and Australia reported that the hours-long episode had affected some of their operations.

In the UK, where NHS England has a five-year deal to use Microsoft 365, vital public services were hit, with hospital staff resorting to paper records and one union reporting that ambulance services had suffered a “serious impact”.

The already backlogged court system was also hit, with juries in some cases being sent home early or prisoners not being sent to court, while at Minshull Street crown court in Manchester staff scrambled to locate a fax machine.

In the US, school districts told parents they must reach out by phone or online apps to contact their child’s school, while staffers at the House of Representatives told Politico they had lost a day of work.

One detention facility in Colorado said they were unable to take online bond payments to release detainees and told anyone needing to post bond for immediate release to do so in person at the jail.

Diungkapkan bahwa in australia, many people who rely on microsoft 365 reported being unable to access their inboxes, including at councils, courts and schools. The federal police and Asio, Australia’s national domestic security and intelligence agency, were also affected by the outage.

Asio’s director general, Mike Burgess, said the agency’s systems “operate on multiple levels”, adding that they had been affected “on one level, yes, but not completely”.

Across Europe, government agencies in the Netherlands, Belgium and France reported problems, with a French municipality instructing citizens to use the phone instead of emailing.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, in japan, government email services became unavailable and staff resorted to text messaging. The shipping firm Sagawa Express was unable to accept some online reservations while Taisho, a major pharmaceutical company, said it was having to handle orders by phone.

The Indian airlines IndiGo and Akasa Air said their email support services were affected, and Taiwanese security firms, life insurers and investment trust companies told Reuters that fund management services had been disrupted.

Sebagaimana diketahui, users reported that microsoft 365 services, including outlook, teams and the ai assistant copilot, were interrupted. Downdetector, an online tracker, said it received outage reports from users in more than 70 countries and territories.

Diungkapkan bahwa approximately 430 million people use microsoft 365 apps, microsoft said on its website. Problems began at about midday on Thursday in the US and at 6pm in the UK.

A weekly dive in to how technology is shaping our lives.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the washington-based company apologised on friday for the disruptions and said the outage was “not related to cyber” or artificial intelligence agents. It said the incident “was introduced by an issue during an earlier network capacity upgrade that surfaced” after a recent network change.

Diungkapkan bahwa the disruptions offer the latest example of the cascading problems that can erupt when multiple communications and technology platforms depend on the same provider. The outage has fuelled concerns in the UK about an overreliance on a small number of tech companies.

Diungkapkan bahwa steven murdoch, a professor of security engineering at university college london, told the guardian an outage of this size was usually “the result of some surprising interaction between systems. Each of the systems is normally quite well understood but interactions between them are complex and frequently the cause of large outages like this.

Sebagaimana diketahui, “it’s very hard to build a complex system without there being some risk of some failure. ”.

Tim Clement-Jones, a former chair of the House of Lords artificial intelligence select committee, said the widespread outages of vital government services were an “I-told-you-so moment” highlighting Britain’s dependence on US tech.

Berdasarkan laporan, jeremy singer, a professor at the university of glasgow’s school of computing science, said: “this problem serves to emphasise the dependence we have built on one company’s digital infrastructure, and may lead us to question whether we need more resilience in our it ecosystem. ”.

The total number of people affected was not clear, but Microsoft said in January it had more than 450m paid commercial subscriptions to its 365 services.

The Eurovision Song Contest will crown its first Asia champion in Bangkok on Saturday, in an event that will test whether a high-camp singing competition with an ardent fan base can appeal to audiences in a new market.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the inaugural eurovision song contest asia comprises artists and original songs from 11 countries: bangladesh, bhutan, cambodia, laos, malaysia, mongolia, nepal, the philippines, south korea, thailand and vietnam. local time (8:30 a. It will be live-streamed on YouTube at 8:30 p. m. m. Eastern) and broadcast by television stations across the region.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, eurovision has been a fixture of the european cultural calendar since it began in 1956. Past winners include Sweden’s ABBA and the Canadian chanteuse Celine Dion, who represented Switzerland in 1988.

Sebagaimana diketahui, asian artists have readily embraced the kitschy outfits and spectacular sets that are part of eurovision tradition, with costumes that include traditional dress, as well as feathered capes and sequined corsets. Malaysia’s performer plans to enter the stage in a giant teardrop.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, but the eurovision format has not been tested in asia. Fans and regional partners have expressed concern in recent weeks that budget constraints, production issues and weak audience demand could imperil the spinoff. Organizers say the contest could take time to build an audience.

Berdasarkan laporan, “it would be profoundly arrogant to think that just because we have a heritage brand and a huge global audience for the european show, that we would walk in and demand it to be the same here,” said martin green, the european broadcasting union’s director of the eurovision song contest. “Like any new thing, it needs to find its roots. ”.

Berdasarkan laporan, two previous attempts to take the competition to asia were abandoned by the european broadcasting union, which owns eurovision, and its partners in the region. A Eurovision spinoff in the United States, NBC’s American Song Contest, ran for one season in 2022.

Diungkapkan bahwa the asian edition kicking off on saturday is far smaller than its european counterpart. Eurovision organizers said they were in talks with more countries to join future seasons. They include China, Japan and India, whose music industries have global reach.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, “bringing the world together through music is a fundamentally good idea,” mr. Green said. “Europe shouldn’t keep it to itself. ”.

Sebagaimana diketahui, with about a half hour until showtime, some 7,000 people are waiting to watch the youtube stream (i am one of them!). The contest has a long way to go to match up to the European edition of the contest. The YouTube stream for that had 11 million views in May (even though most people in Europe watch on traditional TV broadcasts).

When the Eurovision Song Contest is staged in Europe, it’s always one of the year’s biggest television events.

Sebagaimana diketahui, this year’s was in vienna in a 16,000-capacity arena. It cost the host broadcaster some 16 million euros, or $17. It involved 35 participants and a glittering four-hour finale broadcast live to tens of millions of viewers across Europe. 7 million.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, that makes the debut eurovision song contest asia look like a tiny event. It will take place in a 5,000-capacity venue in Bangkok with just 11 competitors.

Inside the theater, fans are jostling for spots in front of the stage and near the so-called green room, where the artists will sit after their performances until the results are announced.

Sebagaimana diketahui, it’s less than an hour before showtime at the one bangkok forum, and crowds of fans have gathered outside the theater, taking photos, buying memorabilia and sneaking in a quick bite of dinner. Organizers have handed out cardboard signs with the performers’ images — I’ve been told that they’ve run out of South Korea and Thailand.

Francesca Regalado reported from Bangkok, where she will cover the Eurovision Song Contest Asia on Saturday.

Berdasarkan laporan, the eurovision song contest, europe’s long-running singing competition, is expanding into asia for the first time on saturday, with singers from 11 countries vying for the title. The New York Times is covering it live.

Sebagaimana diketahui, this is the third attempt by the european broadcasting union to develop an asian spinoff of the high-camp competition. With Bangkok as host city, it will test demand in Asia for an international competition based on original songs.

The Eurovision Song Contest Asia could either be Eurovision’s first successful foray into another region — or a one-off flop like NBC’s American Song Contest.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the asian edition will have a far smaller pool of competitors than its european counterpart, which typically includes over 30 countries. But it will include South Korea and Thailand, whose pop songs have found international audiences.

The contest will be live-streamed on YouTube on Saturday night local time (Saturday morning Eastern) and broadcast by government-owned and commercial television stations in the 11 participating countries.

As in Europe, the winner will be determined by votes from a panel of judges and viewers from around the world.

Sebagaimana diketahui, eurovision, which began in 1956 as an experiment in synchronized programming by public broadcasters across europe, has grown into a weeklong spectacle with an international fan base. The competition’s 70th edition in May was won by Dara, a singer who represented Bulgaria, with the dance-pop hit “Bangaranga. ”.

Diungkapkan bahwa organizers have unsuccessfully tried to replicate the contest outside europe. The American Song Contest, which pitted singers from 56 states and territories, ran for only one season in 2022. An Australian public broadcaster, SBS, called off its yearslong attempt to bring Eurovision to Asia in 2021.

This time, the Asian project got off the ground partly because pop music from countries like South Korea, Japan and Thailand has global appeal, said Assaf Blecher, the executive producer of the Eurovision Song Contest Asia.

“It’s the right time for something to happen, with the evolution of music from Asia and the curiosity of Eurovision fans to see what’s happening beyond Europe,” he said.

The 11 countries, in order of performance, are Vietnam, Cambodia, Laos, Mongolia, Bhutan, the Philippines, Bangladesh, Thailand, South Korea, Nepal and Malaysia.

Berdasarkan laporan, asia’s three largest media markets are conspicuously missing. Mr. Blecher said that broadcasters from China, India and Japan had been in talks to join the competition, but did not sign on in time to meet the deadline for entries.

Berdasarkan laporan, to stage the competition in asia, eurovision had to overcome a fraught relationship with the continent’s broadcasters. In 2018, the European Broadcasting Union canceled a contract with China’s Mango TV, a provincial-government-owned streaming platform, after it censored elements of that year’s Eurovision show, including a gay love story depicted in an Irish singer’s performance.

Berdasarkan laporan, last year, china, india and vietnam sent singers to intervision, a cold war-era song contest that russia revived after it was expelled from eurovision in 2022 over its invasion of ukraine. A Vietnamese singer, Duc Phuc, won the contest with a song inspired by a mythical folk hero.

Berdasarkan laporan, each country will send a singer who won a national contest with an original song. For emerging singer-songwriters like Nepal’s Pratik Himal Rai and Bhutan’s Nyendra, winning their national contests was life-changing.

Berdasarkan laporan, others, like malaysia’s aina abdul and vietnam’s toc tien, are established pop stars with decades-long careers. Bangladesh’s entry, Beatmosphere, is a six-member a cappella group that formed in 2009.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the 11 acts will perform a wide range of genres: love ballads, a hip-hop track, a rock song and dance anthems. Some artists, like Thinla of Laos and Junhee of South Korea, will sing in English.

Each act will have three minutes to perform onstage at the One Bangkok Forum, a newly opened auditorium in central Bangkok that can seat around 5,000 people.

Sebagaimana diketahui, once a performance is complete, a jury in each country will rank the songs. Those rankings will be converted into point scores for each singer, from zero to 12.

Sebagaimana diketahui, public voting — in each country and among youtube viewers watching internationally — will also be used to allocate points. The public and jury scores will then be combined to work out the winner.

Viewers from participating countries cannot vote for their own nation’s act.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, a qr code will be shown onscreen to direct viewers to the eurovision asia voting website. Each user will have eight votes for free to distribute to at least three songs. They can purchase up to 10 extra votes.

Berdasarkan laporan, the organizers said that they expect most viewers to watch the show from their phones and personal devices, not on television. Last year, the European contest's final competition received more than five million views on YouTube.

Berdasarkan laporan, the winner of the asian contest will be invited to perform at the european edition next year, though not as a competitor. And unlike in Europe, the winning country will not automatically be chosen to host next year.

On Saturday, the biggest and longest-running international song contest will make a leap into unknown territory.

Eurovision, the pan-European competition famed for zany gimmicks, slick, sometimes over-the-top staging, the drama of its complex voting system and, occasionally, for outstanding music, celebrates its 70th birthday this year.

And to mark it, the European Broadcasting Union is trying out audiences in Asia.

It's an idea that's been talked about for two decades but never materialised, despite many false starts.

Until now - Eurovision Asia will hold its first grand final in Bangkok, starting at 20:30 ICT (13:30 GMT).

Transferring one of the most successful television formulas that has worked in Europe for 70 years to Asia has not been straightforward, says Sarun 'Note' Kungbunpot, a Eurovision enthusiast and Thai singer who has won several competitions in this region.

Sebagaimana diketahui, "it's still very new in asia. I'm not sure many people have heard about it yet," he says, adding that he thinks it will take a bit of time for audiences to adjust.

"When we look at contests in Thailand, the Philippines and Korea, we actually compete based on the singer.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, "it's all about popularity â fans are looking for their idols. I think this needs to be communicated clearly. But Eurovision is all about the song, not the singer. ".

MANG x DAOU have winning form, having previously been declared champions of the show Thailand's Chosen One.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, then there is the long history of eurovision in europe. It began in 1956 as a project to encourage greater cultural exchanges in a Europe which was trying to forge a common future after two world wars.

Berdasarkan laporan, this was the very start of the age of mass television ownership, and eurovision became such a fixture it is now an indelible piece of europe's shared cultural heritage. It has no such resonance in Asia, and arrives in this region in the digital age, when traditional TV formats are struggling to cut through.

Only 11 countries are taking part in this first Eurovision Asia contest â host Thailand, along with Malaysia, the Philippines, Vietnam, Cambodia, Laos, South Korea, Mongolia, Bangladesh, Nepal and Bhutan.

Asian giants India, China, Japan and Indonesia are noticeably absent, although there are negotiations ongoing to try to get them into next year's contest, assuming there is one.

There have also been problems with the organisation of this event.

A sudden million-dollar (Â£760,000) budget cut just three weeks before the final meant many of the technicians familiar with staging Eurovision were not brought to Thailand, and there have been a number of staff resignations too.

Eurovision fans - and there are many passionate followers around the world - have noticed, criticising audio and lighting in rehearsal videos.

Watch: Eurovision is coming to Asia - but will it succeed?.

Berdasarkan laporan, the contest's unusual voting system will be unfamiliar to asian audiences. Like in Europe, Eurovision Asia will determine the winner through a 50/50 mix of public voting and national juries from each of the 11 contesting countries, as well as a 12th "rest of the world" category.

Anyone can vote - you get eight votes once you register - but you cannot vote for your own country's contestant and you must give your votes to at least three others.

Berdasarkan laporan, the public and jury votes are then converted into points. The most popular song among the Bhutanese or Mongolians, for example, will get 12 points from those countries, while the song ranked last will get zero - the famous "nul points".

JUNHEE is a solo singer-songwriter from South Korea who produces bright, mainstream-sounding music.

Berdasarkan laporan, in europe, there have long been reports of co-ordinated voting to back neighbours, for example the four nordic countries voting for each other. This seems less likely in Eurovision Asia, but political differences, for example between Thailand and Cambodia after their border war last year, could influence how their audiences vote.

Diungkapkan bahwa filipinos, with their passion for singing, are expected to be enthusiastic participants and the 11 million who live overseas might make a difference. But as most live and work in countries which are not participating, their votes will only go into the "rest of the world" pool.

Sebagaimana diketahui, for bhutan, with a population of less than a million, this is a rare chance to shine on a global stage, which puts some pressure on 24-year-old thukten nyendra, the singer representing the himalayan kingdom in bangkok with his song lhayi semo (the angel). Before coming here he had never left his country or been on a plane before.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, "i'm not a star. I'm just Nyendra over there," he told the BBC. If I really make it through all of this, it would mean the entire freaking world to us. Actually winning would mean the world to us. "Nobody knows me. But Eurovision has given me a huge platform. ".

Nyendra, Bhutan's 24-year-old contestant, is also a journalism graduate.

The other characteristic of Eurovision is the song format â no more than three minutes, no more than six people on stage, and no backing band, only taped music.

This encourages performers to prepare elaborate, sometimes outrageous choreography and stunts to impress the audience â think Poland's My SÅowianie in 2014 with models in traditional costume churning butter on stage, or the Finnish heavy metal band Lordi donning flamboyant monster outfits in its 2006 entry.

Sebagaimana diketahui, there has also been a long association of eurovision with lgbtq+ artists. Eurovision Asia includes Malaysia and Bangladesh â where same-sex activity is illegal â and there are no visible LGBTQ+ elements this year.

Diungkapkan bahwa performers have been using the last days of rehearsals before the final to try to make their stage acts as striking as possible. Thinla from Laos has abandoned the short, sequinned dress she wore in the first video of her infectious reggaeton song Bae and is adopting Lao hill-tribe costume for her and her backing dancers.

Thinla's music blends traditional Lao and contemporary genres, such as pop, R&B and dance.

Perhaps the most ambitious choreography is in Vietnamese singer TÃ³c TiÃªn's song Em TiÃªn ("Fairy Maiden").

It has been exhausting just watching her rehearse the elaborate moves and costume changes for more than an hour at a time.

The entry from Bangladesh's Beatmosphere, Tumi Ele ("You Came"), is unusual as an a cappella and beatboxing performance by six men with little backing music.

The youngest contestant is 19 year-old Carmelle Collado from the Philippines, whose bubbling confidence and strong stage presence in her song Sobra-Sobra ("Too Much") belie her youth.

"I'm actually quite scared because I'm the youngest, but also really happy," she told us.

Sebagaimana diketahui, "the song is about feminine energy. It's about being brave, strong, fierce, and it's about how strong Filipino women are. ".

Bangladesh's Beatmosphere blend traditional vocal harmony with beatbox culture.

Carmelle Collado rose to prominence through a selection of televised singing competitions in the Philippines.

Eurovision is famous for putting unknown acts onto a global stage, and introducing musicians who went on to become megastars â think Abba, little known when they won in 1974 with Waterloo, and Celine Dion winning in Ireland in 1988.

Because of the lack of public awareness of Eurovision Asia many of the finalists chosen for this first contest are already well known in their home markets.

Berdasarkan laporan, aina abdul is perhaps the most famous singer in malaysia, known as much for dramatic costumes as her impressive vocal range. Her song Bluest Sky â which she told us was inspired by her late cat Hiro â is a strong contender to win the contest.

Malaysia's Aina Abdul laughs as designer Melinda Looi adjusts her dress before a media shoot.

Diungkapkan bahwa abdul's spectacular dress, by malaysian designer melinda looi, who has travelled to bangkok with her, had taken 600 hours to make, she told me. She said its glistening texture, made from materials brought from Italy and China, is meant to represent moving water.

If all goes well on the night, the organisers are hoping this could be the start of an expansion of the hugely successful Eurovision brand into a region which, after all, has half the world's population.

Activists dumped rocks off Norfolk coast on site of Burnham-backed project in protest against seabed trawling.

The giant offshore windfarms backed by Andy Burnham this week may face unexpected stumbling blocks after Greenpeace activists unwittingly dumped about 15 tonnes of boulders on to the site as part of a campaign against seabed trawling in the North Sea.

Greenpeace created the “boulder barrier” to safeguard harbour porpoises off the Norfolk coast by dropping giant stone blocks, each weighing up to 2 tonnes, on to the sea floor to prevent a method of fishing known as bottom trawling.

The barrier will pose an additional challenge for the green energy developers because most of the boulders were dropped on to the site earmarked for one of the UK’s biggest planned windfarms, known as the Norfolk Vanguard project.

Greenpeace began dumping boulders on to the site, without consent from the marine authority, days before the prime minister told the Cop31 summit that the UK would invest £1bn of public money in the Vanguard West and Vanguard East windfarms in what is believed to be the biggest investment of its kind in UK history.

The Guardian understands that Greenpeace checked the seabed for any existing cables, pipelines or shipwrecks, but it was not aware of the plans to build the Vanguard East windfarm.

The creation of the underwater barrier in one of “the most heavily trawled” areas of the southern North Sea was timed to coincide with the premiere of the BBC’s Blue Planet III documentary, narrated by Sir David Attenborough.

Some boulders bear the signatures of celebrities including Simon Pegg and Benedict Cumberbatch, who have voiced marine conservation documentaries, and agreed to support the Greenpeace campaign.

Diungkapkan bahwa however, they are likely to be removed within months after renewable energy developers agreed a £12bn deal alongside the uk government to begin building the offshore windfarm next year. Industrial fishing activities, including bottom trawling, are also likely to move elsewhere to avoid the construction area.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the guardian understands that the offshore wind developer, the german utility company rwe, is in talks with greenpeace to verify the exact placement of the boulders so that they can update the seabed surveys they began last summer. The company is also investigating any potential impact to the construction of the project or its undersea cables.

A spokesperson for RWE described its communication with Greenpeace as “constructive” and said the company would “continue to investigate the precise implications” for the Norfolk Vanguard East project.

Will McCallum, the co-executive director of Greenpeace UK, said any suggestion that the boulders would cause a genuine obstacle was “absurd”.

“Anyone familiar with offshore wind in the North Sea knows that energy companies routinely move naturally occurring boulders from the seabed before building windfarms,” he said.

“Some of these boulders can be 10 times heavier than those we placed.

Sebagaimana diketahui, “greenpeace has long championed offshore wind and will continue to do so. While we wait for this windfarm to be built, our boulders will provide an essential barrier to destructive bottom trawlers that are decimating the seabed in this protected area. ”.

The documentary claims that poor screening and welfare checks are having serious consequences for some of the asylum seekers.

Sebagaimana diketahui, last may, the high court ruled that a home office policy change forcing torture survivors to share rooms was unlawful. The accommodation at Crowborough is in large dormitories.

Berdasarkan laporan, the home office’s decision to accommodate asylum seekers on two former military sites – crowborough, and wethersfield in essex – have triggered opposition from local residents. Plans to use three other sites – Bicester, Barnham and Linton-on-Ouse – have caused a similar outcry, mostly around fears about asylum seekers causing a rise in violent crime. However, very low levels of even minor crimes have been recorded by police at Wethersfield and Crowborough among asylum seekers at the two camps.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the crowborough site is run by clearsprings ready homes. According to its latest accounts, it is generating millions of pounds in income every day from its asylum accommodation contracts. Its boss, Graham King, has become the first asylum accommodation billionaire.

Berdasarkan laporan, the documentary footage shows that, although two comprehensive welfare checks are supposed to be carried out each month by clearsprings welfare officers, some staff appear to admit cutting corners and not asking all the questions they are required to ask of asylum seekers. Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, staff appear to admit to falling behind on the 1,000 welfare checks they are supposed to carry out each month saying: “we’re so fucked. ”.

Diungkapkan bahwa concerns about an asylum seeker can be flagged on their file. A welfare officer is filmed telling the undercover reporter: “Those flags mean nothing” and that “nobody ever looks at them again”. ”.

The undercover reporter says he has identified four or five survivors of torture who should not have been sent to the military camp.

Sebagaimana diketahui, louise calvey, the executive director of the charity asylum matters, raised concerns about the findings of the undercover documentary. Her organisation has a campaign to accommodate asylum seekers in communities not camps. “The reports of torture survivors being accommodated on military barracks are appalling,” she said. “Brave survivors endure appalling experiences arriving to a country where they thought they’d be safe – a supposed civilised country, placing them in camps without the support they desperately need.

The Home Office and Clearsprings have been approached.

Members of Congress and advocates warn that returning people to their home countries could be a death sentence.

Dozens of Afghans who are currently in the US but fear being deported back to Afghanistan along with a larger group and possibly killed by the Taliban are experiencing “fragile relief” this weekend after it appeared that the Trump administration had put on hold plans to remove them within days.

Members of Congress and advocates have repeatedly warned that the deportations could effectively be a death sentence.

Berdasarkan laporan, a flight originally scheduled to transport the group out of the us on election day earlier this month had stayed grounded after a federal judge issued a court order temporarily blocking its departure to afghanistan or neighboring pakistan. The whole group numbers more than 150 Afghans, the New York Times reported. And the AP previously reported that the federal government intends to route these detainees to their home country via Pakistan.

Berdasarkan laporan, then, as the temporary court order expired last weekend, immigration advocates battling to prevent the deportations talked of dreading that the detainees could be forced to leave the us during the week of 16 november. This prospect was based on a rescheduled removal date given for at least one Afghan man currently in Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) detention who was due to be on the flight.

As that date loomed, suddenly there was another development amid frantic advocacy efforts.

Late on Tuesday, it was learned that that detainee, along with a handful of other detained Afghans on the original flight manifest, now no longer had a specified departure date issued by the US government.

Some immigration lawyers also reported that their Afghan clients had been moved from staging facilities to long-term detention facilities, suggesting they would not be forced onto a deportation flight in the coming days after all.

Amid some confusion and often few details from the administration, Shawn VanDiver, founder and president of the US non-profit coalition #AfghanEvac, said that a sensation of “fragile relief” had descended on the people involved.

Berdasarkan laporan, some of the afghans in the targeted group have relatives who assisted the us war on afghanistan after the terrorist attacks on the us on 11 september 2001 that drove out the taliban, vandiver said. He had already called Donald Trump’s efforts to remove Afghans from the US cruel and being done in “a heinous matter” as a scare tactic against others.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, “in a matter of days, these allies were told they were being sent through pakistan into the hands of the taliban, then told they were safe, then told that nobody knows. It’s whiplash inflicted on people who already survived a war,” he said. “These men and women kept their promise to America, and it’s time we kept ours by ending these removals for good. That isn’t immigration policy. ”.

VanDiver has slammed any option to use Pakistan as a conduit for “forced rendition”.

Diungkapkan bahwa immigration advocates are hoping continued pressure will result in further delays and the ultimate cancellation of that flight and any others planned for the coming weeks. In the meantime, #AfghanEvac is pushing what will become the newly Democratic-controlled Congress in January to pass a bipartisan bill that has been drafted and would give Afghans who are already in the US temporary protected status (TPS) through July 2029, with a vetting process. The US supreme court in June allowed the Trump administration to strip such protections, including from Afghans.

Such legislation would “keep people we already vetted and brought here from being sent back to the Taliban while their cases are decided”, VanDiver said.

Among the passengers reported to be on the blocked flight were Afghans whose relatives helped American troops, women, at least one gay man and members of the minority ethnic Hazara group – some who have said they were previously beaten by the Taliban.

Diungkapkan bahwa human rights first, the us-based human rights group, has warned about “grave, systematic dangers” for afghans returned to afghanistan. That includes “arbitrary detentions, executions, public flogging, and retaliatory violence”, as well as restrictions on basic freedoms for women and girls.

The Department of Homeland Security (DHS) said in response to questions and a request for comment that the agency complies with all lawful court orders and that US Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) does not comment on or confirm prospective removal operations, for operational security reasons, and the safety of its officers.

Sari Arvey, director of policy, refugee and immigrant rights at Human Rights First, said that the Trump administration’s targeting of Afghans reflects a broader trend of creating arrangements with other governments to send people back to war zones, security crises and countries that don’t have diplomatic relations with the US.

The US suspended relations with Afghanistan after the Taliban government took over in 2021, forcing a scrambled US evacuation.

The Trump administration has held secret talks with Iran about deporting Iranians via a third country, and last Sunday an attorney reported that the US deportation flight of Iranian nationals headed to Iran via Pakistan was abruptly canceled, according to the AP.

Berdasarkan laporan, the trump administration also is increasingly deporting immigrants to such “third countries”. The supreme court is still litigating in what circumstances the federal government can deport people to regions they have no connection to, though in late September, the court ruled on an emergency basis, allowing Trump to continue this practice.

Federal law is designed to prevent the US government from forcing someone to return to a country where they are likely to face torture.

The DHS said in a statement that immigrants sent to a third country “receive notice and an opportunity to challenge their removal unless the Department of State is given diplomatic assurances from destination countries” that they would be safe upon return.

Berdasarkan laporan, more than 60 concerned lawmakers in congress signed a letter to the dhs and the state department, citing relevant law and also calling for the cancellation of any deportation flights of afghans or iranians to their home countries, either directly or through any other country. “The United States is also bound not to return anyone to a country where they would face torture, and that obligation does not disappear because a flight makes a stop along the way,” the letter stated.

Sebagaimana diketahui, in another letter, new york congressman gregory meeks and us senator jeanne shaheen of new hampshire, both democrats, wrote to pakistan’s ambassador to the us, urging the pakistani government not to collaborate in any operation to fly afghans to pakistan and then expel them over the border to afghanistan. With five salt mines situated partly or entirely underneath Great Lakes waterways – in Fairport Harbor, Detroit and Cleveland, and two over the Canadian border in Ontario – a growing concern is that weeks later, Morton Salt officials say they still can’t find the source of the water intrusion.

The salt is extracted by drilling and using explosives, and while the distance between the bed of Lake Erie and Morton’s Fairport Harbor mine is in excess of 1,000ft (305 meters), decades of blasting and the presence of underground aquifers could contribute to significant subterranean rock movement, say experts.

Tanggal: 14 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/nov/14/measles-kalshi-polymarket-betting

Experts warn of risks of platforms hosting bets tied to US public health – including vaccine mandates and drug trials.

Berdasarkan laporan, the sign was pasted on a construction fence next to an elementary school in the brooklyn borough of new york city. “Vaccines,” it proclaimed in bold capital letters against a blue star-spangled background – appearing, at first glance, to be like any other public health message on the importance of getting vaccinated.

But at the bottom of the sign, in smaller letters, it read: “Will any state end vaccine markets?” It was accompanied by the logo for Polymarket, an online prediction market where users can log in to wager on the outcomes of nearly any event – including, now, public health.

Berdasarkan laporan, polymarket joins kalshi, another online prediction market, which began offering health-related predictions over the summer. Users can wager on when the US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) will approve a skin-cancer vaccine, or whether the US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) will change its vaccine recommendations. They can also bet on drug trial outcomes and approval; they can bet on how many cases of measles the US might see in 2026 and whether it will lose its measles-elimination status this year.

Berdasarkan laporan, “i am not surprised,” said matthew eisenberg, professor and chair of health policy and management at the johns hopkins bloomberg school of public health. “Kalshi and Polymarket will list contracts on anything with a checkable outcome. ”.

Despite being functionally “identical” to regulated gambling, prediction markets are largely unregulated, said Lia Nower, a professor and the director of the Center for Gambling Studies at Rutgers University.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, “gambling right now is like the wild, wild west,” she added. “There’s no federal regulatory body that’s really prescribing any limits on any of this, or just minimum guidelines for states to follow – so anything’s possible. ”.

Sebagaimana diketahui, prediction markets position themselves as financial derivatives, rather than traditional bets, in a regulatory loophole, nower said – which means they operate under federal commodities laws, with oversight from the us commodity futures trading commission, and are not regulated by states as gambling operations. Several states have filed lawsuits against the companies alleging that they function as gambling sites.

Diungkapkan bahwa advocates, officials and lawmakers could place bets on ending vaccine mandates at the state level, for instance, and then introduce new laws or policies to do so; there don’t appear to be any laws against that, nower said. There are bets on when certain officials will leave health agencies, which could be affected by resignation or termination decisions.

Berdasarkan laporan, predictions could also affect how drugs are tested and regulated, critics say. Trial participants could purposefully change their behavior to affect outcomes; drug companies could change the timing of trials.

Berdasarkan laporan, predictions on fda decisions and trial endpoints “create a payoff for anyone with nonpublic information”, like agency reviewers, trial investigators and legislative staff, eisenberg said. Prediction markets may create their own safeguards, like employment checks at sign-up, “but the risk isn’t necessarily that a reviewer takes a bribe – it’s that the market now rewards leaks”, he said.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, polymarket did not respond to the guardian’s questions about the potential consequences for public health or medicine. Kalshi did not respond on the record to the same questions, but spokesperson Dani Lever argued that the predictions on drug trials and approvals would improve transparency.

Sebagaimana diketahui, “kalshi’s clinical trial markets are a pilot program aimed at a structural problem in drug development: the people who best know whether a trial will succeed are scattered, and their insight rarely reaches the public,” lever said in a statement. “Public markets avoid those barriers. ”.

Problem gambling is itself a rapidly growing public health concern.

Sebagaimana diketahui, gambling is a “big public health issue” that disproportionately affects people who are younger, black or hispanic and lower-income, nower said. 5% had some degree of gambling-related risk and 10. She co-authored a new report showing that more than half of young people, between the ages of 13 and 27, gambled in the past year – and among the young gamblers, 39. 3% were high risk for problem gambling.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, eisenberg’s research on online sports betting found that legalization is followed by measurable increases in treatment for depression and anxiety among young men. There have been some discussions after such findings to create state-level consumer protections – like deposit limits, self-exclusion, rules about advertising and funding for treatment paid out of state betting taxes, he said. “But the prediction markets sit outside all of that. ” Very little of the revenue flows to states through taxes to support such treatment.

“In effect, these are gambling products that have exited the only regulatory system designed to limit gambling harm,” Eisenberg said.

Sebagaimana diketahui, prediction markets are “really something that the government needs to clamp down on”, nower said. Yet “the federal government still has no federal regulatory body,” she added. There are no research centers at the National Institutes of Health focused on gambling, as there are for alcohol and drug abuse.

“It’s just unaddressed at the federal level,” Nower said.

States like New Jersey are moving to restrict the markets – and concerns include consumer protection and the potential for insider trading, Nower said.

“People with inside information or control over an outcome could potentially profit from what they call ‘event contracts’,” another word for the predictions, she said.

Diungkapkan bahwa this is the future, eisenberg said: “gambling on everything, everywhere, with fewer and fewer consumer protections. ”.

Berdasarkan laporan, yet he pointed out that public-health propositions on the markets were small, and he cautioned against seeing them as any sign of public sentiment. “Prices that small can be moved by a single trader and shouldn’t be read as public opinion,” Eisenberg said. “A few-hundred-dollar contract on the childhood vaccine schedule is not a forecast of anything. ”.

Berdasarkan laporan, within a week, the polymarket sign in brooklyn was vandalized. The bottom, with the Polymarket logo and the text on placing a prediction, was ripped away.

#554. ‘Enough is enough’: rising number of deadly ebike battery fires spark fear in New York City

Tanggal: 14 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026/nov/14/new-york-city-ebike-battery-fires-deaths

City has failed to build infrastructure that could reduce threat, and saw 400 fires, 83 injuries and 12 deaths this year.

Fires from lithium-ion batteries, which power ebikes and scooters, have become regular occurrences in New York, causing deaths and fear among residents, but the city has failed to build infrastructure that could reduce the threat.

Diungkapkan bahwa new york has seen a dramatic uptick this year in fires from the batteries. In 2025, there were 292 fires, 51 injuries and one death, according to the New York fire department (FDNY). This year, there have already been more than 400 fires, 83 injuries and 12 deaths.

In late October, four members of a family, including an 11-year-old boy, died in a fire caused by a battery in an ebike that was in the pathway to an exit of an 11th floor apartment in a public housing building in the Bronx.

Diungkapkan bahwa then recently in a fire at a home in brooklyn, six people died and nine were injured, including three firefighters and two police officers. Investigators discovered lithium-ion batteries at the scene but have not determined whether they caused the fire, the city council speaker, Julie Menin, said in a statement.

Diungkapkan bahwa “the presence of lithium-ion batteries at the scene is a serious concern, and more must be done to encourage and mandate safe storage practices. Enough is enough,” Menin stated.

London and Toronto have also recently seen a dramatic increase in lithium-ion battery fires, which are often caused by overcharging and defective or damaged batteries.

Some of that trend is simply because ebikes, often used by food delivery workers and commuters, have become more popular.

But in New York, the city has not executed its plan to build outdoor charging stations which would prevent people from plugging in the batteries in their apartments, where an overheated or defective battery poses a greater risk, experts say.

“There is a ton of red tape around this sort of new technology, and while it’s well intended to not let something new roll out too quickly, I think in this case, it is time to do something quickly,” said Laura Kavanagh, former commissioner of the FDNY.

Diungkapkan bahwa in 2025, there were 2. 2m ebikes imported into the United States, according to Light Electric Vehicle Association, double the number from just three years earlier.

In response to the increased usage and related increase in fires, the New York City department of transportation conducted a 2024 pilot in which it hired companies to offer battery-swapping cabinets where delivery workers could exchange exhausted batteries for charged ones.

The riders did more than 12,000 swaps over six months, and among participants, there was a 35% reduction in charging batteries at home, according to the city.

Berdasarkan laporan, following its success, the city announced that it would install 25 charging sites but not until 2027. The city first needed to “gather feedback on site selection, design and implementation”.

Diungkapkan bahwa in april, new york mayor zohran mamdani asked residents to provide feedback on where they would like the 25 cabinets. The city planned to make them available in 2028, the announcement stated.

In 2023, the city also announced that it received a $25m federal grant to build 173 electric-micromobility charging and storage stations at 53 public housing developments.

“This means that residents will no longer need to charge their ebikes in their apartments, what we find to be extremely dangerous,” Mayor Eric Adams said at the time.

At the time, the deputy mayor, Meera Joshi, said residents would start “seeing evidence” of the stations in early 2024.

Even though the Biden administration allocated the $25m for the infrastructure, the federal government has not actually provided the funds, according to the New York department of transportation.

Diungkapkan bahwa asked why the process has moved slowly, a transportation department spokesperson stated in an email: “the city’s strategy to reduce the risk e-bike battery fires focuses on getting unsafe devices off our streets and providing safe and convenient e-bike charging options” and the “outdoor battery swapping cabinets will make charging safer and more accessible for the thousands of delivery workers who rely on these devices to serve new yorkers. With the public feedback we gathered this summer, we’re finalizing locations for our public e-bike charging program before advancing to the design phase and remain on pace to launch the service in 2028”.

Meanwhile, Popwheels, one of the companies in the successful pilot, has installed about 45 cabinets around the city, according to CEO Baruch Herzfeld.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, he wants to install hundreds more around the city but has been stymied by a permitting process that he describes as “ludicrous”. He said it often takes six months for the city to approve one cabinet.

Berdasarkan laporan, “if i want to put a cabinet that they approve in a parking lot, i have to use an architect to do a drawing, and then they have to come and do an inspection of a drawing of an ebike battery cabinet in the parking lot,” herzfeld said. “This permitting process is why kids are dying. ”.

The city also often issues tickets to the owners of properties where Herzfeld has installed the cabinets, he said, for minor infractions like a fire extinguisher not having the proper tags or trash at the site.

Amanda Farinacci, the FDNY deputy commissioner public information, stated in an email that the tickets were not for “minor infractions but instead significant concerns”.

Berdasarkan laporan, “the fdny has been very serious partners with the micro-mobility/charging cabinet industry, being very accessible and collaborative to achieve solutions,” farinacci stated. To conflate our regulatory responsibilities with causing people to charge their batteries indoors is entirely misplaced and inaccurate. “We are a public safety agency and our mission is public safety. ”.

Kavanagh, who spent a decade at FDNY before leaving in 2024, argued that the department is focusing on “too narrow of a concern”.

Berdasarkan laporan, “i respect whatever concerns they have about the cabinet as real, but that is asking the wrong question,” said kavanagh, who now works as a visiting urbanist at new york university. If “a battery failed in that cabinet outside, it is almost certain that would do no more than property damage. You are comparing that to” 10 New Yorkers dying in fires in the last three weeks.

“This is just appreciably worse, and so I think we need to frame it that way,” she added.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the latest fire may spur the city to expedite its approval process. On Friday, Menin announced that the city council would hold an emergency meeting on 20 November to conduct oversight to ensure the city is properly enforcing existing laws and that the public is educated on best fire safety practices and lithium-ion battery storage.

Berdasarkan laporan, ebike fires “are something that can cause people to lose their lives as well as their livelihoods”, mamdani said on ms now after the brooklyn fire. “And so, we are really looking at every avenue we have to keep them safe. ”.

#558. Wolf Biermann at 90: The singer who defied East Germany

📅 14 Nov 2026

Wolf Biermann at 90: The singer who defied East Germany

Tanggal: 14 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.dw.com/en/wolf-biermann-at-90-the-singer-who-defied-east-germany/a-79915297?maca=en-rss-en-all-1573-rdf

Berdasarkan laporan, his life is a reflection of contemporary german history, which biermann has addressed via his songs and sharp wit. Turning 90, he’s as feisty as ever.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, he mocks donald trump and vladimir putin as "political lovers," denounces the "endless fratricidal war" over the palestinian territories, and repeatedly invokes "lady liberty. " It is a celebration of the freedom he once so painfully lacked in the former East Germany, and of the freedom people around the world still yearn for.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, these themes run throughout wolf biermann's new album "unterm haar nur himmel" ("beneath hair, only sky") released to mark his 90th birthday. The album's title is a characteristically poetic phrase coined by Biermann himself. It evokes the idea that however restrictive the world may become, the human mind and spirit remain free. Beneath the hair lies open sky: a metaphor for inner freedom, independence and imagination.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, biermann remains one of germany's most influential singer-songwriters, and at 90, he shows little sign of putting down his guitar. Often described as Germany's answer to Bob Dylan, the outspoken troubadour continues to weigh in on the issues shaping the world today.

Sebagaimana diketahui, in his recent song "moritat von den liebespaaren" ("ballad of the lovers"), he delivers a simple but urgent message: no single person can save the world, yet everyone can help make it a better place. Above all, the song is a call to take responsibility for one's own life rather than remain a bystander.

Diungkapkan bahwa this outspokenness was instilled in biermann early on. Wolf was just three months old when the Gestapo, Hitler's secret police, arrested his father. His father was a dockworker, a committed communist, a resistance fighter against the Nazis — and Jewish. When he was born in Hamburg in 1936, Adolf Hitler was already in power. He initially served time in prison before he was murdered by the Nazis at Auschwitz in early 1943.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, just a few months later, british and american bombers attacked hamburg, unleashing a devastating firestorm. When the air raid sirens sounded, his mother took him into an air raid shelter. "Nothing in my life has shaped me more," Biermann has repeatedly said in interviews. The house above them was burning.

Sebagaimana diketahui, yet biermann says his memories of that time are rooted in a profound sense of trust in life. A sense of security in the midst of the end of the world. Roaring corrugated metal, smoke everywhere. (. We stumbled out over the neighboring house and into the open. They had no chance. But I did. 40,000 people died. In an interview with the German magazine Chrismon, he recalled: "I pressed my face into my mother's soft coat so I could breathe. My strong mama. We searched for a way out. The firestorm lifted a burning roof into the air. ) Death was everywhere. ".

Diungkapkan bahwa his mother instilled communist and anti-fascist ideas in him with almost religious fervor. I was supposed to build communism. "My mother had only one goal after those dark years," Biermann recalls. "I was supposed to survive so that I could, as she put it rather grandly, one day take revenge for my father's death. ".

Berdasarkan laporan, in 1953, while countless people were fleeing from east germany, biermann moved there of his own free will — after all, communism was the official state ideology. In East Berlin, he studied political economy, mathematics and philosophy. His role models were writers Bertolt Brecht and Heinrich Heine. He began working as an assistant director at the Berliner Ensemble. He was just 16 at the time. He also began writing and performing his political songs.

Sebagaimana diketahui, he soon realized that life in east germany was far from the communist paradise he had imagined and he wrote about this openly in his songs. Even today, I'm amazed that I wound up cast in the role of the heroic dragon slayer. "The party bosses were torn," Biermann recalls. "They were delighted by this young poet who could play the guitar so beautifully and sing such cheeky songs. They thought they just needed to bring me into line. ".

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, in 1965, east germany's ruling socialist unity party, the sed, imposed a blanket ban on biermann performing or publishing his work. His East Berlin apartment, which was under constant surveillance, soon became a gathering place for dissidents and critical thinkers.

Sebagaimana diketahui, yet, to his great surprise, the east german authorities allowed him to travel to cologne, west germany in 1976. There, around 7,000 people flocked to see him. For four and a half hours, he strummed and sang, mocking the East German regime. His songs were so popular that bootleg copies found their way back to East Germany.

Sebagaimana diketahui, on november 16, while still on tour in west germany, biermann heard the news on his car radio that he had been stripped of his right to continue residing in the german democratic republic. The regime accused him of betraying and slandering East Germany. "I felt like the ground had opened up beneath me. I was overcome with fear, everything went dark," Biermann wrote in his memoirs.

Berdasarkan laporan, in a petition, leading east german intellectuals spoke out against the decision. In response, the regime stepped up surveillance of dissidents, imposed professional bans and jailed its critics. Several prominent public figures left the country.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, "the sed leadership expected an angry media response from the west. What they hadn't reckoned with was that, for the very first time, a group of respected East German writers and artists would make their protest public, disguising it as a humble petition," Biermann writes.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, biermann sank into a deep depression. "The world's conflicts take different forms in each generation," he says. "Not just because I had been torn away from the friends I knew and loved in East Berlin, but also because I had lost my familiar mortal enemies," he says. "But it's always the same struggle for freedom. He became involved in the peace and anti-nuclear movements and continued singing about the injustices of the world. ".

Berdasarkan laporan, the singer-songwriter plans to spend his 90th birthday at home in hamburg with his wife and manager, pamela. "I'm so old and I can feel my strength fading. For the first time in his life, he says, he's skipping the birthday party, even with his 10 children. And I know that the next day I have a major concert at the Berliner Ensemble," he told the German Press Agency (dpa).

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, and should he ever die, he says, he wants to be buried at berlin's cemetery where some renowned german writers and intellectuals have been laid to rest, among them bertolt brecht, anna seghers and georg wilhelm friedrich hegel. Quite a crowd, Biermann says. He still has a thing or two to discuss with them.

#559. Hungary: Millions in hidden cash found in Orban graft probe

Hungary: Millions in hidden cash found in Orban graft probe

Diungkapkan bahwa investigators discovered bundles of banknotes buried in forests and concealed in buildings. The money was seized during an investigation into a former minister accused of accepting millions in bribes.

Sebagaimana diketahui, hungarian authorities have recovered nearly $20 million (€17. 7 million) in hidden cash during a corruption investigation into a former minister under ex-Prime Minister Viktor Orban.

The country's newly established National Asset Recovery and Protection Office said Friday that investigators discovered the money during searches linked to former National Development Minister Miklos Sesztak.

The discovery is part of a sweeping anti-corruption campaign launched by Prime Minister Peter Magyar, who defeated Orban in April's parliamentary election.

The money was discovered during two days of searches in the capital, Budapest, and three Hungarian counties.

Investigators found large quantities of cash buried in forests, concealed in agricultural buildings, warehouses and residential properties, as well as stored in an expensive safe at a secluded location.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the recovered money included 5. 3 million), €2. 3 million, $15. 66 million (€2. 07 billion Hungarian forints (€13. 9 million) and $1. 26 million (€1. 08 million).

According to Finance Minister Andras Karman, 12 employees of the Hungarian State Treasury spent eight hours counting the banknotes using five counting machines.

The agency also released a video showing investigators kneeling beside large piles of bundled cash and digging into the ground in what appeared to be a forest at night.

Authorities said the seized money had been deposited into an account belonging to the Hungarian state treasury.

Sesztak served as Orban's national development minister between 2014 and 2018.

He is suspected of accepting more than $37 million (€33 million) in bribes and kickbacks connected to the purchase of overpriced used buses by state-owned transport companies and state construction projects.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the former minister was taken into police custody in late september. He has denied wrongdoing.

His lawyer, Gabor Papp, so far did not respond to a request for comment on the latest discovery.

Magyar described the recovered cash as a turning point in his government's efforts to tackle alleged corruption under Orban.

The discovery "officially marks the end of the Fidesz-KDNP mafia," he wrote on Facebook, referring to Orban's former governing coalition.

Diungkapkan bahwa "as of today, viktor orbán is a proven mafia boss. A fallen mafia boss. And Fidesz is a criminal organization," Magyar added.

Magyar's center-right, pro-European Tisza party won a landslide victory in April, ending Orban's 16-year rule.

The new prime minister has pledged to repair Hungary's relations with the European Union, which had been strained by years of disputes under Orban.

His government established the anti-corruption agency with investigative and prosecutorial powers to pursue suspected corruption and misuse of public funds.

Diungkapkan bahwa magyar has dubbed the campaign "operation purgatory. ".

Several other senior figures from Orban's time in office have been detained as part of separate investigations.

Among them is former central bank governor and economy minister Gyorgy Matolcsy, once considered one of Orban's closest allies.

Berdasarkan laporan, matolcsy is being investigated over the alleged misuse of a central bank foundation that received 288 billion forints ($818 million, €787 million) in public assets. He and other former officials under investigation have denied wrongdoing.

Police also detained Orban's younger brother earlier this week as part of an investigation into suspected human trafficking and influence peddling.

Sebagaimana diketahui, orban has condemned the investigations as political "tyranny" aimed at removing him from hungary's political landscape. He has described his brother's detention as an act of political revenge.

Berdasarkan laporan, according to a survey by pollster median published by news website hvg this week, 70% of respondents considered the anti-corruption campaign "very important. ".

A separate Median survey showed support for Orban's Fidesz party had fallen to 16% of voters by November, roughly half its level before the April election.

Sudan: Misery worsens amid plummeting aid for displaced people

Diungkapkan bahwa sudan's humanitarian crisis is exacerbated by cuts in international aid. Almost 34 million people are in need as war and drone strikes are making it difficult to deliver aid to the population.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the international organization for migration (iom) and the united nations high commissioner for refugees (unhcr) are sounding the alarm: serious funding gaps have depleted the supplies of emergency shelter and basic household goods intended for sudan. Without urgent provision of flexible funding, even more families will have to cope without adequate protection from extreme weather conditions, insecurity, violence and exploitation in the coming months.

Berdasarkan laporan, according to a recently published joint statement, $2. 62bn) is needed for the United Nation's Humanitarian Needs and Response Plan. 9 billion (€2. 4 million people in Sudan. This funding is intended to provide life-saving aid to 20. So far, however, only 47% of the required funds have been raised.

Diungkapkan bahwa a total of 33. Some 15. 4 million alone require emergency shelter and basic household items. 7 million people in the war- and famine-stricken country are dependent on humanitarian aid. However, due to a lack of funding, aid organizations have been able to assist only 10%.

Sebagaimana diketahui, more than three and a half years after the war began between the sudanese armed forces (saf) and paramilitary rapid support forces (rsf), sudan is still the site of the world's largest humanitarian and displacement crisis. 6 million people fled within the country to escape the escalating violence and more than 4. Another 5. 6 million fled to neighboring countries. However, their towns and infrastructure have been destroyed. About 8. 2 million have returned to their regions of origin despite the ongoing war. Fighting, drone strikes and logistical problems further complicate the delivery of humanitarian aid.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, between 40,000 and 250,000 people have been killed. Accurate or updated figures are not available as fighting continues, satellite-based internet communication is curbed, and many aid organizations and observers have left the country.

Berdasarkan laporan, "it's hard to imagine how people are supposed to survive," marina peter, chairwoman of the sudan and south sudan forum in germany, told dw. In large parts of the country, people have been cut off from humanitarian aid since the war began. Some have survived by eating roots. According to the Sudan expert, the fact that people are still returning to war zones from neighboring countries is also linked to shortages: Food rations have been drastically cut in refugee camps.

Diungkapkan bahwa ivo körner, sudan specialist at caritas international, criticizes the international community for the sharp decline in aid. "Globally, we're seeing a dramatic drop in funding for humanitarian aid," Körner told DW. It's not just the United States that has slashed its contributions; Germany and the European Union are also providing significantly less funding than they did four or five years ago, he said.

Diungkapkan bahwa in sudan, caritas international supports refugees and the communities hosting them with cash assistance, drinking water supplies, basic medical care and seeds. However, Sudan's Caritas' projects in 2026 have been financed exclusively through donations. While Körner hopes for additional funding from the German Foreign Office for Sudan projects, he predicts that funding opportunities will be significantly more limited than in previous years.

Diungkapkan bahwa according to sudan expert marina peters, the consequences of the crisis are becoming increasingly difficult to assess. Peter also notes that child mortality in Sudan is above average. "In many parts of the country, people have already been completely cut off from humanitarian aid since the start of the war," she told DW. However, it is nearly impossible to determine the actual extent of the crisis more precisely because the warring parties continue to obstruct humanitarian access.

Berdasarkan laporan, on october 23, the united kingdom and 31 other international partners, including germany, issued a joint statement on the looming famine in sudan. The countries are calling on the warring parties to allow unimpeded access for humanitarian aid and to refrain from attacks on civilian infrastructure. 5 million people — about 41% of the population — are suffering from acute food insecurity. According to the statement, 19. At the same time, they are demanding an increase in international aid funding.

Sebagaimana diketahui, while marina peter welcomes the appeal in principle, she sees a contradiction. "The question is: Who is this appeal actually directed at?" Most of the signatories have themselves systematically cut funding for humanitarian aid and development cooperation. The appeal to the international donor community is thus ultimately directed at the states themselves.

Meanwhile, the Sudanese government based in the country's capital Khartoum — led by General Abdel Fattah Al-Burhan's SAF — rejects all warnings of a famine.

Berdasarkan laporan, in a statement dated october 26, it claims that the food situation in the country is reportedly reassuring and that government reserves and ongoing agricultural production are sufficient to meet demand. According to Khartoum, the warnings from Western countries amount to a politicization of the humanitarian situation.

Berdasarkan laporan, peter criticized this statement as "truly cynical and almost perfidious. The government's claim that humanitarian organizations have unrestricted access also does not reflect reality, she said. In many places, aid continues to be obstructed.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, in addition to hunger and displacement, the threat to civilians posed by the use of drones is also growing. In the first three weeks of October alone, at least 306 people were killed in attacks. The Peace for Sudan Platform issued an appeal on November 5 calling for an end to attacks on civilians, markets, hospitals, and water and electricity supplies. According to the UN Human Rights Office, drones claimed the lives of at least 1,120 civilians in the first half of 2026.

Sebagaimana diketahui, "drone strikes are a major problem," caritas' körner confirmed. This makes local partner organizations all the more important, he said. They cause widespread anxiety among the population and often strike civilians. Added to this is the danger to humanitarian workers. They enjoy the trust of the local population, are deeply rooted in the regions and in some cases are able to reach areas that international aid workers can hardly access.
