Diungkapkan bahwa critical global issues at all these summits will include ai supply chains and governance, tariff reductions and the green energy transition. Trump’s focus has been on denuclearisation. A key regional focus will be on the South China Sea, where Beijing has built massive military outposts in disputed waters, as well as the gigantic Indonesian forest fire haze blanketing the region.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the humanitarian and security crisis in myanmar has become a perennial issue, as is status of taiwan, which china does not recognise. The self-ruled island is sending the founder of the tech hardware company Acer as its envoy to Apec.

For well over a decade, Washington’s engagement in the region has been coloured by concern over the rise of China, with the then president Barack Obama telling Australia’s parliament in 2011 that the US was “a Pacific power, and we are here to stay” – a policy known as the “pivot to Asia”.

The strategy of intense diplomacy and trade deals was adopted by Joe Biden, who hoped to gather allies on the continent who wanted to balance their relationships with both superpowers.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, some analysts see trump’s transactional style in asia as a continuation of the pivot policy. Still, the president’s volatility and unpredictability have spooked smaller nations, who regard China as a more predictable partner.

Jayant Menon, an economist at Singapore’s Iseas-Yusof Ishak Institute, said that countries in south-east Asia had been “laying the groundwork for a future with reduced dependence on the United States” by seeking deals elsewhere, including with each other and the EU.

“Amid persistent uncertainty and an administration determined to levy tariffs by any legal means, south-east Asia’s ability to ride out another round of tariffs depends on deeper regional integration and diversification beyond the US market,” he wrote this month in the East Asia Forum.

Beijing’s more predictable policies do not necessarily make it any more palatable for its regional neighbours, however, and the Chinese premier, Li Qiang, could have tough talks when he goes to Manila for the Asean summit, especially on the South China Sea.

Berdasarkan laporan, brunei, china, malaysia, the philippines, taiwan and vietnam have been locked in decades-long territorial standoffs in the busy waterway, which could sit on deposits of oil and gas. Diungkapkan bahwa diplomats at the asean summit will also be focusing on myanmar, which is seeking reintegration. Each country in the group is assessing how to deal with their isolated neighbour. The coup leader, Min Aung Hlaing, remains barred from Asean but is allowed to send a representative.

Asia’s week of diplomacy will be followed next month by the G20 summit in Miami, Florida, which Xi is expected to attend if US and Chinese relations continue to hold steady.

Declaring the current course "Trash Island", he announced in October it would be renovated over 15 months to create a space that "will be open to the Public while, at the same time, designed to the Highest Level of Golf and able to hold World Class Tournaments" - despite the ongoing litigation.

Sebagaimana diketahui, in a 30-page decision issued on saturday, reyes said the trump administration's justifications for the proposed course closures were pretextual, and that the government violated at least two federal laws "to meet an arbitrary deadline. ".

"The Government proposes to close a historic park, daily enjoyed by Washingtonians of all stripes, indefinitely," Reyes wrote.

She said the closure "runs counter to the public interest in utilising national parkland", adding that the government had not "plausibly identified any harm it would suffer from a temporary restraining order that preserves the status quo pending further proceedings".

Her order will last until the 28 November.

'Trash Island' or DC landmark? How a golf course got Trump in a messy legal dispute.

The legal dispute dates back to February, when the DC Preservation League and others sued over redevelopment plans for the park.

The historic course, which sits 2 miles (3km) south of the White House, is one of three public courses run by the National Park Service in the nation's capital.

The legal fight then escalated in October, when the NPS began to cut down hundreds of trees without notifying Reyes until 15 hours before work was set to begin.

After the trees were cut, Reyes ordered the Trump administration to stop tree removal until at least 26 October and give her three business days' notice about making any other permanent changes.

Sebagaimana diketahui, despite the work stoppage, trump announced that the course would be closed for 15 months from 15 november to accommodate the renovations. He also shared a rendering of the course redesign.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, "the current course is old, broken, dilapidated, and of no further use or effect. It is in very poor condition, with falling, dangerous, and disease-infested trees and, importantly, a collapsing and hazardous seawall," he said in a post to Truth Social.

Reyes has since separately opened an inquiry into whether the justice department attorneys "have made misrepresentations to the court and otherwise violated ethical rules".

That included whether giving late notice to the court about the renovation plans was "done in bad faith" and whether the attorneys failed to correct previously false statements or withheld information.

She said she would carry out the inquiry with a special master, an independent third party.

Judge investigating whether Trump administration lied about golf course renovations.

Party’s NSW leader Mike Newman says contenders are ‘people from the real world’ and not ‘career politicians’.

Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast.

The failed federal Liberal candidate Katherine Deves, who campaigned to exclude transgender women from women’s sport, will stand for One Nation at next year’s New South Wales election.

Deves was among four NSW Legislative Council candidates announced by One Nation’s NSW leader, Mike Newman, on Sunday.

The other candidates were Arnon Wither, a construction worker from the Hunter region who works as an electorate officer for Senator Sean Bell; Manti Steele, a farmer, teacher and mother of eight from Dubbo; and Daniel Hill, a surf lifesaver from the state’s south coast.

The NSW election will be held on 13 March.

Newman said on Sunday the upper house candidates were “authentic”, “people from the real world” and not “career politicians”.

One Nation has only announced a single lower house candidate – Newman, in the electorate of Cessnock – but he said the party would run candidates in all 93 lower house seats.

“We want to make sure that these people bleed orange, and like I said, they’re all from the real world,” he said.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, “that’s the that’s the type of person we’re aiming at … people from the real world who understand business, who understand their pinch points and pain points, understand the cost of living, understand cashflow. ”.

Sebagaimana diketahui, deves was handpicked by the former prime minister scott morrison to run in the federal nsw seat of warringah in 2022. Her candidacy was marred by controversy, including when she likened anti-trans activism to standing up against the Holocaust.

On Sunday she said she joined One Nation “because I wanted to be a part of the rescue, recovery, and restoration of our nation”.

“We are seeing cost of living skyrocket, whether it’s fuel, housing, energy, and we are watching a government that is so wedded to destructive ideologies like DEI and net zero that they are prepared to impoverish us all,” she said.

#629. Thunderstorms, giant hail and powerful winds forecast for NSW as wild weather hits east coast

📅 15 Nov 2026

Thunderstorms, giant hail and powerful winds forecast for NSW as wild weather hits east coast

Volatile weather predicted after storms on Saturday, with a man in his 20s struck by lightning while swimming on NSW Central Coast.

Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast.

Dangerous and severe “supercell” thunderstorms with the potential for giant hail and destructive winds were forecast for parts of New South Wales on Sunday, as volatile weather continued in the eastern states over the weekend.

Storms dumped heavy rain across large parts of northern and eastern NSW and much of Queensland on Saturday, with strong winds recorded up to 98km/h in Goulburn and rainfall totals of between 30mm and 50mm in the Coffs Harbour area.

Berdasarkan laporan, a man in his 20s was struck by lightning while swimming at ettalong beach on nsw’s central coast on saturday afternoon. He was pulled from the water by fellow swimmers and given CPR by first responders until NSW Ambulance paramedics arrived. He was taken to Gosford hospital in a serious condition, and later transferred to Royal North Shore hospital.

The young man was in a critical but stable condition on Sunday morning, a hospital spokesperson said.

Witnesses said while there was storm activity visible in the distance towards Gosford, the area around the beach was clear and sunny and that the lightning bolt appeared to come “out of nowhere”.

Lightning can strike up to 30km from the centre of a storm cell.

Sunday was expected to be “another big storm day”, with “very dangerous and severe thunderstorms” likely for north-eastern NSW, said Sarah Scully, senior meteorologist at the Bureau of Meteorology.

Those storms could bring hail with a diameter greater than 5cm, and winds in excess of 120km/h.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, “that’s being driven by a southerly change that’s pushing up the new south wales coast,” scully said. “It’s a potential trigger for these supercell high-end thunderstorms. ”.

Severe thunderstorms with 2cm hail, wind gusts in excess of 90km/h, heavy rainfall and flash flooding was possible on Sunday through a broader area of NSW extending down towards inland parts of the ranges to the east of Sydney, and pushing up into south-east and central parts of Queensland.

Sebagaimana diketahui, storms were expected in sydney on sunday, but were likely to be less severe than further north, though rain was likely. The forecast temperature was 23C. Showers and thunderstorms were expected in Brisbane with a top of 31C.

The BoM expected to release more severe weather warnings throughout Sunday as the storms develop.

On Monday, the risk of high-end severe thunderstorms would move into the NSW northern rivers and south-eastern parts of Queensland, including Brisbane, the Gold Coast and the Sunshine Coast, again with the potential to bring giant hail, destructive winds, and intense rain that could lead to life-threatening flash flooding.

“That again is being driven by that trough that’s pushing up the coast combined with the very humid conditions that eastern Australia has been experiencing the last few days,” Scully said.

A coastal trough with a low-pressure system appeared to be developing off the north coast of NSW near the Queensland border, which had the potential to bring even more rain onto the coast.

“How much rainfall accumulates is highly dependent on how close that trough sits to the coast, and also how long it lingers there,” Scully said.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, “at this state we’re only expecting moderate rainfall totals during tomorrow from that coastal trough, between 30mm to 70mm, easing into tuesday morning. If they just move that little bit closer to the coast they can sometimes dump a whole lot of rain. But we are watching it very closely as rainfall totals associated with these coastal troughs are notoriously challenging to predict. ”.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, elsewhere, there were showers developing in melbourne on sunday with a forecast top of 17c. There was a high chance of showers in Hobart, with 13C expected, and cloudy in Adelaide with a mild 20C forecast. It was partly cloudy in Canberra, where they were expecting 24C, and in Perth, with an expected top of 28C. Darwin was expecting 34C and an afternoon storm.

#631. Judo champion shakes up French presidential race with surprise candidacy

📅 15 Nov 2026

Judo champion shakes up French presidential race with surprise candidacy

Tanggal: 15 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/c6dj1e8wyykmo?at_medium=RSS&at_campaign=rss

Five-times Olympic champion Teddy Riner is one of France's most popular athletes.

Apart from an overwhelming urge to pin one's opponent to the floor of the house, there is no obvious connection between politics and the world of top-level judo.

That has not stopped France's much-garlanded world heavyweight champion Teddy Riner from throwing his hat into the ring for next April's presidential race.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the guadeloupe-born 37-year-old may have no experience of public office, no party behind him, and as yet no manifesto. All so far is a slogan La France qu'on aime (The France we love), a declaration on social media, and a campaign visit to a hospital in the Seine-Saint-Denis suburb of northern Paris.

But it would be a foolhardy pundit who would totally write off his chances.

Diungkapkan bahwa riner is, after all, one of the most popular figures in modern-day france, regularly topping the polls for embodying the nation's "values". He is a proven winner, with five Olympic golds and 11 world championships under his belt, as well as a successful career in business.

Berdasarkan laporan, more than 28 million people have watched his election broadcast on instagram and x, shot with proper presidential decorum against a backdrop of books and a french flag. Some 22% told an Ifop poll within 24 hours they "could" vote for him.

Diungkapkan bahwa teddy riner's video has attracted 14. 5 million views on Instagram alone.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, actors and television personalities have become presidents in other countries. The ex-leader of Liberia â George Weah â was formerly a professional footballer.

So why not a judoka in the ÃlysÃ©e Palace?.

"Anyone who thinks that being out of the political in-crowd disqualifies Riner from running for the ÃlysÃ©e would be very wrong," says Guillaume Tabard of Le Figaro.

Sebagaimana diketahui, "but [riner] too would be wrong if he thinks not belonging to the in-crowd is all it takes. ".

Diungkapkan bahwa for now the whole of the french political world has decided to take the riner candidacy seriously â or at least to pretend to. That is partly because he is such a popular personality that mocking his political hopes could easily rebound badly.

But it is also because the state of French politics â outside of the burgeoning forces of the hard left and hard right â is one of total disarray.

The centre-ground is floundering, with no candidate yet emerging who can inspire anything like the sense of mission of hard-right leader Marine Le Pen and Jean-Luc MÃ©lenchon on the hard left, who for now look set to face off in the final round of the presidential election in May.

So when a popular figure like Riner enters the race - proclaiming himself "neither left, nor right", wanting to "unite the country" and "put money back in people's pockets", railing equally against "racists" and "yobs who scare people off our streets" â politicians have to take note.

Hard-right leader Marine Le Pen currently leads the polls in the race to be France's next president.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, it is perfectly possible, probable even, that riner's campaign will fizzle out after a brief period of hype, and that the judoka will after all be a joker in the pack. But it is also possible that it won't, in which case the pre-election arithmetic will need a hasty readjustment: and it won't be the centrists who are smiling.

Thus far, Riner has shown himself a master of the codes required for this kind of out-of-nowhere candidacy, the first of which is to press home the message: "Don't Worry! I'm NOT a Politician!".

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, in this day and age in france, anyone who smacks of the "system" is automatically downgraded in voters' eyes, so it is important to emphasise that you are only running for office because, one, you have experienced real life (unlike those loafers in paris); and two, you have discovered that there are solutions out there for the country's many problems. Solutions that are invisible to those same blinkered apparatchiks.

All this Riner was able to express in last Monday's social media broadcast by using sophisticated rhetorical devices.

"People say I am a fool for wanting to run for the presidency," he said.

Sebagaimana diketahui, "am i a fool? well, if refusing to see france sink under the weight of debt; refusing to see mothers and fathers grit their teeth every time they do their weekly shop, and tremble with fear when their kids go out on the streetâ¦ if all that means being a fool, then yes call me a fool. ".

It was a promising oratorial start for the sportsman, and certainly attracted the viewers.

Are student protests being manipulated ahead of France's presidential election?.

France's Marine Le Pen, fighting court conviction and running for presidency.

But if he is serious â and Riner says he never does anything half-heartedly - that's not how he became an Olympic champion â then the hard work begins now.

What does Riner actually want to do? Who will be on his team? Where does he position himself on the all-consuming matters of the day: pension-reform, investment in education, the cost of living, public debt, the rise of populism or Russia's war in Ukraine?.

In short, how does he intend to transform his undeniable popularity as a sporting figure into a political mandate?.

Protesters have for weeks taken to the streets in France over wages, the cost of living and public services.

Sebagaimana diketahui, broadly, riner appears to be on the right on economic matters and law and order, but being black and of caribbean background he is also very strong on racism. When he says he is anti-extremism, he is referring mainly to Marine Le Pen.

In other words his pitch is somewhere in the centre, and against the extremes.

The trouble is, this is already an extremely crowded area, with important figures like ex-prime ministers Edouard Philippe and Gabriel Attal signally failing to take off.

Currently there are a dozen or so candidates in the area between centre right and centre left, stretching from the Socialist-backed RaphaÃ«l Glucksman to the Republicans' Bruno Retailleau on the right.

The latest possible addition is Christine Lagarde, who steps down as head of the European Central Bank next February.

President Emmanuel Macron is among the few politicians who appears genuinely pleased by Riner's decision to run.

The addition of yet another contender will dilute their polling numbers even further, making a second-round qualification for MÃ©lenchon more likely.

Diungkapkan bahwa so no wonder the leader of france unbowed (lfi) seemed so happy about riner's decision to run. "We know how it goes: neither right nor left means not left," MÃ©lenchon told reporters on Friday.

The only other politician who seems genuinely pleased, rather than putting on a fixed smile, is President Emmanuel Macron, who said Riner was a "great champion" and that politics "did not belong to the professionals".

That could be explained by the president's cool relations with his former prime ministers, Philippe and Attal, both of whom are doing all they can to distance themselves from their unpopular one-time boss.

Riner said he viewed Macron's praise as a "poisoned chalice", telling reporters on Saturday that he was "not the president's envoy, I'm not a Macronist".

Politics and judo have very little in common, but of the two, as Riner will soon discover, the more vicious is not the one that is fought out hand-to-hand after mutual acknowledgement on the tatami mat.

In Japanese, judo actually means "the gentle way".

If he starts looking like a serious candidate, Riner must know his life will be turned upside down, not just his physical form.

Diungkapkan bahwa in politics you do not bow in respect to your opponent. You give him a metaphorical headbutt.

#632. David Jones’ future looks grim. Is Myer next?

📅 14 Nov 2026

David Jones’ future looks grim. Is Myer next?

Tanggal: 14 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.theguardian.com/business/2026/nov/15/myer-david-jones-stores-closures-administration

With Myer’s profitability battered and share price languishing near all-time lows, DJs’ slide into administration raises an uncomfortable question.

Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast.

When the retailer’s doors slide open, shoppers are greeted by rows of slashed price tags, frantic discounting, and all the other hallmarks of a department store closing down.

Except this isn’t David Jones, the embattled upmarket retailer that is shutting half its 38 stores.

This is its longtime rival, Myer, where entire floors are seemingly permanently on sale.

With Myer’s profitability battered and share price languishing near all-time lows, DJs’ slide into administration raises an uncomfortable question: is Myer next?.

Sebagaimana diketahui, at first glance, myer’s headline numbers seem to defy the retail gloom, with double-digit sales growth to $4. 1bn last financial year.

That lift, however, was not driven by surging demand, but by adding sales from the newly acquired apparel chains, Just Jeans, Jay Jays, Portmans, Dotti and Jacqui E, bought from billionaire businessman Solomon Lew’s Premier Investments.

Meanwhile, to keep registers ringing, Myer employed “higher than planned promotional activity to stimulate demand”, according to its annual report, which reduced its profitability.

The department store has also slashed the value of its brands, down more than $200m in one year alone, in an admission that its labels are worth far less than they once were.

Department stores have faced a “sustained erosion of relevance over the past five years”, according to IBISWorld market researchers, as online platforms win over bargain-hunters and specialists like beauty retailer Mecca prove more nimble in capturing shifting tastes.

DJs and Myer, on the other hand, have been weighed down by long-running physical property leases tied to underperforming stores in their sprawling networks.

The era of Australian families being fiercely loyal to either David Jones or Myer is long gone, replaced by a grim battle for both chains to stay relevant.

The stress on big department store profitability has been exacerbated by a period of cost of living pressures that have “entrenched deal-hunting behaviour, reshaping how and when consumers engage with department stores”, according to IBISWorld.

Myer, however, has a critical advantage over David Jones: time.

While DJs fell into administration under mounting debts, Myer finished last financial year with a $100m net cash buffer, buying management breathing space to fix the business.

It has been reducing store numbers and with it lease liabilities – down to 56 stores from 60 before the pandemic – which is something David Jones is only doing now that it has collapsed into administration.

For the moment, Myer is leaning into the discounts demanded by shoppers, in the hope that more profitable trading conditions will emerge.

Richard Hemming, the editor at Under The Radar Report, says in retail “volume is everything”.

“If you get the volumes through, that customer base will eventually be in a position to pay more, and when volumes and margins both improve, you get that double effect,” Hemming says.

While analysts have mixed views on whether permanent discounting is a smart survival tactic or a slow-motion way to go bankrupt, department stores do need to move huge volumes of stock to keep cash flowing and clear seasonal goods.

They can use those discounts to get more people signed up to their loyalty programs – such as the successful Myer One scheme – in the hope they will become long-term customers.

Hemming sees the upside in Myer’s current pain, noting the retailer is “cleaning house earlier than rivals” precisely because investors have long priced it “like it’s going to go broke”.

Myer is revamping the business to aggressively pursue online sales.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, myer shares have been heavily sold down over the years, and now hover around the 24c mark, representing a fraction of its $4. 10 float price from 2009.

It did, however, receive a price bump on the day DJs fell into administration.

With roughly two in five Myer stores sharing a shopping centre with a David Jones outlet, investors are betting the coming closure of 19 DJs sites will hand Myer an easy market-share boost, even as its own long-term turnaround demands further store cuts.

Broader retail sentiment is also souring, as a string of interest rate rises and escalating cost-of-living pressures force cash-strapped shoppers to pare their discretionary spend.

When Dr Raymond Kasereka Kamwanga told his family he suspected he had Ebola and was going to a treatment centre in the city of Butembo in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo, his family were horrified.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, they regarded the specialised unit as a "death house" as not many patients do recover - especially those admitted in the late stages of the illness. His 50-year-old mother was in tears, pleading with him not to go there.

"Why are you choosing to die at the Ebola treatment centre?" Masika Ndungo had asked him.

But as a doctor at Butembo's Katwa Hospital, he knew that if stayed at home, he was unlikely to survive.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, this was in july, two months after the world health organization (who) had declared the ebola outbreak in dr congo a public health emergency of international concern. Since then 5,400 people have died and 11,000 have been infected, making it the second-most deadly outbreak ever recorded.

Butembo is in North Kivu province, the epicentre of the crisis, with the highest number of reported cases, according to the Congolese health ministry.

Dr Kamwanga is one of 3,031 people who have survived - and is evangelical about sharing his story in an effort to help stop the spread of infections devastating his community.

After staring death in the face and overcoming ostracisation, he has even started writing a book about his experience.

"As someone who has recovered, I am living proof that the disease exists, but also that it is possible to recover from it," he tells the BBC outside Katwa Hospital where he still works.

The 30-year-old medic believes he contracted the virus through contact with a patient in a setting where protective measures are not always adequate.

Raymond Kasereka Kamwanga uses his book to help convince sceptics that Ebola is real.

Berdasarkan laporan, the first symptoms appeared gradually: a bitter taste in his mouth, headaches and a general feeling of malaise. He contacted the Ebola response team.

After an initial consultation and some tests, he returned home, but his condition did not improve.

Butembo does not have the equipment to quickly test for Ebola - samples need to be sent to the city of Beni, 54km (33 miles) north.

This delays diagnosis as the condition of roads in this war-torn and underdeveloped part of DR Congo means it can take between 48 and 72 hours to travel even this relatively short distance.

Berdasarkan laporan, after three days at home, kamwanga felt extremely weak and experienced muscle pain. On the fourth day, he began vomiting and had diarrhoea.

This is when he gathered his family members - including his mother - to tell them he had to go to the Ebola treatment centre.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, "she had started crying, along with my sisters. I told them everything would be alright, that I was a doctor and that I was confident. But they weren't reassured," he says.

Around 18:00, he set off on foot to the nearby centre but refused to use the main entrance.

Diungkapkan bahwa he called his colleagues and asked them to put on their protective gear before they approached him and isolated him. The virus spreads from one person to another by contact with infected bodily fluids.

Dr Kamwanga's mother says his experience has helped dispel some of the misinformation she had heard about Ebola.

The current outbreak is caused by the Bundibugyo species of the virus for which there is no approved vaccine or treatment.

"The treatment given to Ebola patients is symptomatic - meaning that doctors treat the symptoms the patient presents," says Kamwanga, explaining that in his case it was severe vomiting and diarrhoea.

In some patients these symptoms can lead to organ failure and then some develop internal and external bleeding.

Kamwanga lost a lot of fluid and struggled to stay hydrated - he was terrified.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, "i was afraid for myself. Every day, patients were dying right before my eyes. But I stayed positive," he explains.

Over 13 days lying in his hospital bed, he tried to keep his spirits up by watching movies and TV shows on his phone, reading and scrolling through TikTok.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the day he learned he had recovered, kamwanga felt immense relief. He thanked the healthcare workers who had cared for him.

However, even a certificate showing he was Ebola-free did not initially dispel the unease those around him felt after he was discharged.

'I buried my parents one day after the other' - Ebola mourners learn how to grieve safely.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, "we welcomed him home warmly. But because of our fear, we didn't get close to him any more," Ndungo, his mother, tells the BBC.

For 21 days - the incubation period of the virus - the doctor lived separately in another part of the family home, which was crowded at the time with at least 18 people living there, including several children and people displaced by recent fighting in the region.

They all agree the experience changed their perception of Ebola.

Some do not believe the disease even exists - Ndungo says that witnessing Ebola first-hand helped to dispel some of that misinformation.

After his recovery, Kamwanga threw himself into community outreach - sharing his story as a way of combatting rumours and mistrust.

Sebagaimana diketahui, "i started writing my book - the price of saving lives - one week after recovering and leaving the hospital," he says. "However, it is not finished yet. What I currently use during my awareness-raising activities is the draft, and it is already making a significant impact. ".

During these sessions, he also distributes photos taken while he was sick to help convince residents that Ebola is real.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, but in butembo, this mission remains difficult. Kamwanga explains that some people view awareness campaigns as a way for humanitarian organisations to profit from donor funding.

Such mistrust, which is also levelled at healthcare professionals, is often fuelled by poverty and trauma related to years of armed conflict, he says.

"Ebola has come alongside the war," he says, explaining that some even interpret it as a way for those in authority to threaten a vulnerable population "to finish off those whom the war failed to exterminate".

He also believes that the number of deaths observed during epidemics - compared to recoveries, which are sometimes less visible - reinforce fear and suspicion.

But putting himself on the front line also comes with risks - and Kamwanga says he receives death threats on his phone.

Diungkapkan bahwa some residents accuse him of being paid to spread information about ebola. He also reports that outreach workers have been attacked by members of the community.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, he feels the authorities do not work effectively to address all these problems: "our government is taking things lightly. ".

He agrees too with the recent report by MÃ©decins Sans FrontiÃ¨res (MSF) that Ebola funds are going missing.

Berdasarkan laporan, "the money allocated to the ebola response is being misappropriated by the government. We do not have enough protective equipment," the medic says.

The BBC has asked the Congolese government for comment.

Despite the intimidation and the obstacles he and other medics face, he remains determined - his goal is to help put an end to the disease.

Sebagaimana diketahui, "should we give up the fight against ebola? no. We continue to do what we can with the resources available to us, which are unfortunately very limited. ".

Berdasarkan laporan, “it clearly would be a massive step to change the age of consent, but it deserves proper consideration and scrutiny. I can absolutely understand why she is calling for it. ”.

Sebagaimana diketahui, “i do think there is a very strong case to look at banning ndas in all circumstances where they relate to harassment or discrimination, to make sure that no victim, regardless of where it happened or what their relationship was with the perpetrator, should ever be silenced. ”.

Commending Latter for the “extraordinary bravery” it took to waive her anonymity, Brown-Fuller said: “I think we must go further to increase protections for young women and girls, and looking at a staggered age of consent is an important step.

Sebagaimana diketahui, “we already have rules that recognise power imbalances in professions: between teachers and students, or barristers and junior colleagues. It’s time for the government to recognise the implicit power imbalance held by older men over teenage girls. ”.

Women like Mia are leading the charge, but we can and must do more to make this a moment of change. ”.

Starship’s 15th test flight was envisioned as a historic double-catch mission, where all parts of the rocket would be returned intact to the launch site, rather than recovered from the ocean as with some previous test flights.

The hulking spacecraft is composed of two parts: a lower booster stage called Super Heavy, whose Raptor engines powered the orbital ascent, and an upper stage also called Starship.

Basically, it detected that the booster was not in the place it was supposed to be to proceed with a catch,” SpaceX spokesperson Dan Huot said early on Saturday. The booster was also “slightly low on fuel”, according to SpaceX chief executive Elon Musk.

This week’s test flight was still a victory for SpaceX, marking the first time that the company caught its upper stage.

It was also only the second time Starship has entered Earth’s orbit.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, starship’s advances have also aided the expansion of musk’s satellite internet empire. The spacecraft deployed 26 Starlink V3 satellites during this recent flight.

Hundreds of thousands of Czechs are expected to rally in Prague on Sunday to protest against what they say is a government attempt to stifle media freedom.

The gathering to save the mandatory licence fees that fund Czechia’s public broadcasters could be one of the biggest in the country’s history, organisers say.

It will mark the latest challenge to the prime minister, Andrej Babiš, and his coalition of populist, hard-right nationalist and Eurosceptic parties, and follows weeks of demonstrations in towns and cities and a strike by staff at Czech TV and Czech Radio.

Protesters say the plan to scrap licence fees and fund the broadcasters from the state budget would give ministers more leverage over newsrooms and follow the example of Slovakia, Hungary, Poland and Serbia, where current and previous rightwing populist governments eroded media independence.

Diungkapkan bahwa the million moments for democracy group that is organising the demonstration said the authorities would see the level of opposition. “Babiš and his government obviously think they will get away with anything … that they can ignore experts, silence critics and treat democratic institutions like their property,” it said.

Diungkapkan bahwa the group expects 400,000 to 600,000 people at letná plain, which overlooks prague’s historic centre. Some protesters would be channelling wider opposition to the government, said Daniel Stach, a TV presenter and one of the most recognised faces of the campaign.

The proposed changes, which would cut state television and radio budgets by about 15%, have drawn fire from international media organisations.

The European Broadcasting Union, the European Federation of Journalists, Reporters Without Borders and the International Press Institute have also criticised the government’s media plan, likening it to controversial moves by Slovakia’s prime minister, Robert Fico, and Hungary’s former premier Viktor Orbán.

Sebagaimana diketahui, babiš, a billionaire who returned to power last year, said protesters were riling up the public with unfounded claims about threats to media freedom. Nine people were killed in the shooting at the Greek Orthodox church last month.

A Jordanian court has sentenced three men to death by hanging for carrying out a fatal mass shooting on a church last month.

The attack on 23 October killed nine people and injured 34 others who had been attending a Christian funeral at a Greek Orthodox church in Karak governorate.

Jordan's Armed Forces said in a statement on Sunday that the men had been convicted of committing "terrorist acts", as well as possessing weapons, "promoting the ideas of a terrorist organisation" and "conspiracy to commit terrorist acts".

Diungkapkan bahwa the three men - two jordanian brothers and their brother-in-law - fled the scene of the attack and were arrested three days later. They have not been publicly identified.

Karak is home to a sizeable Christian community in the Muslim-majority kingdom.

CCTV footage from the day of the attack showed three men holding guns approaching and firing on St George's church in the village of Hmoud.

Watch: CCTV footage appears to show gunmen near church.

A second video showed dead and wounded people lying on the ground amid chaotic scenes at the church.

It is still unclear why the attackers chose to target that specific church.

Shortly after the attack, Jordan's King Abdullah II wrote on X: "The terrorist attack against Karak will be met with the harshest retaliation.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, "those who delude themselves into thinking that they can divide jordanians with their bullets have no chance in the face of our unity. ".

The three men fled the scene of the shooting and were later located inside an abandoned house in Karak governorate, south of the capital, Amman.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, they refused to surrender and opened fire on security forces, who returned fire and wounded all three of them, the public security directorate said at the time. No security personnel were hurt in the shootout.

King Abdullah praised security forces for chasing the suspects "to the very end".

The week after the Karak shooting, Jordan struck what its military said were "terrorist organisations" in Syria in retaliation to the church attack.

Diungkapkan bahwa syrian health officials told state media that five people, including women, children and an elderly man, were killed in the strike on a village in the southern daraa province. Jordan said its fighter jets had killed and wounded "several terrorists" without giving further details.

Jordan said it had co-ordinated with the Syrian government, but Syria said it had not been notified in advance.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, executions in jordan are carried out by hanging. The kingdom previously observed an unofficial ban on executions from 2006 to 2014, and another pause from 2017 until June this year.

Jordan carries out deadly strike in Syria in retaliation for church attack.

#652. World’s top court to rule if Myanmar committed genocide against Rohingya

📅 15 Nov 2026

World’s top court to rule if Myanmar committed genocide against Rohingya

Tanggal: 15 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/nov/15/myanmar-rohingya-genocide-icj

International court of justice has never before found a state guilty of genocide, and ruling will have implications for case against Israel.

The world’s top court will deliver a judgment this week on whether Myanmar committed genocide against its Rohingya minority, in a landmark case that will set a critical 21st-century benchmark for the gravest of all international crimes.

The closely watched judgment could become one of the most significant moments in international law since the end of the second world war.

Diungkapkan bahwa the international court of justice (icj) has never found a state responsible for genocide, a crime defined after the nazi-led holocaust. The ruling will have implications for a separate high-profile genocide case against Israel.

Nearly a decade after a military campaign forced hundreds of thousands of Muslim Rohingya to flee across the border, the ICJ in The Hague will deliver its judgment on Thursday morning.

“The ICJ ruling will be historic for Rohingya survivors and their families around the world,” said Yanghee Lee, a former UN rights investigator to Myanmar.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, “the international community failed to prevent myanmar military atrocities against the rohingya nine years ago. It must seize this opportunity to finally secure justice for the Rohingya and begin to reckon with these failings. ”.

ICJ judges have spent seven years weighing accusations by the Gambia, a Muslim-majority state, that Myanmar’s repression of the Rohingya breached the 1948 UN genocide convention.

A key issue in previous cases has been how to prove “intent” in a crime defined as acts committed with the “intent to destroy, in whole or in part” a national, ethnical, racial or religious group.

Antonia Mulvey, the founder of Legal Action Worldwide (Law), a group that represents hundreds of Rohingya survivors, said she was “cautiously optimistic” the court would hold Myanmar fully accountable.

Government actions showed “patterns of conduct” that proved clear attempts to destroy the group, she said.

Sebagaimana diketahui, “the attacks on the villages took place the same way,” she said. “They would attack the civilians, burn the villages, separate men and women, conduct sexual violence … and then as they fled, they would continue to kill them. ”.

Two other ICJ cases dealing with atrocities in the Balkans fell short of finding states directly responsible for genocide, although Serbia was found legally responsible for failing to prevent the genocide at Srebrenica.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, mulvey said a key part of the upcoming judgment will be how it handles the issue of rape and sexual violence as an act of genocide. Her team has collected accounts of soldiers mutilating women’s genitals and biting their faces. “That’s to mark people, to brand them … it is also to stop reproduction,” she said.

“Yes, we would say sexual violence is a critical part to show their intent to destroy the group,” she added.

Sebagaimana diketahui, “you don’t need to gang-rape people. You don’t need to do it in public. You don’t need to mutilate them. You don’t need to kill their children in front of them. What is the purpose of that? The purpose is to destroy the group. ”.

Berdasarkan laporan, in january, the icj held closed-door sessions to hear directly from rohingya survivors who travelled from camps in bangladesh. One witness said her child was taken from her arms, stabbed and thrown into a fire, according to Law, while another described seeing piles of bodies in a mass grave.

During hearings, Gambian justice minister Dawda Jallow told the court the case was not “about esoteric issues of international law”.

Berdasarkan laporan, “it is about real people, real stories and a real group of human beings,” said jallow. They have been targeted for destruction. “The Rohingya of Myanmar. ”.

Myanmar, which has denied carrying out a genocide, claims its actions targeted a military uprising from insurgents.

For decades, Rohingya people have been stripped of their citizenship and targeted by increasing discrimination, amid a backdrop of communal violence with Buddhists in the country’s western Rakhine state.

Berdasarkan laporan, the crisis reached a climax after a rohingya militant group conducted guerrilla-style attacks in the summer of 2017. The Myanmar army responded with massive “clearance operations”.

Refugees who fled into Bangladesh in 2017 told the Guardian of a massacre in the village of Tula Toli, where survivors described systematic shooting of civilians, including the drowning of children in a river.

This testimony from Tula Toli – which satellite footage later showed had been razed – added to dozens of witness accounts collected over the years to build a case for genocide.

A ruling that Myanmar committed genocide would add international pressure on its leader Min Aung Hlaing, who headed the military during the 2016-2017 attacks and later overthrew the elected government of Aung San Suu Kyi in a 2021 coup, triggering a civil war that has left tens of thousands dead.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the former general is separately b​eing investigated by the international criminal court (icc), which prosecutes individuals and not states like the icj, on allegations of crimes against humanity. He was installed as civilian president in April after elections that were widely condemned as a sham, and has made efforts to rebuild diplomatic ties.

For many onlookers, the ICJ decision will hold relevance far beyond Myanmar, as it will provide the strongest hint of how judges might assess the seminal genocide case brought by South Africa against Israel over its campaign in Gaza.

The cases have much in common, with an ethnic group targeted by a powerful military, although Israel has far stronger diplomatic backing from the US.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the judgment comes as washington has been on the offensive against international human rights bodies, including sanctioning the icc. Washington technically already considers the Rohingya crisis to be a genocide, based on a decision by the Biden administration.

However, Trump’s UN ambassador, Mike Waltz, warned that the ICJ “must not be allowed” to establish a standard for genocide that could be used against “allied soldiers”, a statement that will be relevant for Israeli troops.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, supporters of the myanmar case say the judgment should compel states to block arms transfers and jet fuel supplies. While the court does not have the means to enforce its decisions, they have been respected in the past, and the UN security council could give it strength, although divisions, especially between the US and China, make this unlikely.

Sebagaimana diketahui, more than 1 million rohingya remain in bangladesh, in the world’s largest refugee settlement. Fewer than 600,000 are estimated to remain in Myanmar.

A displaced Rohingya living inside Myanmar told the Guardian he hoped the judgment would “help end decades of persecution and discrimination”.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, “we are not asking for sympathy alone,” he said. “We are asking for justice, recognition, equal rights and a future in which our children can live safely and with dignity in their own homeland. ”.

Israel kills Hamas commander in strike on Gaza camp, officials say

Tanggal: 15 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/cqrkg4r6mg7xo?at_medium=RSS&at_campaign=rss

One of the camps in Al-Mawasi in southern Gaza.

A senior Hamas figure who helped plan and oversee the 7 October 2023 attack on Israel has been killed in an Israeli airstrike, officials in Israel and Gaza have said.

Samir Abu Younis, the newly appointed commander of the Rafah Brigade, was killed on Saturday in Al-Mawasi in the southern Gaza Strip, according to Hamas's Al-Qassam Brigades military wing.

Berdasarkan laporan, a local hamas official confirmed younis's death. The Israeli military said it had targeted him and that prior to the strike "steps were taken to mitigate harm to civilians".

Eyewitnesses in Gaza said four missiles struck a tent in the Al-Waha camp, which shelters hundreds of displaced people in Al-Mawasi, causing a fire to break out.

A medical source at Nasser Hospital in the southern city of Khan Younis said three injured people had arrived there, as well as a dead body.

The Israel Defence Forces (IDF) and Israel's security agency, the ISA, confirmed in a statement on Telegram that it had "eliminated" Younis.

Describing him as a "central figure among Hamas's senior figures", it said he had "acted with the aim of trying to restore the strength of the brigade and the Hamas terrorist organisation".

Diungkapkan bahwa it added: "younis directed the brigade's terrorists to advance and carry out terror attacks against israeli civilians and idf troops. ".

Al-Qassam Brigades wrote on Telegram that Younis had "participated in numerous high-profile operations and resisted enemy incursions", and was "one of the most important commanders involved in planning and overseeing the 7 October attack".

It described his killing as a "cowardly assassination".

Younis, 53, had been in his position since 15 September, following the death of the brigade's previous commander, Nael Abu Obeid.

Berdasarkan laporan, he joined hamas' armed wing in 1991 and held several senior operational roles before becoming commander. His funeral will be held on Sunday afternoon in Khan Younis, Hamas said.

The Hamas-led attack on southern Israel on 7 October 2023, when about 1,200 people were killed an 251 others taken hostage, triggered the most recent war in Gaza.

Since then, more than 74,650 people have been killed in the Palestinian territory, the health ministry there says.

Though a ceasefire was reached last October, Israel has continued strikes it says are targeting remaining Hamas militants, which it argues it has the right to do under the terms of the ceasefire agreement.

More than 1,640 people have been killed in Gaza since the October 2025 ceasefire, according to the territory's health ministry, whose figures are considered reliable by the UN.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, update november 15: an earlier version of this article referred to israel carrying out 'occasional' strikes in gaza following a ceasefire in october 2025. This word has been removed to better reflect the frequency of Israeli strikes on Gaza since the ceasefire.

#655. Christmas ‘dupes’: the cheaper gift versions proving a festive hit in the cost of living crisis

📅 15 Nov 2026

Christmas ‘dupes’: the cheaper gift versions proving a festive hit in the cost of living crisis

Tanggal: 15 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.theguardian.com/money/2026/nov/15/christmas-dupes-gift-aldi-candles-quince-cashmere-jumpers-price

Berdasarkan laporan, from aldi candles to quince’s cashmere jumpers, cut-price versions of high-end sellers have gone mainstream. But is it fair?.

For fans of the festive season nothing is more Christmassy than lighting a super-sized botanical candle with its trim of orange slices and berries.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, but as the notes of cinnamon and clove fill the room will you be burning money spent on the white company’s £95 “winter indulgence” candle that customers describe as the “scent of christmas”. Or have you followed TikTok’s advice and bought the Aldi “dupe” for £25.

Sebagaimana diketahui, dupes are products that claim to offer a similar experience to a high-end item though do not claim to be that product. They were originally a Gen Z obsession but have become a mainstream shopping trend at a time of strained household finances.

“No matter what age you are, how much money you’ve got to spend, everyone wants to ‘luxe it up’ with a dupe,” says Catherine Shuttleworth, a retail consultant and chief executive of Savvy Marketing.

“The message is ‘why not be smart like me saving cash but still looking good’,” she says.

“In the case of homewares, a high street dupe of a luxury branded candle can look and smell just as good as the real thing, and will your visitors really notice that your table lamps are from B&M not the White Company?”.

Diungkapkan bahwa dupe culture is being supercharged by social media, particularly tiktok. More than 30 million people across the UK now use TikTok each month, according to the company, with Gen-Z’ers admitting that seeing products sell out or go viral makes them more likely to buy them.

Berdasarkan laporan, data firm ypulse has been tracking consumer attitudes to dupes for several years and tori d’amico, managing content editor, says: “the idea that a dupe can be a true replacement for a luxury item is still prevalent. Dupes are not shameful or embarrassing to own. Young consumers brag online about finding a good deal and share it with the masses. ”.

Diungkapkan bahwa ypulse’s most recent research found that 44% of uk 13- to 39-year-olds have bought a dupe in the past year. When asked, just over half (53%) of this age group agreed that “the quality of dupe/fake luxury items makes me less likely to want to purchase a real luxury item”.

Dupes are particularly prominent in the beauty world but are also found in other sectors including food, furniture, homeware and designer fashion.

Diungkapkan bahwa us “dupe” retailer quince, which sells upmarket products ranging from candles to cashmere sweaters, has just launched in the uk. Alongside each product on its website it suggests the saving you are making against more expensive brands. A £50 woman’s red cashmere jumper, for example, is pictured alongside graphics comparing it with jumpers from Cos and Reiss costing three times as much.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, fragrance, in particular, is a popular target. There are more than 50,000 videos on TikTok under the combined hashtag #perfumedupe and #perfumedupes, where influencers rate imitation fragrances against famous names and tell viewers where to find them.

Berdasarkan laporan, with fragrances a sought-after christmas gift the platform is awash with content extolling these cheaper scents. Instead of spending nearly £130 on Mugler’s Alien try Zara’s Violet Blossom for £15. Or, if you can’t afford Le Labo’s Another 13, try Marks & Spencer’s Aura Ambrette, a snip at £22. 99, suggests one. 50.

In TikTok Dupeland budget supermarket Aldi is lauded as a perfume house with its Lacura brand tipped to offer substitutes for high-end favourites ranging from Paradoxe to Flowerbomb and Baccarat Rouge – for £7 a bottle.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, “these cut-price products are in focus right now as consumers look for cheaper alternatives in response to rising prices,” says eric mills from market research firm nielseniq. In a recent survey, 38% of UK consumers said that in the past 12 months they had switched to lower-priced brands to manage their shopping bills.

“The buyers of these brands are often thought of as only younger consumers, but while Gen Z are key spenders, it’s millennials who account for the greatest proportion of sales,” he adds.

Get set for the working day – we'll point you to all the business news and analysis you need every morning.

In a microcosm of what is likely happening elsewhere in the market, the number of people buying dupe fragrances online is up 17% in the past year which is ahead of the overall market.

Berdasarkan laporan, with the continued adoption of ai tools, mills says: “it’s easy to imagine dupes gaining further traction, as consumers can simply ask a chatbot for a cheaper alternative to their favourite luxury scent. ”.

Sebagaimana diketahui, with dupes copying well-known brands without pretending to be the real thing they occupy a space somewhere between authentic and fake. While consumers might love dupes, the targets are less enthusiastic.

Celebrity makeup artist Charlotte Tilbury, whose £350m fortune stems from the sale of her eponymous beauty empire to Spanish fragrance and fashion group Puig, recently told the BBC that “when you dupe, you dupe the consumer”.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, “it is not charlotte tilbury … and it is not performing the way that my products do,” tilbury says of cheaper imitations. “If I could do them for those prices I would. ”.

Charlotte Tilbury has had some success pushing back and, in 2019, brought a successful copyright case against Aldi over the designs on its Filmstar Bronze & Glow palette which the supermarket had copied.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, claire breheny, partner and head of trade marks at mathys & squire suggests that business owners should be requesting that dupes be taken down from online platforms or social media. Brand owners “need to protect their packaging and get-up, not just their name.

Sebagaimana diketahui, “the risk for consumers is that similar packaging doesn’t guarantee similar quality, ingredients or performance – although a cheaper alternative isn’t necessarily always going to be inferior. ”.

With the cost of living crisis only making dupes more attractive to shoppers, Savvy Marketing’s Shuttleworth says that nearly 80% of shoppers its survey polled were happy to selectively spend more on treats and luxuries where they think it’s worth it.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, “the challenge for top brands like charlotte tilbury, is that they need to be able to convince shoppers the quality difference is always worth paying for. ”.

#658. Fifth Canadian soldier dies from injuries caused by large fire at military base

Fifth Canadian soldier dies from injuries caused by large fire at military base

Tanggal: 15 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/cmrlgn4x2xw8o?at_medium=RSS&at_campaign=rss

Pte William Douglas Dal Bianco died from his injuries suffered at a Canadian military base last month.

A fifth Canadian soldier has died from injuries he suffered when a grass fire swept through a military training area last month.

Four people were killed initially and dozens were injured when the fire, which ignited during a live fire training exercise, spread rapidly through Canadian Forces Base Wainwright carried by strong winds on 17 October.

Pte William Douglas Dal Bianco, who had been receiving medical care in Ontario, died on Friday, the Canadian Armed Forces said in a statement.

Sebagaimana diketahui, prime minister mark carney wrote on x: "canadians are holding private dal bianco's loved ones, and all those still grieving in the wake of this terrible tragedy, in our hearts. ".

Berdasarkan laporan, the canadian armed forces said that 24 military personnel were still in hospital receiving treatment, while 14 had been released as of saturday. Thirty-eight military personnel had been injured in total.

Canadian Forces Base Wainwright in Alberta is one of the country's busiest military training bases.

Members of 1 Canadian Mechanized Brigade Group had been conducting live-fire training at the base, in the province of Alberta, when the fire broke out.

Military officials said at the time that the fire spread across a kilometre in a matter of seconds, taking many of those on the base by surprise.

Firefighters battled the blaze through the night, while nearby hospitals became inundated by injured personnel and staff.

Carney described it as "one of the worst tragedies for the forces on Canadian soil in peacetime".

An investigation found that the fire was likely sparked by a grenade launcher being fired on the base's grenade range, officials said.

Firefighters on the base had known about the fire but could not tackle it because it was in a danger area that could contain unspent explosives.

Canadian Chief of the Defence Staff Gen Jennie Carignan said the nation's armed forces were "heartbroken" by the loss of Dal Bianco, while Defence Minister David McGuinty offered his "deepest condolences" to his family, friends and colleagues.

"No words can ease the pain of losing a loved one, and my thoughts remain with all those affected by this tragedy," he said.

Diungkapkan bahwa "we remain committed to supporting the families and the canadian armed forces community during this profoundly difficult time, and to honouring private dal bianco's service, dedication and sacrifice to canada. ".

Author of major review into youth unemployment rejects ‘crude cuts’ to payments and downplays opposition to his proposals within Labour.

Alan Milburn has said “there is no such thing as a free lunch”, in response to critics who believe the government should make tougher cuts to out-of-work benefits for young people.

The former health secretary will publish a major review on Tuesday, urging ministers to implement radical reforms to address the UK’s youth unemployment crisis, which has seen the number of young people not in employment, education or training (Neet) rise to about a million.

He told the BBC’s Sunday With Laura Kuenssberg programme the government would have to be “candid with people”, and that it would take 10 years for the benefits bill to come down and for the country to reach a “reasonable level” of youth unemployment as a result of his recommendations.

He also warned the additional investment in young people would cost billions of pounds over a 10-year period.

Berdasarkan laporan, milburn said it was impossible to “wave a magic wand” and fix the crisis sooner. “You can if you just do crude cuts,” he clarified. “But if you do crude cuts in benefits, all that happens is that young people show up somewhere else on the government ledger. ”.

Diungkapkan bahwa asked what he would say to critics such as the opposition leader, kemi badenoch, who has repeatedly called for benefits to be slashed over a short period of time, he said: “there’s no such thing as a free lunch. If you are going to will the ends, you’ve got to will the means.

Berdasarkan laporan, “i don’t think there’s a single person in this country who believes that it’s tolerable to have 1 million young people, aged 16 to 24, who are not in education, employment, or training. ”.

The Labour government is expecting opposition to Milburn’s recommendations from its own MPs on the left of the party, who rebelled against Keir Starmer’s plans to reform welfare last summer.

Sebagaimana diketahui, asked about the mood in the parliamentary party, the former cabinet minister said: “when i talk to labour mps about this, they know quite well that in their constituencies there are hundreds, sometimes thousands, of young people who are being doomed to a life on benefits. ”.

Milburn’s long-awaited report on youth unemployment will promise almost half a million job and education opportunities within a decade, but will also advise sweeping changes to the benefits system for under-25s.

It will recommend that some young people with disabilities should lose their ongoing personal independence payment (Pip), and instead be able to apply to local funds for short-term expenses and equipment.

While entitlement for those with the most severe needs will be protected, most under-25s will be no longer eligible for either Pip or the health element of universal credit and will instead get a new youth allowance paid at the standard universal credit rate.

Speaking to Sky News, the work and pensions secretary, Pat McFadden, acknowledged the overhaul would have an “element of compulsion” for Neets, suggesting government intervention to compel young people to work or train would be strengthened.

Asked whether he agreed with some under-25s losing out, he said this was necessary because the number of young people claiming Pip had doubled since the start of the decade, while the number of young people on the health element of universal credit had gone up by 80%.

He’s saying if you have a long-term disability, that means you can never work. You will actually get more than you will now.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, “he’s saying that if you have extra costs, there will be a benefit you can apply to for extra costs. He’s also saying there should be a local fund for short-term needs. And for other people, he’s saying there should be more support to get into work.

Sebagaimana diketahui, “but the status quo is important for this reason … if you’re 20 right now and you sign on to long-term sickness benefits, you’ve got more chance of marking your 30th birthday and still being on them than having a steady job in between. ”.

#663. Trident nuclear submarine concludes record underwater deployment

📅 15 Nov 2026

Trident nuclear submarine concludes record underwater deployment

Tanggal: 15 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.theguardian.com/uk-news/2026/nov/15/trident-nuclear-submarine-hms-vengeance-record-tour

HMS Vengeance’s seven-month patrol prompts concerns about slow pace of maintenance of ageing fleet and impact on crew.

A Trident nuclear submarine has concluded a record seven-month deployment, returning to the Faslane naval base in Scotland, where its crew are expected to be greeted by senior members of the government.

HMS Vengeance began its patrol on 12 April and spent 217 days submerged before returning on Sunday, leaving the country when Keir Starmer was in Downing Street and Manchester United were third in the Premier League.

Its tour underwater surpasses the old 205-day record, set by HMS Vanguard, and has raised questions about the strains placed on sailors and the reliability of ageing submarines sent on the extended missions.

Berdasarkan laporan, “patrols are getting longer and longer,” said david cullen, a nuclear expert with the basic thinktank. “The fleet was designed around three-month tours, and that was considered to be a long time to be stuck underwater in a metal box with no contact with the outside world. ”.

The increase in the time spent at sea reflects the slow pace of submarine maintenance, prompting Labour to blame spending cuts implemented by the Conservatives, though naval chiefs insist there is a plan for improvement.

Sebagaimana diketahui, hms vengeance is one of four submarines responsible for carrying britain’s trident nuclear missiles. At all times a boat is at sea, so the UK could launch strikes even if Britain had already been destroyed in a nuclear war.

Berdasarkan laporan, when the vanguard class of submarines was brought into service in the 1990s, they were designed to carry three to four months of food for the crew of about 140, and deployments of more than 100 days were considered highly exceptional. Missions now start with tinned food crammed into corridors and other available spaces.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, each submarine has to keep its location secret so it cannot be targeted, meaning it also cannot be resupplied. The boats maintain radio silence and so the crew cannot message out on the long deployments, though they can receive news and other information.

Diungkapkan bahwa such is the length of the patrols that the return of a trident submarine, known as a “day zero”, has become a political event. Starmer made an unannounced visit when the last patrol ended in April, praising the crew on their return.

There have been worries about the psychological impact of the patrols on the crew members, who have to spend seven months underwater in a boat 150 metres long, at a time when the Royal Navy is struggling to recruit new personnel.

Last week, the head of the Royal Navy, Gen Sir Gwyn Jenkins, said he had “nothing but tremendous respect” for the Trident sailors, but added that the UK needed to “improve our submarine maintenance” to allow faster turnaround.

The submarine service, in line with the rest of the navy, has a “no touching rule” – prohibiting physical intimacy on board – though the service has had to contend with allegations of sexual abuse and harassment during deployments.

In October 2024, the then first sea lord was forced to issue an apology to women – who make up about 10% of the navy – who had suffered “misogyny, bullying and other unacceptable behaviours” in the submarine service.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the navy conducted an inquiry after a whistleblower, sophie brook, complained of a “constant campaign of sexual bullying” from male sailors. Reports of rape, physical and verbal abuse were examined in a heavily redacted report.

Trident submarines can carry 40 nuclear warheads, with enough destructive power to destroy Moscow and several other major Russian cities, and a letter from the prime minister to tell the captain how to proceed in the event it is determined the UK no longer exists after an all-out nuclear attack.

Such is the length of the boat’s patrol it will still be carrying Starmer’s letter, though the replacement submarine on rotation will have Andy Burnham’s instructions, written in longhand in the days after he took over at Downing Street.

In July, Labour announced a £26bn, 10-year plan to invest in Britain’s three main naval bases, at Faslane, the operational home of the Trident submarines, Devonport and Portsmouth, as part of a wider increase in defence spending.

However, the first of the replacements for the four Vanguard class submarines, HMS Dreadnought, is not expected to be ready until about 2032, meaning that the old boats have at least five more years to remain in service.

Sebagaimana diketahui, “the inherent risks of operating submarines are being pushed by them being run as they are. At the end of the submarines’ design life they should be run gently, not as hard as they are,” Cullen said.

Exclusive: Shepard Fairey says image will hold PM accountable over promise to get people off the streets.

The “Hope” portrait of Barack Obama by the US street artist Shepard Fairey came to symbolise a historic 2008 presidential campaign, became one of the most ubiquitous and reproduced political portraits of modern times, and ended up in the Smithsonian.

Fairey’s latest work, of the UK prime minister, Andy Burnham, may not elicit the same response but will, he hopes, deliver a hard-hitting message: one of a promise made.

The portrait, “Home”, captures Burnham in a red Big Issue tabard when, as Greater Manchester mayor, he sold copies with vendor Colin in 2023, and is the front cover of a new collectors’ edition of the magazine.

Berdasarkan laporan, designed exclusively for the big issue, it’s a reminder to the new prime minister of his pledge to tackle rough sleeping. From Monday, it will be sold on streets, and also be unveiled on the walls of the Saatchi Gallery in London as part of a six-month street culture exhibition, Beyond the Streets.

Sebagaimana diketahui, fairey said: “the thread that runs through all my work is a push for justice. Politicians often want people to forget to hold them accountable for the promises they’ve made. This is harder to do when a symbol of that promise is in thousands of people’s hands. This portrait reminds us of the pledge Burnham made. ”.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the art work was created after the big issue approached fairey, who said he was “overjoyed” that the portrait would be in the public sphere. “What I wanted to convey was simply warmth, and a reminder that he has actually been out on the streets promoting and selling the Big Issue, even before he was prime minister,” he said.

Berdasarkan laporan, the magazine also carries an exclusive interview with burnham. In it, the prime minister said: “I don’t think anyone should sleep rough in this country … I’m not going to be naive. I can offer people a route off the streets, but not everybody will take it.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, “what i can say though is, i can ask every council as part of the funding we’ve given to provide an offer to everyone. And that’s what we’re confident of now ….

Diungkapkan bahwa “big issue knows better than anybody. What I’m saying is that public money won’t fall away. This is a fixable problem and it’s about a national effort to fix it. Stop-start is not fair to the organisations that are out there working with rough sleepers. That’s the only way to do it. You get a surge of sentiment around rough sleeping later in the year, for really good reasons, but when you hit the earlier months of the new year it falls away. ”.

Sebagaimana diketahui, those unable to get their hands on a copy by buying one from a vendor can order the limited edition burnham cover magazine from the big issue online shop. The managing director, Russell Blackman, said it was “up there” with some of the most significant Big Issue covers during the 35 years since it launched.

Sebagaimana diketahui, “over those 35 years, we’ve supported 110,000 vendors who have benefited from buying and selling the magazine. And that combines to make £162m worth of earnings for those vendors. They’ve sold over 230m copies. ”.

Sebagaimana diketahui, of the “home” cover, he said: “for me, this is a symbol of a promise. So this artwork and this front cover of the Big Issue could be part of his legacy if he exceeds in his ambitions, but it also could be a constant reminder that he hasn’t achieved it.

Diungkapkan bahwa “it’s striking. Every magazine we produce has to be eye-catching, but it always has to have an element of creative activism within that as well. It’s bold. ”.

#670. ‘Shameless venality’: how a flurry of lawsuits has thwarted Trump’s self-enrichment schemes
