#722. ‘Pull back the curtain’ on treatment of sexual assault victims in court, says UK government adviser

📅 15 Nov 2026

‘Pull back the curtain’ on treatment of sexual assault victims in court, says UK government adviser

Tanggal: 15 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.theguardian.com/law/2026/nov/15/examine-courts-treatment-sexual-assault-victims-says-government-adviser

Professor urges ministers to use awareness triggered by Russell Brand conviction to examine use of rape myths in trials.

The debate triggered by high-profile cases must “pull back the curtain” on the treatment of people making allegations of sexual offences in the criminal justice system in England and Wales, the government’s independent adviser on rape has told the Guardian.

Prof Katrin Hohl, who has advised the government in an overhaul of how rape is treated by police forces and the Crown Prosecution Service (CPS), said the government should use the public awareness triggered by Russell Brand’s conviction for rape to examine the use of rape myths and jury direction in trials.

“So many things are going wrong in our justice system when it comes to the treatment of victims of rape and sexual assault, but most of the time no one ever finds out what has happened during the investigation process or during a trial,” she said.

Hohl said that despite “significant progress” made by police forces and the CPS – who have been directed to make investigations more focused on suspects rather than victim behaviour under a system known as Operation Soteria – the court system was being left behind.

A report published by Hohl last month suggested sexual assault cases prepared under the new system were experiencing “a cliff edge” when they came to trial, and were potentially coming up against practices such as the use of rape myths by defence barristers.

“We essentially know very little about how rape and sexual assault cases play out in England and Wales and it is time to pull back the curtain,” said Hohl.

Sebagaimana diketahui, “we need proper research into the actions of barristers, judges and juries during trials so that victims can actually get the justice the law says they should achieve. ”.

Sebagaimana diketahui, hohl’s remarks come after the victims commissioner, claire waxman, called for a new legal duty on judges to direct juries, if rape myths have been ventured during a trial, stating: “justice must be grounded in evidence, not misconceptions. ”.

During the Brand trial, which saw the comedian sentenced to more than 10 years in prison after he was found guilty of raping one woman and sexually assaulting three others, his barrister, Ian Winter, said Brand’s accusers had not “resisted or screamed or even tried to leave”.

Government ministers are also understood to be considering calls for a “staggered” consent law, which would make it illegal for adults over a certain age to have sex with 16- and 17-year-olds, after a woman who alleges she was raped by Brand when she was 16 launched a campaign for the law to be changed.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, mia latter, who says she was in an abusive three-month relationship with brand when he was 30 and she was 16, told the sunday times: “i think we all sort of agree that … adults shouldn’t be allowed to have sexual relationships with children, with somebody under the age of 18. That really doesn’t seem like a gigantic leap to take. ”.

Diungkapkan bahwa on sunday, pat mcfadden said ministers would discuss the issue. Speaking to the BBC’s Sunday with Laura Kuenssberg, the work and pensions secretary said questions over a staggered age of consent have “been raised and will be discussed”, adding: “[I] can’t tell you what the conclusion of that would be, but the last week has certainly put that up in lights. ”.

Since the trial, several support services for victims of sexual assault and rape said they had been experiencing a significant increase in the number of calls and messages to helplines.

Rape Crisis centres are experiencing “very significant demand” and phonelines have been inundated with calls since Brand was convicted of rape, said Ciara Bergman, chief executive of Rape Crisis England & Wales.

Many women are also now questioning their own experiences with older men, she said, after separate allegations were made public that David Walliams preyed on young women for sex.

Berdasarkan laporan, earlier this week, it was announced that a series of “serious” sexual offence allegations against walliams were being looked at by the metropolitan police after an investigation by the guardian and itv news. One woman described her alleged encounter with Walliams when she was 15 as “sexual assault”. Walliams denies any wrongdoing.

Bergman said calls to the 24/7 rape and sexual abuse support line had quadrupled since the start of the month, while rape crisis centres were reporting a massive rise in demand for help.

Berdasarkan laporan, “that demand comes from a range of places,” she said. “There are people who see the news and are reminded of their own experiences and people who are retraumatised by seeing this issue in the news.

Sebagaimana diketahui, “but there are people who may have experienced predation and exploitation at vulnerable times in their lives, and they’re now beginning to question their own experiences. ”.

She echoed calls for greater transparency in trials, and argued the coverage of high profile cases had highlighted the gap in the public knowledge around the experience of going to trial and issues around consent.

Diungkapkan bahwa “our centres are adept at responding to victims but they are under very significant pressure,” she said. “When you look at these stories and the response to them there is no question about the need for more comprehensive support and more rape crisis centres so victims and survivors can get the justice they deserve. ”.

A Ministry of Justice spokesperson said: “We are always looking at ways we can improve how the justice system treats victims of sexual violence.

Diungkapkan bahwa “that’s why we are changing the law to stop irrelevant evidence that relies on myths being weaponised against victims, rolling out specialist courtrooms for rape and serious sexual offences and improving support for victims, backed by our record £550m investment in support services. ”.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, support for anyone affected by sexual abuse issues is available in the uk from rape crisis on 0808 500 2222 in england and wales, 0808 801 0302 in scotland, or 0800 0246 991 in northern ireland. Samaritans can be contacted on freephone 116 123. The National Association for People Abused in Childhood (Napac) offers support for adult survivors on 0808 801 0331. Other international helplines are available for people affected by sexual abuse and childhood abuse, and people in crisis.

Labour rebellion over Rosebank oilfield expected to top 100 MPs

Total of 75 have already signed letter to Burnham opposing plans as discontent also grows over Europe and welfare changes.

As many as 100 Labour MPs could sign a letter opposing the giant Rosebank oilfield, as discontent among backbenchers looks likely to surge this week, with rebellions also brewing over Europe and welfare changes.

A total of 75 MPs have already signed the private letter, which is expected to be delivered in the next fortnight to Andy Burnham as part of a campaign in which Labour MPs from the party’s 2024 intake are playing a significant role.

While the energy secretary, Miatta Fahnbulleh, is said to be minded to reject the controversial oilfield, she could still be overruled by the prime minister, amid a cabinet split in which the chancellor, John Healy, is in favour of the plans.

The letter, first reported by the Sunday Times, says Britain’s credibility as a global climate leader would be destroyed if drilling went ahead off the Scottish coast, and argues that it would not reduce energy bills.

“We’re at a point where Reform and the Greens are on the back foot and Labour is enjoying a bounce, but a lot of people are very worried about Rosebank,” said one Labour MP who signed the letter.

Berdasarkan laporan, “andy’s big problem is also that he has let three fights start at the same time, which could prove to be very awkward. Rows about this and what our position should be on European relations have come at the same time as the debates that will come this week over [Alan Milburn’s] proposals on out-of-work benefits for young people. If control of the narrative on one issue is lost it could lead to panic about another. ”.

Diungkapkan bahwa another labour mp said: “the interest in this is not just from the 2024 mps. There are a good number of colleagues who just don’t sign letters like this normally, but who are concerned. It’s about staying true to what we told voters, and the fact that a lot of people after the summer we’ve had are really now making a link between the climate crisis and what their experience was when it comes to temperatures or flooding.

Berdasarkan laporan, “the prospect of government resignations also looms if the drilling licence is granted. While the foreign secretary, Ed Miliband, is unlikely to go, such a decision would also put [him] in an awkward position given his past description of Rosebank as a ‘colossal waste of taxpayer money and climate vandalism’. ”.

Instrumental in organising the letter is Sera, an affiliate and member-led environmental organisation within Labour, whose members include Miliband as well as ministers such as Luke Pollard, Georgia Gould, Matthew Pennycook and others.

Some who have signed the letter include those who had reluctantly backed the smaller Jackdaw field on the basis that it was primarily gas.

The company operating both fields said on Sunday that gas had begun to flow from the Jackdaw platform, “bringing vital UK energy resources ashore in time for winter”.

Diungkapkan bahwa claire mueller, jackdaw project director at the north sea oil and gas producer adura, said rosebank and jackdaw were expected to generate £1. 4bn in tax revenues before the end of this parliament, rising to £3. 8bn by the end of the next.

“With Jackdaw now producing, and other major projects including Rosebank in our pipeline, we have an opportunity to build a bright future for the North Sea, supporting jobs, investment and Britain’s energy security for years to come,” she added.

Sign up for the Breaking News UK email to get newsletter alerts direct to your inbox.

Heavy backing for Rosebank is also coming from Labour-supporting unions the GMB and Unite, which have considerable influence over Burnham’s operation, and who are also expressing concern at his talk of rejoining the EU.

Diungkapkan bahwa the letter opposing rosebank is modelled on the one that derailed keir starmer’s welfare overhaul plans, which spanned the new intake and veterans. Yet one of its signatories pointed out stark differences.

Diungkapkan bahwa “i do think it will probably get to around 100 mps and may go beyond it, but the welfare rebels were willing to be much more ruthless. The other thing is that some of the people behind that rebellion are now in government and they are wise to these things. ”.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the government has described their process around rosebank as “quasi-judicial”. Fahnbulleh previously told the Guardian that the decision would be consistent with the UK’s climate obligations, carbon budgets and the energy transition.

Proposed secure accommodation blocks at Campsfield House immigration removal centre in Oxfordshire will be 20 metres from a sewage pumping station, according to a written submission from Thames Water.

Diungkapkan bahwa a senior development manager at the company wrote that it could give rise to “amenity effects, including odour, noise, vibration, lighting associated with maintenance activities, insects and flies” for any inhabitants. In a previous submission, the company wrote that any development may lead to sewage flooding.

The warnings, which come as the government hopes to expand the immigration detention estate by 40%, have been seized upon by campaigners against the expansion.

Ally Swadling, the lead legal education officer at the charity Right to Remain, said: “Thames Water’s concerns about sewage infrastructure at Campsfield show how little regard is being given to even the most basic standards of sanitation and human dignity.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, “they reinforce what we already know – this government is putting its political priorities above people’s lives and wellbeing. ”.

The centre near Kidlington re-opened in December 2025 after it was shut in 2018 following years of problems, including suicides, riots, escapes and complaints about conditions.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the home office is planning to increase the centre’s capacity from 160 bed spaces to 400, and to convert existing buildings. According to the Thames Water submission in October, officials also “raised concerns regarding capacity within the foul water, surface water and water supply networks” in the local area.

A separate 2015 written consultation response, which was submitted in June, states the development may lead to sewage flooding in the area.

“Thames Water request that an impact study be undertaken to ascertain, with a greater degree of certainty, whether the proposed development will lead to overloading of existing infrastructure,” it said.

Written representations, including that of Thames Water, will be heard at a public inquiry beginning on 14 December.

Oxfordshire county council has formally objected to the expansion of Campsfield House, saying it risks intensifying existing public concern, and called for the site to be shut permanently.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, this week, the head of germany's federal employment agency, andrea nahles, warned that the introduction ai would cost germany as many 800,000 jobs in the next 15 years. Though she also said AI could eventually create a similar number of jobs, clearly the socioeconomic upheaval would be considerable.

Sebagaimana diketahui, nahles is not the only leading figure concerned about job losses caused by ai. Karsten Wildberger, Germany's minister for digital transformation and government modernization, takes any opportunity he can to warn that Germany must prepare for the economic disruptions of AI.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

Berdasarkan laporan, and even for wildberger, a former ceo of a massive retail company, part of the future economy might come down to giving people free money. He was convinced, he told the Neue Osnabrücker Zeitung in March, "that an unconditional basic income can be part of the solution to cushion the upheavals in the labor market. ".

Diungkapkan bahwa campaigners have cautiously welcomed this new openness from unexpected quarters. "It shows that in the face of technological transformation we also need to look differently at the question of how we need to secure people's economic stability," said Kirsten Herrmann, board member at the nonprofit Mein Grundeinkommen (My Basic Income), which runs various projects examining the social and economic impact of universal basic income (UBI).

Diungkapkan bahwa "but i also think that individual statements by politicians don't amount to a political change, of course," she told dw. "It just means that we need to enter a serious and constructive debate about what kind of a role a basic income can play. ".

Sebagaimana diketahui, the idea of a universal basic income is very old: english renaissance philosopher thomas more mentions it in his 1516 book utopia, for instance. But since the 20th century, it has largely been seen as an idealistic notion adopted by leftists — that is, until some of the world's most high-profile tech bosses latched onto the idea as a way to offset the utopian advances they said AI would bring.

Diungkapkan bahwa in 2017, elon musk, who had co-founded the corporation openai two years earlier, predicted that a universal basic income would at some stage become inevitable. Since then, leading figures in the AI sector, including Dario Amodei, CEO of Anthropic, and Sam Altman, the other founder of OpenAI, have all gone on record in support of UBI (though Altman's interest has cooled somewhat since he launched a massive UBI experiment in the US in 2019).

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

Berdasarkan laporan, but herrmann said it's a "double-edged sword" when such figures mention the idea. She isn't convinced that organizations like hers and people Elon Musk want the same thing.

Diungkapkan bahwa "on the one hand, it's always nice when the debate about a basic income gets attention from prominent voices," she said. "On the other hand, the basic income that people from the tech business talk about is a kind of neoliberal basic income: They talk about what to do when there are no more profitable jobs for people, because they still actually do need people to do certain things, whereas we talk about a basic income that is meant to give people a secure economic base — before the crisis in the job market happens. ".

What makes the comments of Merz and Wildberger all the more eyebrow-raising is that mainstream German economists have long since rejected the basic income idea.

Diungkapkan bahwa dominik enste, director of the democracy, society, and economic ethics department at the german economic institute in cologne, dismissed the idea out of hand — ai or no ai. UBI was, he said, just too expensive, especially in a country that already has plenty of social welfare costs.

"Many economists have calculated that implementing this in many countries is financially unfeasible — in Germany, for one, simply because of the need to fund commitments that have already been made (including pension payments)," he told DW in an email.

Diungkapkan bahwa however, he also added: "we will have to change our social security systems if work is replaced by ai and, if necessary, tax ai-generated income. But it will be a conditional basic income that still provides incentives to earn a living. ".

Diungkapkan bahwa other economists are more positive about the idea. "But a lot of the current thrust is to replace workers to increase profits and increase corporate control, though this is not the only path possible. "How this plays out depends on many choices we make, and on who makes these choices, in whose interest," said Maximilian Kasy, professor of economics at the University of Oxford and author of a book on the impact of AI on society. ".

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, kasy thinks a basic income could be a good solution, "especially if it's financed in a progressive way (so that only those at the lower end of the income distribution are net recipients)," he wrote. "The 'small print' matters very much, though!".

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

Berdasarkan laporan, if the warnings of wildberger, musk, altman et al. are to be believed, AI is already causing a bigger upheaval than any other technological advance in history, partly because of the speed of the innovations, but also because of the scale of the potential impact.

Berdasarkan laporan, ai innovation is affecting the jobs of the traditional urban middle classes across the entire world. In 2024, the International Monetary Fund predicted that some 40% of employment in the world would be shaped by AI innovations, and as much as 60% in rich, industrialized nations.

For her part, Herrmann thinks we are not yet asking the truly fundamental questions about the socioeconomic implications of AI: Not just how do we replace the lost jobs and keep the capitalist system going, but what do we actually want to use AI for? As she put it: "Who actually profits when we become more productive through AI? And how do we redistribute that profit to everyone?".

Sebagaimana diketahui, this, she argued, is why there needs to be more debate about how exactly ai is used in the world of work. "Which jobs are going to be replaced by AI is not some law of nature," said Herrmann. "It's something that we can shape politically and socially — and then the bigger question is: Who gets a say?".

Tanggal: 16 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/nov/16/pope-leo-speech-peru-justice-for-amazon-activists-environment

Pontiff delivers forceful speech on final day in Peru as he travels from high in the Andes into the Amazon.

Pope Leo XIV has demanded justice for environmental defenders killed for protecting the Amazon and backed efforts by Indigenous peoples to stop their lands from being ravaged by logging and illegal mining.

On the penultimate day of his South American tour, Leo on Sunday travelled into the Peruvian Amazon and channelled one of Pope Francis’s core teachings that links care for the most vulnerable with care for God’s creation.

“The cry of the Earth and the cry of the poor are inseparable,” Leo told Indigenous representatives and missionaries gathered along the Ucayali River in the north-eastern city of Pucallpa.

He said he came to Pucallpa to support them in their search for justice and peace and referred to what environmental groups estimate have been 57 murders of environmental defenders between 2010 and 2024.

“The blood of these brothers cries out to God and demands justice,” Leo said to applause from the crowd, many of whom were wearing traditional feathered headwear and face markings of the region.

Berdasarkan laporan, in addition to deforestation, illegal gold mining has become an increasingly lucrative business in the amazon, devastating forests and polluting rivers. Illegal mining and coca production has also driven deforestation.

Leo addressed the combination of threats in one of his most forceful speeches to date, drawing on his years of experience as a Peruvian bishop and Francis’s constant preaching about the environment and the plight of Indigenous groups.

During the encounter and a subsequent mass in Pucallpa, he demanded a different model of economic development that respects the Earth and the Indigenous peoples who care for it, rather than the “irresponsible exploitation” by outside actors.

Sebagaimana diketahui, “very little has been done – and very slowly at that – while the means to exploit and pollute creation have accelerated,” he said at mass. “In the face of these evils, let us not bury the Lord’s gifts, for he gives us the strength to repair and heal the suffering caused by an insatiable thirst for domination. ”.

In Peru, most murders of environmental defenders go unpunished; only a few have resulted in convictions.

The most recent conviction came in the case of Kichwa leader Quinto Inuma Alvarado, who was murdered in 2023 when he was ambushed by hitmen on a river in the San Martín region, the Amazonian territory he was defending.

Leo also referred to a notorious rise in sexual violence against Indigenous Awajún and Wampis schoolgirls in the northern Amazon, and blasted the “impunity” and “corruption” surrounding them.

The Awajún and Wampis Women’s Council has recorded 370 cases of sexual violence in the Condorcanqui province between January and July.

Julio Cusurichi, an Indigenous leader, handed Leo a letter during his visit to Pucallpa, asking him to help protect the rights of uncontacted Indigenous relatives.

“The Peruvian state is weakening the mechanisms that should safeguard their territories,” said the letter from the Indigenous rights organisation Aidesep, on which Cusurichi is a board member.

Diungkapkan bahwa “we cannot allow economic interests to take precedence over the lives and rights of these vulnerable peoples. Therefore, we ask Pope Leo XIV to raise his voice and support this urgent call for their defence. ”.

Berdasarkan laporan, cardinal pedro barreto praised the pope’s decision to meet with indigenous peoples. Barreto, a former Peruvian archbishop who helped win a multimillion-dollar pollution payout for an Andean town, said: “[Leo] is well aware of all the historical suffering … corruption, illegal mining, deforestation, and the contempt shown by politicians. ”.

Sebagaimana diketahui, luis e fernandez, co-founder of cincia, a scientific research centre in peru, also hailed the pontiff’s power to raise awareness. “Pope Leo’s recognition of pollution from illegal mining brings much-needed attention to a crisis affecting Indigenous and riverine communities across the Amazon,” he said.

Fernandez visited the Vatican in October and presented Leo with scientific evidence detailing the impact of illegal gold mining and associated mercury poisoning.

Diungkapkan bahwa leo’s last full day in peru was also his most ambitious, crisscrossing the nation to minister to communities high in the andes mountains. Peru’s air force released footage of the pope inside a helicopter and said it was “an unforgettable memory” to take Leo around the country.

His first stop was the mountain city of Cusco, where huge crowds greeted him.

Diungkapkan bahwa “it is all worth it,” said margarida salomon, 63, who said she came from sucre in bolivia to see the pontiff, spending about $500 to take a bus and sleep in a tent. “I am still getting to know this pope, but the fact he is here in the Andes means a lot. ”.

Diungkapkan bahwa the visit to cusco, 3,400m (more than 11,000ft) above sea level, tested leo’s stamina as he continues recovering from lung cancer surgery last month. Leo sat in the chair of his popemobile during part of the ride around Cusco, but it wasn’t clear if that was to preserve his energy or to steady himself on the uneven streets.

In general, the 71-year-old Leo has seemed unfazed by the toll of the three-nation South American trip, the longest of his pontificate.

Pro-government forces said troops were being moved to defend the interim capital, Aden (file photo).

Yemeni pro-government forces backed by Saudi Arabia have said they are withdrawing from an area overlooking the strategically important Bab al-Mandab Strait, leaving it under the control of the Iran-backed Houthi movement.

Yemen's military said it was redeploying troops from the key shipping gateway at the southern end of the Red Sea to defend its interim capital, Aden.

The shift ends a weeks-long offensive to try to secure the area near the waterway after the Houthis seized it in a surprise offensive in September, squeezing global oil exports and prompting thousands to flee.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, houthi-run media reported later on sunday the group had taken control of the territory. Saudi Arabia has not commented.

Pro-government forces said they had "secured" the strait in early October as they sought to retake crucial ground from the Houthis, who said they had captured areas including Perim Island at the mouth of the strait and the strategic port city of Mokha a month prior.

Watch: Why is the Bab al-Mandab Strait so important?.

But the Saudi-backed forces fighting on behalf of Yemen's internationally recognised government said on Sunday they were withdrawing to reinforce troops elsewhere, with the southern city of Aden a "priority".

The Reuters news agency reported a Southern Armed Forces statement which said troops were being withdrawn "from Dhubab Airport and the Bab al-Mandab area".

It said the decision had been made with the aim of "strengthening the front lines and addressing existing threats".

The Houthis said they posed no threat to international shipping passing through the waterway when they captured it, but that they would continue to target vessels from Saudi Arabia.

However, the seizure contributed to a surge in global oil prices because Saudi Arabia had been relying on the Red Sea for oil exports since the US and Israel's war with Iran effectively closed the Strait of Hormuz.

Saudi Arabia responded with hundreds of air strikes, while the Houthis launched hundreds of drones and missiles at its cities and infrastructure.

Diungkapkan bahwa the un has estimated that nearly 330,000 people have been displaced in yemen as the fighting has since escalated. Hundreds of people are reported to have been killed.

Why is the Bab al-Mandab Strait so important?.

Yemeni military says it has 'secured' Red Sea waterway.

Yemenis flee across Red Sea as Houthis and Saudi-backed forces escalate war.

Yemen has been devastated by a civil war that began in 2014, when the Houthis ousted the government from its capital Sanaa.

The conflict escalated in 2015, after a Saudi-led coalition of Arab states intervened in an attempt to restore the government's rule.

A four-year informal ceasefire began to unravel in July, when the Houthis announced a "maritime embargo" against Saudi Arabia and began missile and drone attacks on Saudi airports, oil facilities and tankers in the Red Sea.

The Houthis said they were retaliating for a Saudi blockade of ports and airports in their territory, as well as an air strike on Sanaa airport that they blamed on the kingdom.

Haines, known for supporting stronger climate action and helping establish a national anti-corruption commission, entered parliament in 2019 as the Member for Indi after working as a nurse and midwife.

Victoria Police has said its investigation, with support from the Australian Federal Police, remains ongoing and a motive is yet to be established.

"All our thoughts and prayers continue to be with Helen for her recovery," he said in a statement.

Sebagaimana diketahui, "we continue to provide support to helen, her family, community and staff as she undertakes her rehabilitation. ".

Jensen Huang resigned as chief executive of the chip manufacturer Nvidia after reports of extramarital affairs with Alice Huang and two company employees.

US intelligence agencies believe the tech chief, whose products have been crucial to the AI boom, had been targeted by Alice Huang, the former director of Megaspeed International.

US officials have alleged Alice Huang may have been acting as a Chinese intelligence asset, passing commercial information to Beijing, the New York Times has reported.

Sebagaimana diketahui, in the past three years, megaspeed has been one of nvidia’s biggest foreign customers, buying nearly us$5bn (a$7. 4bn, £3. 8bn) in AI chips and advanced hardware.

A US senator asked the commerce department to investigate whether Megaspeed had diverted Nvidia chips to China.

Megaspeed said on Sunday it would not comment on Alice Huang’s “personal and private matters”.

“Alice Huang officially left Megaspeed effective August 30, 2025 and currently has no role with the company,” it said in a statement.

The global facades of Megaspeed International form a puzzling corporate picture, and involve a lottery retailer in rural Australia, a dilapidated storefront in Kuala Lumpur and a near-empty office in Singapore.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the company on sunday said: “megaspeed designs and maintains its global operational and supply-chain control frameworks to comply with all applicable laws and regulatory regimes, including united states export control requirements and local jurisdiction rules in every market where we operate. ”.

Short seller Culper Research in May quoted a Megaspeed employee as saying Alice Huang was “still our boss”, in a report accusing Nvidia of having a “China problem”.

On Thursday, Singaporean authorities said Alice Huang had been barred from re-entering the city state after a 2025 investigation into the company’s “suspected breaches of our domestic laws”.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the ministry of home affairs said it had held alice huang’s passport from june 2025 until february. Police believed she had given them “inaccurate” information, to downplay her role at the company, but released her due to insufficient evidence.

Berdasarkan laporan, she was issued a stern warning and barred from re-entering the country. Taiwan has also barred her from re-entry, its authorities have said.

Singapore’s initial investigation related to Megaspeed’s potential “false declarations” over the purchase of computer servers.

On Friday, Malaysia said it was investigating a subsidiary of Megaspeed International over the possible diversion of advanced AI chips to other countries.

Megaspeed has previously said there was no evidence of illegal chip transfers.

Berdasarkan laporan, its registered sydney office is home to numerous business and had no megaspeed signage, mailbox or physical presence when the guardian visited last week. No one had heard of Megaspeed Australia or its listed director, 29-year-old Kai Kang.

Reuters visited a news agency and lottery retailer, in Seymour, Victoria, an hour’s drive north of Melbourne, where a woman, who identified herself as Kang’s mother, said Kang was based in Shanghai and did not know anything about the Singaporean company.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, kang has not been accused of any wrongdoing. Attempts to contact him were unsuccessful.

The US attorney general, Todd Blanche, said last week that the Justice Department had not concluded whether Alice Huang was a Chinese spy.

Diungkapkan bahwa asked whether she was a spy, the us president, donald trump, said: “i don’t know if that’s been determined yet. ”.

Berdasarkan laporan, beijing rejected the allegations as unsubstantiated. Associated Press was unable to reach Alice Huang for comment. The Guardian has sought comment from Alice Huang.

Berdasarkan laporan, megaspeed began as the overseas arm of a chinese video game developer and was incorporated in singapore in 2015 as 7road international. It adopted its current name in March 2023, when all its shares were transferred to Huang Le Limited, a British Virgin Islands company. Alice Huang is also known by her Chinese name, Huang Le.

By November 2023, she was no longer listed as a Megaspeed director, and all her shares had been transferred to an entity owned by Singaporean businessman Tan Yong Pong, also known as James Tan.

Diungkapkan bahwa the company’s finances have also attracted attention. Singapore corporate records show its total assets rose roughly 90-fold from end-2023 to 2024, reaching almost US$3bn (A$4. 4bn, £2. 3bn).

#753. Prince Harry praises war veterans on surprise visit to Ukraine

📅 15 Nov 2026

Prince Harry praises war veterans on surprise visit to Ukraine

Tanggal: 15 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/c60evn992jq8o?at_medium=RSS&at_campaign=rss

Prince Harry made an emotional visit to meet injured war veterans inside Ukraine.

The Duke of Sussex has received an enthusiastic welcome in a surprise visit to Ukraine to support injured war veterans, meeting Ukrainian competitors taking part in his Invictus Games.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, there were emotional scenes as he was applauded by injured service men and women in lviv, where he told his audience: "you're going to win the war. ".

Prince Harry spent two days at events for veterans, with a press blackout for security reasons until he had left Ukraine, as the country continues to face missile attacks from Russia.

Ukraine has more than 150,000 injured war veterans and the prince visited projects supporting their treatment and rehabilitation.

Prince Harry met Kostiantyn Vlasenko, who was airlifted by a drone from the front.

"Ukraine now is experiencing elements of war that no other country has experienced before," he said - with technology advancing in areas such as drone warfare, but also in protecting cities and providing treatment.

A mobile phone app is where Ukrainians look for air raid warnings, telling them the direction, timing and type of any incoming missiles.

At the Superhumans Center near Lviv, Harry was shown how growing numbers of injured veterans receive groundbreaking treatment.

International experts used to come to help Ukraine, he said, but "now that has flipped," with Ukraine having the greater expertise with trauma injuries to share with others.

Mykhailo Damaskin, pictured with his dog Stitch, has received experimental treatment to walk.

That included an innovation for Mykhailo Damaskin, a Ukrainian air assault forces veteran, who was so seriously injured in fighting in Kherson he was never expected to walk again.

Berdasarkan laporan, in an experimental treatment he had a spinal cord stimulator implanted in his back, which allows him to walk, but has to be re-charged every 12 hours. He cannot feel his feet and controls his steps using his eyes.

He needs to be plugged in and charged up to be able to move - and jokes that he is "like a demo model of a Tesla".

Berdasarkan laporan, "my goal is to go to the invictus games. I promised my father before he was killed that I'd be part of the team to represent Ukraine internationally.

"I'll prove to every guy with spinal cord injuries that life goes on after injury," said Mykhailo.

At the Superhumans Center Prince Harry sat at the bedside of Konstiantyn Vlasenko, who was airlifted from the front line by a drone last month in a rescue that was a first of its kind.

He had been alone for more than 200 days and had stayed at his position, despite losing both his feet.

In a moving encounter, Prince Harry told him he represented the spirit of resilience of Ukraine.

Berdasarkan laporan, and he described the injured veterans as "role models", promising his audience: "the rest of the world will continue to support you. ".

Along with all the determination, it was an inescapably poignant sight too, with so many families and children at the medical facility visiting the growing numbers of badly injured war casualties.

Injured veterans took part in a game of wheelchair rugby.

Blast damage from missiles on an historic building in Lviv.

At a noisy sports centre, Prince Harry arrived to watch a wheelchair rugby match taking place, with some thunderous collisions between the players.

He was welcomed by the competitors in what he has called his Invictus "family" and soon the visit turned into something approaching a group hug, with Harry disappearing into a sea of selfies and handshakes.

He was presented with a T-shirt remembering prisoners of war held by Russian forces.

And he later had a chance to play one of the events at the Invictus Games, a tennis-style competition called pickleball.

Ivan Voinov, who lost a leg, has learned to dance again with his wife.

Watching was Ivan Voinov, who has lost a leg and suffered head injuries, but who is using sport to help his rehabilitation - including learning to dance again.

He said that dancing was his way to be together with his wife again, which meant so much to his recovery and recovering his identity.

At an Invictus awards ceremony during the visit, Prince Harry was greeted with choruses of "Harry, Harry, Harry", getting a rock star welcome.

A Banksy-style piece of street art in Lviv shows the missiles falling.

"Every single time I come back to Ukraine, I feel welcome, I feel warmth, I feel encouragement," he said, having returned for a fourth trip here during wartime.

He promised that "when the war is over and when Ukraine wins, we will be ready to support you in holding an Invictus Games".

There have been 400 wounded service men and women in Ukraine taking part in trials for next year's games, being hosted in Birmingham.

The sports events are an attempt to encourage rehabilitation and to recognise the resilience of people overcoming their challenges.

Prince Harry told a gathering of new Invictus members of a "cultural shift" from people being socially awkward about seeing injured veterans to wanting to show respect.

"These people have so much to offer," he said.

"Recovery cannot wait for the war to end, The scale of need in Ukraine is huge, and wounded, injured and sick service personnel and veterans need the chance to rebuild their lives now," said Rob Owen, chief executive officer of the Invictus Games Foundation.

#755. Canada bars Russia from Junior World Championships

📅 15 Nov 2026

Canada bars Russia from Junior World Championships

Tanggal: 15 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/ice-hockey/articles/cqkgm0jgv4mdo?at_medium=RSS&at_campaign=rss

Russia's hopes of reintegration into international sport suffered a setback when it was barred from the upcoming Junior Ice Hockey World Championships.

Canada said it would deny entry to Russian athletes as a result of the war in Ukraine.

"Due to the position and restrictions formally communicated by the Canadian government, the Russian Under-20 national team is unable to participate in the World Junior Championship," the International Ice Hockey Federation (IIHF) said in a statement.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, it said that "after carefully assessing the feasibility of alternative arrangements, the iihf council has determined that canada will remain as host and the tournament will proceed from 26 december 2026 to 5 january 2027 in edmonton and red deer. ".

The Russian Ice Hockey Federation called the IIHF's decision "unacceptable and unlawful" and said it would appeal to the International Olympic Committee (IOC).

"The IIHF's decision was made solely due to political reasons," it said in a statement.

Sebagaimana diketahui, "the exclusion of the russian national team violates fundamental legal principles, olympism, the principle of non-discrimination, equality among athletes and the integrity of international tournaments. ".

Russia had been suspended from competing in IIHF events since the country invaded Ukraine in 2022, but last month the Court of Arbitration for Sport overturned the ban.

It said that the IIHF's arguments citing safety and security were "not supported by sufficient evidence" and ordered it to allow Russia to participate in its events.

The move was welcomed by Russia but condemned by Ukraine and along with some sponsors of the Junior World Championships.

Six European ice hockey federations said they would refuse to play Russia if they were allowed to take part, appearing to leave the tournament in limbo.

On Wednesday the Canadian government said it would deny visas to any Russian athletes, effectively barring them from participating.

It is the latest example of a wider backlash against efforts to allow Russia to return to international sport.

This week Norway, Finland and Estonia said they would block visas for Russian and Belarusian athletes.

Norway is preparing to host skiing's Cross-country World Cup next month, while Finland is due to stage the Figure Skating World Championships in March.

The International Skating Union (ISU) has said it "believes that athletes should not be punished for the actions of their governments in a world where, sadly, many conflicts are ongoing", and that it was "seeking clarifications" from officials in Finland.

In March several athletes from Russia and Belarus were allowed to compete under their national flags at the Winter Paralympics after partial suspensions by the International Paralympic Committee were lifted.

In July the IOC provisionally reinstated Russia to its competitions, saying a ban introduced in 2023 was "no longer applicable".

However, sports federations can enforce their own eligibility criteria.

While World Gymnastics, World Aquatics and World Boxing have removed restrictions on Russian athletes competing, a total ban has been maintained by World Athletics.

Last month it was announced that Moscow will host the 2030 World Weightlifting Championships, the first time an Olympic federation has chosen to stage a global event in Russia since the invasion of Ukraine.

#756. Wife of assassinated ex-Haitian leader registers for presidential election

📅 16 Nov 2026

Wife of assassinated ex-Haitian leader registers for presidential election

Tanggal: 16 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/cmwy83432q1jo?at_medium=RSS&at_campaign=rss

Martine Moise was injured in the gun attack that killed her husband.

The widow of assassinated former Haitian president Jovenel Moise has registered as a presidential candidate for next year's elections in the Caribbean nation.

Martine Moise was injured in the gun attack that killed her husband at their home in the capital, Port-au-Prince, in 2021.

Haiti, which last held an election in 2016, has been plagued with chronic instability and gang violence.

Elections were scheduled to be held in December but were postponed last month until July due to the country's insecurity.

Moise has to comment on her candidacy but the electoral council website showed her registration on Sunday.

Diungkapkan bahwa last week she said on x: "haiti will rise again on its own two feet, because politics needs to be done differently. ".

A total of 33 candidates have registered for the elections, including former presidents Michel Martelly and Jocelerme Privert, former prime minister Claude Joseph and former foreign minister Dominique Dupuy.

Jovenel Moise, who led Haiti from 2017 until his death, was shot dead at his home in Port-au-Prince in July 2021, allegedly by a group of mainly Colombian mercenaries.

Martine Moise suffered serious gunshot wounds during the attack and was flown to a hospital in Florida.

She was charged in connection with the assassination in 2024, but the indictment was overturned last year.

The assassination shook the Caribbean nation to its core, with many Haitians shocked that the 53-year-old was killed with such apparent ease.

Thirty suspects have been indicted over the killing so far and in September 18 people were flown from Haiti to Florida to stand trial for their alleged involvement in the assassination.

Haiti has been engulfed in a wave of gang violence since the assassination of Moise.

At least 1,408 people were killed and 656 injured from April through to June this year, according to the UN Integrated Office in Haiti.

#757. Rocket from Boeing-Lockheed firm fails mid-flight, destroys payload of Amazon satellites

📅 16 Nov 2026

Rocket from Boeing-Lockheed firm fails mid-flight, destroys payload of Amazon satellites

Tanggal: 16 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.dw.com/en/rocket-from-boeing-lockheed-firm-fails-mid-flight-destroys-payload-of-amazon-satellites/a-79953931?maca=en-rss-en-all-1573-rdf

Berdasarkan laporan, a vulcan rocket suffered an anomaly about 10 minutes after liftoff from florida, failing to deliver 40 amazon leo satellites to orbit. It was the first total mission failure in the company's history.

Sebagaimana diketahui, a vulcan rocket operated by united launch alliance, a joint venture of boeing and lockheed martin, failed about 10 minutes after liftoff from the cape canaveral space force station on sunday. The incident resulted in the loss of all 40 AmazonLeo internet satellites aboard, marking the company's first mission failure.

"Based on data received by our Launch Director, we confirm that the Vulcan vehicle launched from Space Launch Complex 41 suffered an anomaly 10 minutes into the flight and failed to deliver the Amazon mission to orbit," ULA said in a ​statement.

The exact cause was not immediately clear.

Berdasarkan laporan, "every flight generates data, and every flight teaches us something. Since the anomaly just occurred, we don't have any specific data yet to understand what occurred today," ULA added.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the failed launch marks ‌a major setback for ula's new flagship rocket. The two-decade-old ⁠company was set to begin a regular cadence of launches for Amazon's burgeoning satellite internet program.

The failure is expected to trigger a lengthy technical investigation, potentially grounding the Vulcan rocket for months.

Diungkapkan bahwa us companies could face reduced launch capacity amid other rocket failures, industry challenges and uncertainty over the future availability of spacex's falcon 9, the world's most active rocket. SpaceX is no longer accepting bookings for the rocket.

Sebagaimana diketahui, "there is risk with any launch, and that's especially true for inaugural missions like lv-01," amazon said in a statement, referring to sunday's mission. "ULA has been a trusted partner for Amazon, and we believe they'll learn from this mission and deliver on their long-term plans for Vulcan. ".

Sebagaimana diketahui, ula was formed in 2006 through the merger of boeing's delta rocket program and lockheed martin's atlas rocket program. The incident marked the first total mission failure in the company's history, ending its record of successful mission deliveries since its formation.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, sunday's launch was vulcan's fifth since its debut in 2024 and its first in nine months. The gap followed separate technical investigations into its solid rocket boosters and core BE-4 engines, which are supplied by Blue Origin, the space company founded by Amazon founder Jeff Bezos.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the solid rocket boosters had come under scrutiny after anomalies on vulcan's previous two flights, including a february 2026 mission for the us space force. Both missions successfully delivered their payloads into orbit despite the booster problems.

Diungkapkan bahwa the space force paused vulcan's national security launches pending the outcome of an investigation and the implementation of corrective measures. Sunday's Amazon mission was expected to provide further data before the military decided whether to clear the rocket for those launches.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, an investigation traced the problem to the engine's main oxygen valve. Blue Origin subsequently developed modifications for the BE-4 engines supplied to ULA, and the engines installed on Vulcan were retrofitted, ULA officials said.

It remains unclear whether the BE-4 engines played any role in Sunday's failure.

Diungkapkan bahwa amazon relies on third-party launch providers to deploy satellites for its leo internet network. Other launch providers have also faced technical problems and delays.

Blue Origin's New Glenn explosion in May occurred during a ground test, just days before the rocket was scheduled to launch Amazon Leo satellites.

Repeated launch setbacks have complicated Amazon's efforts to compete with SpaceX's Starlink satellite internet network, which has more than 11,000 satellites and millions of customers worldwide.

Sebagaimana diketahui, spacex's advantage over satellite internet rivals is partly due to its ability to use its own rockets to deploy satellites. Other companies rely on external launch providers, adding to the cost and complexity of building their constellations.

Sebagaimana diketahui, before sunday's failed mission, amazon had launched 398 leo satellites across 14 missions since 2025, according to reuters. That represented about 12% of the 3,236 satellites the company needs for global coverage. Amazon had hoped to begin initial internet services this year.

#758. Steering failure preceded New Orleans cruise ship collision, says NTSB

Steering failure preceded New Orleans cruise ship collision, says NTSB

Tanggal: 15 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/c65y131w1534o?at_medium=RSS&at_campaign=rss

The tanker that struck a cruise ship docked in New Orleans on Friday had a steering failure, officials said, citing preliminary findings into the collision.

It remains unclear what caused the "steering casualty" on the Atlantic Asphalt cargo vessel, the National Transportation Safety Board (NTSB) said in a media briefing on Sunday.

The collision left 32 people from the stricken American Heritage riverboat in hospital with non-critical injuries, but no-one was unaccounted for.

The NTSB said there are many different things that could be classified as a steering casualty, and they are "looking at all of them".

New Orleans port files $1m lawsuit over 'miracle on the Mississippi' tanker collision.

The tanker was upbound on the Mississippi River as it moved toward the east bank of the river just before the collision, said the NTSB, based on findings from the vessel's voyage data recorder.

Minutes before the crash, investigators said audio consistent with the ship's warning system was broadcast, along with commands to deploy the vessel's anchors and emergency ship handling orders.

"We are aware that there was an issue with the steering on board and causing the rudder to remain at a starboard position, causing the heading of the vessel to veer towards the east bank," investigator-in-charge Bart Barnum said during the news conference.

The exact issue with the steering has yet to be determined, he added.

A preliminary report from the NTSB is expected in 30 days.

Calls about the collision began around 13:30 EST (18:30 GMT) on Friday, when people began trying to help passengers escape the boat as it took on water, Port of New Orleans chief Melanie Montroll said after the incident.

There were about 129 passengers, in addition to crew members, on the American Heritage at the time of the collision, according to the port authority.

Passengers began getting off the paddlewheeler vessel, operated by American Cruise Lines, as it started listing before tipping onto its side.

Tugboat operators, police and other rescuers rushed to help while officials shut down traffic in the Mississippi River during the rescue effort.

The American Heritage had been finishing an eight-day cruise calling at destinations in Louisiana and Mississippi along the waterway.

#759. MP Helen Haines’s first words since leaving hospital after alleged attack led to double amputation

Independent MP says she is ‘overwhelmed’ by thousands of warm wishes and thanks Australians for charity donations.

Get our daily political email, free app or daily news podcast.

The independent Australian MP Helen Haines has been discharged from hospital, four weeks after she was allegedly attacked by a man outside her electorate office in Victoria resulting in the double amputation of her legs.

In a statement, Haines said she had moved to the rehabilitation stage of her recovery, which would continue in Melbourne.

“This is a really positive moment, and I am full of gratitude for the expert and compassionate care I received at the Alfred [hospital] and am receiving in this next stage,” Haines said.

Berdasarkan laporan, “i appreciate the thousands of warm wishes and supportive messages from people across indi, throughout australia and around the world. They are giving me strength as I focus on this next phase of healing. ”.

The prime minister, Anthony Albanese, said his thoughts were with Haines.

“We continue to provide support to Helen, her family, community and staff as she undertakes her rehabilitation,” Albanese said in a statement.

Haines said she was “overwhelmed” by the many Australians who had donated to the Save the Children charity fundraiser.

Her husband, Phil Haines, had made the request to the public on her behalf to donate to the charity in lieu of flowers in the aftermath of the alleged attack.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, as of monday afternoon, more than $1. 46m had been raised for the charity through Haines’s fundraising appeal.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, “i am overwhelmed by the generosity of australians in the form of donations to save the children and i look forward to working with them in due course on applying these funds to improve the lives of children. ”.

Berdasarkan laporan, haines, the federal member for the victorian seat of indi, had been in a critical but stable condition after she was repeatedly struck by a vehicle in wangaratta on 19 october. Her condition was then downgraded to “serious but stable” on 24 October.

Police will allege the 65-year-old was standing by the boot of her car outside her electoral office when a car did a U-turn and struck her repeatedly.

Sebagaimana diketahui, tarrawingee man brendan nugent, 43, has been charged and the incident continues to be investigated. He is known to her family.

Police charged Nugent with dangerous driving causing serious injury, intentionally cause serious injury and the commonwealth offence of causing harm to a commonwealth public official.

Police have also charged him with two additional offences – cultivating and possessing cannabis – according to court documents.

Our political team brings you up to speed on the stories that really matter and what they mean for you.

The foreign affairs minister, Penny Wong, paid tribute to Haines in the Senate on Monday and on behalf of the parliament wished her strength through her challenging rehabilitation.

Diungkapkan bahwa “it says a great deal about her character that even as she faces these challenges, in her statement she looks ahead to the work she wants to do to improve the lives of children following the donations to save the children that australians made at her request. It is an example of her determination and her generosity that is so admired,” Wong said.

The leader of the opposition in the Senate, Michaelia Cash, added that Haines’s discharge from hospital was warmly welcomed across the parliament.

Diungkapkan bahwa “she has demonstrated extraordinary courage and resilience. And on behalf, in particular, of my Coalition Senate colleagues, we wish Helen every strength during her continued recovery. ”.

Haines has been given leave of absence until 26 November, the last sitting day of the year.

MPs across parliament have expressed concern for their safety and that of their staff since the alleged attack, and prompted conversations about the temperature of political debate.

Albanese, during the last parliamentary sitting, warned against the rise in anger “that distorts and corrodes our public discourse”, and urged voters and politicians not to ignore it.

Berdasarkan laporan, “enabled by the anonymity and speed afforded by social media, we are seeing rage and aggression increasing, not just in politics, but towards workers in hospitality and retail, in schools and in hospitals, towards police, paramedics, and other officials, we are seeing a normalisation of the language of grievance and violence. ”.

The independent MP Allegra Spender said it was “wonderful” news that Haines was making good progress in her recovery.

Diungkapkan bahwa “she is a remarkable person and her strength and positivity after everything that has happened inspires me. ”.

#761. Russia's mega-rich are already imagining a future after Putin

📅 16 Nov 2026

Russia's mega-rich are already imagining a future after Putin

Tanggal: 16 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/c60733mxm0x0o?at_medium=RSS&at_campaign=rss

Russia's mega-rich are already imagining a future after Putin.

Hours after launching his full-scale invasion of Ukraine on 24 February 2022, Vladimir Putin gathered Russia's richest men in the Kremlin's cavernous Yekaterininsky Hall.

Sebagaimana diketahui, more than three dozen of them sat huddled along a wall, wearing face masks because of the covid pandemic. One Russian newspaper reporter described them as "pale and sleep-deprived". On entering, Putin sat down at the opposite side of the hall, creating a vast space between him and the businessmen. As usual, he was wearing no mask.

Using his typically coded language, he said he expected them to support the war.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, "i would like to call on you to show understanding of what is going on," he said, "and work together with the government to find the tools which would support production, the economy, jobs. ".

In the Kremlin-published video of the meeting, none of the invited billionaires said a word.

Sebagaimana diketahui, that silence has become a feature of the russian super-rich. In 2003, oil magnate Mikhail Khodorkovsky, Russia's richest man at the time, who was funding a number of opposition groups, accused Putin of presiding over rampant corruption. He spent the next 10 years behind bars, convicted of tax evasion, fraud and embezzlement - a warning to other would-be critics. Over the decades of Putin's rule, they have learnt that the price of piping up could be high. He denied the charges.

The silence of Russian businessmen at a Kremlin summit with Putin in 2022 perhaps demonstrated their fear of the president.

And even if any of the tycoons objected to the war, they have tended to keep their thoughts to themselves.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, but even in that silence, there are murmurings: some members of russia's once-mighty business elite seem to be imagining a russia after putin. They are wondering if, once the president has left office or died, the country might look more like it did in the 1990s, when the oligarchs enjoyed the fruits of power - or even if a healthier politics may take root.

The journalist Arkady Ostrovsky, a prominent Kremlin-watcher at The Economist newspaper who recently spent hours interviewing one of Russia's richest men, says he feels that a "historic, political shift is happening" in terms of how the ultra-rich view the future of the country.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the collapse of the soviet union in 1991 gave birth to a new, powerful force on the domestic scene: people who took advantage of the end of communism and became extraordinarily rich, and then wanted to control politicians for their own benefit. They were dubbed "the oligarchs", from Ancient Greek for the "few who rule". â¯ They had money, which back then meant power.

Berdasarkan laporan, this era of the "wild 1990s" was when the so-called "new russians" burst onto the scene. Huge state companies came up for grabs, and men with the right connections became millionaires - even billionaires - almost overnight. Corruption was rife, cronyism rampant, and contract killings frequent.

Sebagaimana diketahui, but almost immediately after putin was first elected as president in 2000, he subjugated the oligarchs. He had little interest in sharing power with anyone else. He could afford to stand up to the billionaires because Russia's economy was getting back on its feet, and the central government was getting stronger.

Some oligarchs developed a distinctive dress sense in the 1990s, as later satirised by this St Petersburg artist.

Bill Browder, a financier who used to be the biggest foreign investor in Russia, and was banned from the country in 2005 after campaigning against corruption, says the Russian tycoons cowered and wilted in front of Putin - for example at the Davos economic forum, in the pre-war years when they were still welcomed there.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, "i can remember seeing oligarchs walking around like they own the place, the most arrogant and self-confident individuals. And then Putin showed up, and it was just remarkable to see how these supposedly alpha-male-on-steroids individuals turned into absolutely subordinate, almost desperate schoolchildren," he tells the BBC.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, since the outbreak of war in 2022, the kremlin has kept russia's rich businessmen in line with a ruthless policy of carrot and stick. Critics of the war have seen their assets seized, while loyalists have been rewarded with lavish government war contracts: today there are more Russian billionaires than ever (155 in total, according to Forbes magazine). â¯Their collective wealth has reached a new high of nearly $700bn (Â£525bn).

Diungkapkan bahwa but even for those tycoons who have stayed loyal and been rewarded, all of that money doesn't seem to be making them happy. Some are growing restless.

Their billions do not go as far as they used to: domestically, they cannot buy much political influence.

Sebagaimana diketahui, "they have no cards, they have no game," exiled politician and analyst dmitry nekrasov says. "They're rich because they've got something to do with Putin, not the other way round. ".

And outside of Russia, they are ostracised because of the Western sanctions imposed on Russia after its full-scale invasion.

Berdasarkan laporan, "they're treated like low-level criminals. Their yachts can't park in all the best harbours in Europe. They can't fly their private jets. It must be very awful and humiliating for them," says Browder, the avowed Putin critic.

Diungkapkan bahwa and so, quietly, some of their minds are turning to what happens after putin leaves the scene. That's what I'm told by well-placed analysts, who are immersed in the world of these tycoons.

Diungkapkan bahwa there's no immediate prospect of the president's departure, and there's no reason to think he's in bad health. But Putin, who turned 74 last month, has served in the Kremlin for a quarter of a century; people in Moscow know that his exit will come one day. When asked by Reuters last year if he intends to serve until 2036, when his constitutional term technically ends, Putin replied: "Only God knows if we have enough health. ".

One prominent oligarch of the 1990s was Boris Berezovsky, who fell out with the Kremlin and lived his later years in the UK.

Sebagaimana diketahui, if putin resigned or died in office, the prime minister, mikhail mishustin, would take over. But Mishustin has not exhibited any presidential ambitions (that's probably a key reason he was appointed). That would create something of a power vacuum.

In that scenario, Russia-watchers I have spoken with envisage a few potential scenarios.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, some in the west, and no doubt within russia, hope that democracy might flourish in a post-putin russia, with government led by the people, rather than by a new cadre of oligarchs or a single autocrat. But this seems like the least likely path, analysts say. Key democratic institutions have been eroded or destroyed over Putin's rule. "Russia is so used to violence, it has grown unaccustomed to standard democratic procedures," says Alexandra Prokopenko, an exiled Russian journalist and analyst.

Berdasarkan laporan, another path is more autocracy. But Prokopenko thinks this wouldn't be another strongman dictatorship - at least not right away. A different figure could replace Putin and continue his culture of repression. These things take time, she says: at first, Putin's successor would be weaker than him, with fewer resources.

Diungkapkan bahwa and then there's the third option: tycoons re-assert their power and russia returns to something resembling a 1990s-style system of oligarchy. Dmitry Nekrasov, a former Kremlin adviser and opposition politician who now lives in exile, says under this scenario, the country would be governed by a handful of powerful elite clans in alliance with business interests.

Diungkapkan bahwa this last option, of course, is the one that many tycoons want. "They'd like to return to a time when they were listened to, when they were not stripped of assets and when they understood the rules of the game," says Prokopenko, who has spent a lot of time speaking to Russia's richest people.

Though their power has been seriously curtailed since the 1990s, it's still worth listening to the tycoons: given their immense wealth, it seems likely that sooner or later they will try to re-assert their political influence.

Sebagaimana diketahui, already, some are "trying to be friends with the right sort of security officials or ministers", says nekrasov, the exiled politician. But he says any further steps are "too dangerous to take".

Putin has kept tycoons in line with a ruthless policy of carrot and stick since Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, he says the behaviour of the tycoons in coming years will depend in part on their finances. Those who have lots of liquid cash will be more confident to "play political games" and jockey for position, preparing for a post-Putin country. But those whose wealth is dependent on state contracts or government goodwill will feel too afraid, in case they lose everything, he says.

Sebagaimana diketahui, prokopenko says there's already been a shift in how the businessmen talk about putin. They used to nickname him "Nachalnik" (which translates as "boss"), as well as "Perviy" ("first"), or by his initials "VV" - all nicknames that convey a degree of respect. Now they call him "Ded", with what Prokopenko calls "a pinch of contempt". "Ded" translates as "oldie" or "granddad" - a much less reverent name.

Some rich Russians are pining after a "return of politics into people's lives", she says, with less repression, more open speech, and healthier competition between parties and politicians.

Berdasarkan laporan, but at the moment, she says, they are too afraid to make that happen due to russia's stifling atmosphere. Prokopenko interviewed one tycoon who physically sat on his phone during the whole conversation, because he thought it would make digital eavesdropping more difficult for secret police. "I thought that it's an absolutely Stalinistic type of fear. It's absolutely irrational," she says.

An interesting clue for what tycoons might want from a post-Putin future came from Andrey Melnichenko, who is known as the world's fertiliser king and is currently Russia's eighth richest man.

Berdasarkan laporan, earlier this year, he surprised observers by giving an interview to the economist - a rare thing for a rich russian to do, especially to a publication from a country the kremlin considers unfriendly. They also published an essay written by him.

Sebagaimana diketahui, in parts of the interview, melnichenko repeated kremlin talking points. He said that Ukraine is a battlefield between Russia and the West, and he thinks the West ignored Russia's security concerns and threatens its sovereignty.

Sebagaimana diketahui, but then it got more interesting. Melnichenko did not call for Putin to go, but - and it's a big but - he argued for a change that would bring about an end to one-man rule in Russia. He said Russia needs to engage more with the world.

Berdasarkan laporan, prokopenko thinks the tycoon was trying to stir a public conversation. It was a "call on rich people like him to start talking", she says.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the journalist who interviewed him, arkady ostrovsky, tells me the pair had "tense and heated discussions" in "hotels and cafes, mostly drinking coffee, lots of coffee, sometimes smoking". He says the tycoon seemed to be "genuinely thinking" about his answers, rather than giving politician-style spin.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, nothing in russia is simple, and most observers think the interview probably happened with some form of approval - implicit or explicit - from the kremlin. We don't know why authorities would have been happy to authorise the unusual call for change; it's possible they were trying to show that some degree of pluralism still exists in the country.

Berdasarkan laporan, no tycoons came out to support him. Still, the journalist feels that Melnichenko was not speaking for himself alone, but also for his fellow businessmen.

Some tycoons feel ostracised because of Western sanctions, unable to fly private jets and visit Western resorts like Saint-Jean-Cap-Ferrat in southern France, which used to be popular with rich Russians.

Some of them are hoping that after Putin's departure, the country might become an "oligarchic republic", as journalist Ostrovsky puts it - something like how it looked in the 1990s, with the business elites in charge.

Based on his years of reporting on Russia, Ostrovsky says that many of the country's mega-rich currently feel a "sense of complete dead end, which this war has led Russia toâ¦ [an] absence of the future".

But even if the tycoons are thinking about the future, there's a slim prospect of them acting any time soon, it seems.

Sebagaimana diketahui, browder, the putin critic, says that although many of them are unhappy, they're unlikely to conspire against putin while he is still alive. And Putin is a very paranoid little man. "They understand that if they were to do anything that would challenge Putin, he would kill them. ".

Sebagaimana diketahui, mike calvey, an american financier who used to be a key investor in russia, agrees. "What can they do besides just go straight to the prison and lose their assets? It's easy for people who are sitting in London to say that, 'why don't you just all go stand up and go straight to prison?' That's really what would happen. ".

Diungkapkan bahwa russia's richest men used to be able to pull strings at the highest levels of power. Once Putin is gone, there is no doubt they will try to claw back their past influence. The question is: will remnants of the current regime let them?.

Spain and China are cosying up - to the anger of many in the EU.

Europe's youth is on the march - but does anything actually unite them?.

Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast.

Australia’s second-largest retailer has been targeted in a cyber-attack, though it is still too early to tell whether any of its data has been stolen or compromised.

Coles revealed the threat on Monday morning, saying it was investigating with support from the Australian Cyber Security Centre and global security experts.

“Coles Group Limited is currently investigating a cyber security incident,” the company said in a statement to the stock exchange.

“We have not identified any evidence that customer, team or supplier data has been compromised or removed from Coles’ systems.

Diungkapkan bahwa “operations continue and customers are able to shop as normal with coles in stores and online. ”.

Coles apologised to its customers for any concerns they might have at “a time of increasing cyber incidents in Australia and around the world”.

“We have security measures in place to protect customer and supplier accounts and are continuing to closely monitor our system,” it said.

Berdasarkan laporan, “we recommend you regularly update your password with a strong, unique password for your account and not reuse the same password across multiple services. ”.

Coles also warned customers to be cautious if they received unexpected emails or SMS messages purporting to be from the retailer, and not to click any links.

Sebagaimana diketahui, in a separate and unrelated incident, woolworths said it was aware of reports from customers who purchased compromised e-gift cards. The ABC first reported on Monday some customers had lost hundreds of dollars after buying the company’s Everyday WISH gift cards through its rewards website or app, only to find the sums loaded on to them had been spent by someone else.

Some customers told the national broadcaster they had lost up to $500, with transactions showing up at stores in different states to where they purchased the cards.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, “we are aware of reports of an issue affecting a number of customer e-gift cards and are looking into the matter as a priority,” a woolworths spokesperson said in a statement. We encourage any customer who notices a transaction they don’t recognise to contact our Gift Card Support team. “We recognise the concern this has caused affected customers and we apologise to customers impacted. ”.

The company says it is working through all reported issues and will look into replacing affected e-gift cards.

Tanggal: 16 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/cry49plv8v3go?at_medium=RSS&at_campaign=rss

SpaceX boss Elon Musk and Nvidia's former chief executive Jensen Huang.

Allies of Jensen Huang are trying to rally support for the former Nvidia boss to get his job back after resigning last week over a scandal involving extramarital affairs, one involving an alleged Chinese spy.

SpaceX boss Elon Musk and Tim Sweeney, chief executive of Fortnite-maker Epic Games, are among those backing a campaign to get the AI chip giant's board to "Bring Jensen Back".

Huang resigned as chief executive of Nvidia after the emergence of two affairs, one of whom was with a woman suspected of spying for China and another allegedly with one of his employees.

It has created a crisis for one of the world's most valuable firms which is a key part of the AI industry and its huge expansion.

An open letter calling for Nvidia's board to give Huang his job back while an internal probe is conducted has received more than 175,000 signatures, including Musk and Sweeney, according to a website named "Stand with Jensen".

The campaign group said it is made up of current and former Nvidia employees, partners, shareholders and supporters.

"We write with gratitude for Jensen Huang and with a clear demand to the board: bring Jensen back while an independent investigation establishes the facts, unless and until you can provide compelling evidence that his removal is in NVIDIA's best interests," the letter said.

Allies of the ex-Nvidia boss wrote they were "concerned that Jensen was removed without meaningful due process".

Huang had been expected to weather the storm following the revelation of an affair involving Alice Huang, alleged to be a Chinese spy.

However, he resigned last Thursday after a second extra-marital relationship emerged, this time allegedly with an executive at Nvidia who reported to him.

Diungkapkan bahwa the scandal-hit tech boss is now discussing a possible return to nvidia with confidants, according to the financial times. , external.

The newspaper quoted one ally saying that a "war room" of Silicon Valley executives was being convened to lobby for the former Nvidia boss's reinstatement.

A representative for Jensen Huang declined to comment on the report.

The so-called war room also wants to get support for Huang from the White House.

While President Donald Trump recently spoke in glowing terms about Huang, the scandal has created tensions between the US Treasury and Commerce departments over shipments of high-end Nvidia chips to Alice Huang's former firm, Megaspeed.

It has raised questions about the possibility that the chips may have ended up in China despite US export restrictions.

The former Nvidia boss has agreed to testify in Congress, including before the House Select Committee on China.

The BBC understands that the likelihood of Huang being reinstated is low while the Nvidia's internal investigations are ongoing.

The FBI is also investigating the affair between the former Nvidia boss and Alice Huang, according to Trump.

Musk claimed that "critical deals" involving Nvidia's technology would be lost following Huang's resignation.

"Jensen drove supply chain brilliantly at Nvidia but many of those deals were a handshake with Jensen, not a written contract.

Diungkapkan bahwa "without jensen, at least some of those critical deals will be lost," he posted on x. , external.

Sebagaimana diketahui, he later added: "if jensen gave me his word about compute delivery or i asked for components to be accelerated, he always came through. ".

Berdasarkan laporan, if huang was reinstated, it would face scrutiny from washington. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent has called for Nvidia to hire its next chief executive from outside the company.

Shareholders in Nvidia also want Huang back at Nvidia's helm.

In an open letter to the board, Brad Gerstner, founder of Altimeter Capital and Atreides Management boss Gavin Baker called for management to leave "all options on the table, including the potential return of Jensen Huang".

Lord Sarfraz, a member of the UK's House of Lords, has also written to Nvidia's new chair, Harvey Jones, urging the firm's directors to give "serious consideration" to Huang's return following the investigation.

For the moment, Nvidia's chief financial officer Colette Kress is leading the firm and will present the company's results on Tuesday.

Suspected China spy linked to Nvidia's ex-boss left in 2025, Megaspeed says.
