#844. Revealed: Israel uploaded millions of photos to Amazon’s facial recognition platform to track Palestinians

📅 16 Nov 2026

Revealed: Israel uploaded millions of photos to Amazon’s facial recognition platform to track Palestinians

Tanggal: 16 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/nov/16/israel-amazon-facial-recognition-palestinians

Upload came as the Israeli military was increasing its reliance on Amazon’s cloud platform to meet the technological demands of its bombardment of Gaza.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the israeli military uploaded 3. 5m photos to Amazon’s cloud platform in order to use the US company’s facial recognition technology to analyse images of Palestinians, the Guardian can reveal.

Leaked documents show the expansive catalogue of images was moved into Amazon’s cloud in the early months of Israel’s devastating aerial bombardment and ground offensive in Gaza.

The images were uploaded by a department of the Israeli military that holds a vast collection of photos covering the Palestinian populations in Gaza and the West Bank.

The department informed Amazon of the decision to upload the images in early 2024 so it could use Rekognition, the company’s AI-powered image analysis platform for a facial recognition project.

The documents obtained by the Guardian form part of an investigation into the Israeli military’s reliance on the technology and infrastructure of Amazon’s cloud computing business to monitor Palestinians.

According to the files and interviews with military sources, Israel has in recent years migrated huge volumes of data – including sensitive intelligence material and information about Palestinians living under occupation – into Amazon’s datacentres.

The large set of images was moved into an Amazon datacentre near Tel Aviv by a department commonly known as Rolling Stone, which sits within a military software unit.

The department takes its name from a system widely used by the Israeli military that serves as a central repository of information about Palestinians living in Gaza and the West Bank.

At the time, the department was exploring using facial recognition technologies to analyse the extensive catalogues of images of Palestinians it holds, several sources with knowledge of its work said.

After Israel’s ground invasion of Gaza in October 2023, its military routinely collected images of Palestinians as they passed through checkpoints, often after they had been forcibly displaced by the bombing campaign.

Sebagaimana diketahui, it’s not clear whether the 3. 5m images uploaded to Amazon’s Rekognition were captured at these checkpoints, which effectively served as pop-up surveillance posts.

However, a military source familiar with facial recognition efforts at the checkpoints said Amazon’s cloud infrastructure was used due to the “very large scale” of images collected at the sites.

Diungkapkan bahwa israel has long used facial recognition technology, particularly in its occupation of the west bank. Face scanning is routine at checkpoints, while Israeli soldiers use custom-built smartphone apps to collect images of people living in the Palestinian territory.

Sebagaimana diketahui, in the early stages of its campaign in gaza, israel used rekognition to identify hostages captured by militants in the hamas-led attack on southern israel on 7 october 2023. The military also deployed facial recognition technology to identify people it suspected were militants.

The New York Times has previously reported how the military experimented with commercially available technology in Gaza to detect faces in crowds and in drone footage, at times wrongly flagging civilians as militants.

The new documents reveal the Israeli military’s use of Amazon technology, both for experiments with facial recognition and for a more far-reaching project to move its data on to the servers of the computing arm of the conglomerate founded by billionaire Jeff Bezos.

They also shed light on what the Israeli military is moving into the cloud and how it uses Amazon Web Services (AWS) infrastructure to support the collection and processing of Palestinians’ personal data, typically gathered indiscriminately, through intrusive means and without their consent.

The files suggest the ties between AWS and the Israeli military deepened during a period in which Israel has been accused of committing grave crimes in Gaza, including genocide – a charge denied by Israel, but supported by a UN commission of inquiry, Israeli human rights groups and genocide experts.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, a spokesperson for aws said it had no “visibility” into workloads held by its customers in its cloud. They added: “We respect the privacy of our customers, and we do not discuss our relationship without their consent. ”.

In early 2024, a small group of Israeli soldiers worked from AWS’s offices in Tel Aviv, located on the 28th floor of one of Israel’s tallest skyscrapers.

The soldiers were exploring ways to use the company’s cloud infrastructure to more effectively operate a facial recognition programme underway in Gaza, several military sources said.

Berdasarkan laporan, it’s not clear whether their work was made operational or if it related to the 3. 5m images uploaded to Rekognition. The presence of the group at AWS’s offices, however, underscores the close relationship between the Israeli military and the cloud provider.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, an aws spokesperson said its customers “regularly visit our offices for briefings and meetings”. They added: “Any suggestion that these visits are anything other than routine customer engagement is wrong and unsubstantiated. ”.

Diungkapkan bahwa the foundation of israel’s relationship with amazon is a sweeping 2021 contract known as project nimbus. Under the multibillion dollar deal, AWS and Google provide cloud services to a wide range of government and military clients.

The Guardian revealed last year that the Nimbus contract contains unusual terms that prohibit the US companies from restricting or suspending Israeli government and military use of their cloud services, even if Israel breaches their terms of service.

This would prevent the kind of unilateral action taken by Microsoft last year when it disabled the Israeli military’s access to technology used to operate a mass surveillance system uncovered by the Guardian and +972 Magazine.

Berdasarkan laporan, as part of the nimbus deal, aws opened new datacentres in israel in early 2023, allowing the israeli government and military clients to migrate data from their own servers, according to documents. A large proportion of data was also moved from AWS datacentres in Ireland.

A central component of the Nimbus contract, files show, was an obligation on AWS to provide the Israeli military with access to a segregated area within its Tel Aviv datacentres, fortified with enhanced digital and physical security measures.

This isolated area within the AWS cloud – used to store sensitive material relating to military operations and intelligence collection – was described by the company and its client as a “walled garden”.

The Israeli military’s reliance on AWS reflects its embrace in recent years of leading US tech companies to meet the technological demands of war with rapidly scalable storage, computing power and AI-driven services.

The role of AI in Israel’s offensive in Gaza has come under fresh scrutiny particularly after the release of NAZA, a Guardian-produced documentary about the remote surveillance and killing of Palestinian civilians.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the rolling stone department is among aws’s most significant israeli military clients, documents suggest. Its use of Rekognition in early 2024 to analyse 3. 5m images came after it had expanded its use of AWS products and services to store and analyse its data.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, files show the department migrated significant volumes of the data it holds into the so-called “walled garden” in aws’s cloud throughout 2023. A military source involved in this effort said it had planned to move all of its databases from the military servers into AWS’s cloud.

Diungkapkan bahwa the source, who spoke on the condition of anonymity, said: “the plan [at rolling stone] was to migrate pictures, videos, all the confidential intelligence information – everything. ”.

A spokesperson for the Israel Defence Forces (IDF) said it “does not intend to comment on engagements or services related to operational needs”.

The Rolling Stone department oversees several expansive databases that collate data on Palestinians, including the system from which the branch takes its name.

Used by the military for decades, the Rolling Stone system is constantly updated and includes data such as basic personal and family details, property holdings, and information on checkpoint crossings, work permits, and criminal activity.

A soldier who provided testimony to Breaking the Silence, an Israeli NGO, in 2016 described Rolling Stone as “a computerised system where all the information relevant to the control of the Palestinian civilian population is centralised”.

As a result of Israel’s control of the population registries covering Gaza and the West Bank, the Rolling Stone department has amassed millions of Palestinians’ photographs taken for the identity cards issued to every resident when they turn 16 years old.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, sources familiar with its work said the images were routinely used for facial recognition programmes. These include Blue Wolf, a smartphone app Israeli soldiers use in the West Bank to scan Palestinians’ faces and access information about them, including whether they’ve been flagged as suspects for arrest.

#845. South Korea to Examine How K-Pop Industry Treats Underage Performers

South Korea to Examine How K-Pop Industry Treats Underage Performers

Tanggal: 16 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.nytimes.com/2026/11/16/world/asia/kpop-underage-idols-survey.html

The announcement came after a New York Times investigation about the restrictive contracts of the group NewJeans, signed when its members were 14 to 17.

South Korea’s government is planning to study how the K-pop industry treats underage performers, who are central to the industry, and to re-examine the standard template for contracts it released nearly two decades ago.

Berdasarkan laporan, the ministry of culture, sports and tourism will start an industrywide survey sometime next year, a ministry official said in a telephone interview on monday. The government already studies the K-pop industry, checking whether record companies follow its standard contract and how much money is invested in training young stars. The new effort will focus specifically on how underage artists are treated, but its methodology, scope and exact timeline have not been decided on.

Berdasarkan laporan, the announcement came just over a week after the new york times published an investigation into the record contracts signed by the members of newjeans, one of k-pop’s biggest girl groups, when they were ages 14 to 17. The investigation found that the contracts removed language included in the government template that guarantees rights for minors, such as the rights to education and sleep.

Sebagaimana diketahui, it was a rare look into the business of k-pop, which has long been dogged by allegations of exploitation. Record companies recruit children who are aspiring stars, put them through years of intensive training and then often bill them for those costs. Several stars have died by suicide.

Sebagaimana diketahui, two years ago, newjeans tried to quit their label in a dispute that turned into one of k-pop’s most public fights, with the members saying they had been mistreated. A court later held them to the contracts they had signed, which run until 2029.

The Seoul Broadcasting System reported the ministry’s plan earlier.

Diungkapkan bahwa in 2009, after a boy band sued its label over restrictive work agreements, the authorities created a standard contract. It outlined protections such as capping agreements at seven years, taking into consideration an artist’s physical and mental well-being and transferring trademark rights to the artist after the terms end.

Diungkapkan bahwa the template has been amended several times over the years but still largely remains legally nonbinding. Record companies often alter clauses and add their own conditions. Some do not use the template at all, a government survey found.

Jin Yu Young is a reporter for The Times, based in Seoul, covering South Korea and international breaking news.

Sarah Hurtes is a Times reporter working on international investigations from Brussels.

#846. ‘I saw a picture of a two-year-old girl buried in mud. I knew we had to do something’ – This is climate breakdown

Sebagaimana diketahui, when the floods hit pakistan he went out to help. Then the water reached his own family. This is Imran Lodhi’s story.

Please enable Javascript to fully experience this interactive article.

Disaster: Pakistan intense monsoon rainfall.

Diungkapkan bahwa imran lodhi is a university lecturer with a doctorate in climate change and sustainable development. The 41-year-old was living in Dera Ghazi Khan, a city in south-western Punjab, when floods devastated provinces across Pakistan. Climate change made the monsoon rainfall that caused the floods more intense.

Sebagaimana diketahui, in 2022, i was living in an area that had less risk of flooding. It was probably her last breath. I tried to avoid flood news on social media until I saw a picture of a two-year-old girl who was buried in mud. She died after that. I had a small child and my PhD thesis was just a few weeks away. That was the turning point.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, i immediately called my friends, six to seven people, in a mosque. ” Initially, it was food. I talked to them: “We don’t know what to do, but at least we can start from somewhere. We hired some commercial cooks.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, we planned to work only in villages close to our city. A lot of people were taking refuge in nearby high places, high enough that the water did not reach them. On the first day we went with some food to the nearest village.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, when the rain is over, the sun comes out. There was no camp. It was like being naked. I could see trolleys, tractors, vehicles and homes all drowned in the flood. It felt like it opened a scar. Usually, it’s a good sign. The pain that was hiding somehow had become open. But, in those areas, it didn’t feel good. There was nothing from the government, nothing from any development sector. People were just living under open skies.

Berdasarkan laporan, men felt that their women being in an open place was a kind of emotional damage for them. It was not normal for most of the people here. Their hair was full of dust and dry mud. Their clothes had a heavy layer of dry mud; no shoes on their feet. They came out for their work, the agriculture work, but not sitting that openly among the public. Many women never came out. Mothers were not breastfeeding. Babies crying for milk, and the milk was not there. Mothers trying to soothe them with fake sounds.

Berdasarkan laporan, the cows did not have feed and were not giving milk. Many of the animals were lost, their bodies wide open, decomposed. Then the water, which stayed there for a week, started to smell very bad. There was no good smell.

Berdasarkan laporan, we prepared food in the morning. We generally finished distributing food around 8pm. One night it was 11pm and we thought some people might not have food. Then we prepared food at lunchtime. So we just cooked some food late at night and went to every camp.

Berdasarkan laporan, one old woman started to laugh. ’ And suddenly you appeared. I was surprised. I asked her: “It’s OK, we have food, but why are you laughing?” And she said: “I was just complaining, ‘Lord, that you left me with an empty stomach today. ”.

Sebagaimana diketahui, it was a very strange experience for her. People, when they are in tough conditions, are attached to their beliefs. For us also. And, when things like that come up, they establish a spiritual connection with the people who are helping out.

Sebagaimana diketahui, we posted on social media. Money poured in and we kept expanding the team. A lot of people contacted us who were from other parts of Pakistan. We tried to mobilise. From two or three villages, we started to cover the entire district, and then almost the entire region.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the government protocols were to not go into certain areas that looked dangerous or were not safe for a boat. There was no land in one village. Families were trapped, many, many kilometres into the water. They somehow made a swing for the kids. The whole family was in the tree. Small wooden cupboards were hung on trees so stuff could be saved from the water. The elders were lying on the branches. The immediate shelter was a big tree near them. They spent days in those trees.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, a few villages were completely destroyed. She was so attached to that home that she felt like there was no life after it. Not a single home was standing. She had a small cupboard in which she kept some small things to sell, for her independence. One old woman who was living with her married kids was not ready to leave that rubble. Everything was in shock, even the trees. She was so concerned about that small cupboard. When I reached there, that cupboard was all broken.

Diungkapkan bahwa one day i had a fever and my wife stopped me: “don’t go out – you are not well enough to help other people. My family was there. There was water coming toward the city. Within hours, the water would be in the city. When we reached there, I got news that the city we were living in – which I thought was safe – suddenly was a source of threat. ” But I still went out to a village to help people. And I was almost 100km away.

Sebagaimana diketahui, so i rushed back. I gave them some suggestions: how they could save themselves and evacuate. I called my wife and I asked them to stay vigilant and look out for water in the city. But the road toward the city was cut off by the flood. There was no way I could go back to my family. That was a very, very tough call.

Diungkapkan bahwa eventually, the city was saved. Next day, we took a boat to get past the road that was cut off. Sitting in that boat, I was thinking about my family. Once I reached the other side, I called some people to take me home.

Diungkapkan bahwa when i reached home, i had a very strong fever and i spent that day at home. I tried to behave normally, but everybody knew I was not feeling well. I took one day off from community work.

Berdasarkan laporan, the next day i wanted to stop. But the problem was, I was in the middle of that network. If I stop, this whole process will stop. This whole network of relief work will stop.

Berdasarkan laporan, the next day, even with a high fever, i left for the field because i didn’t want that to stop. When I grew up, the community fabric was very strong. It was common practice that whenever people got sick, got in an accident, hospitalised, people would visit the person and share some money.

This was the kind of culture I observed happening around me.

Berdasarkan laporan, i went back to those areas where the flood came. I can smell that sweet in those villages. I see shops open. I felt good watching people working again. There was still some water standing so there were remains of that devastation. I see farmers, labourers. But there’s a very common sweet in that area we call jalebi. It looked like life was coming back.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, there was an annual poetry event happening three months after the flood. Saraiki culture is very rich, one of the oldest. I was consulted by one of my friends who is the organiser of that event. Should we suspend this year’s events or not?.

Berdasarkan laporan, i said you should never suspend the event. Let people believe the normalisation, let people believe in the spirit of survival. They organised the poetry event.

When Andy Burnham told the Labour conference that he wanted to start a debate on a new relationship with the EU, because Brexit had done more harm than good, he raised the possibility that this could lead to Labour proposing to rejoin at some point after the next election.

But some ministers and Labour MPs are deeply unhappy about that prospect, believing that there would have to be a referendum and that this would be deeply divisive, and there are some signs that Burnham (who is on record as saying he would like the UK to rejoin in his lifetime) is starting to scale back his ambitions.

Berdasarkan laporan, in his speech to the welsh labour conference on saturday, burnham repeated the argument he made in september about brexit having done more harm than good. But he focused on making Brexit better, not overturning it. At one point in the speech he said:.

Berdasarkan laporan, double quotation marki don’t believe brexit and the deal that they got has been good enough for britain. I think we’ve lost more than we’ve gained over the last 10 years.

double quotation markPeople’s jobs depend on working together and collaborating.

Berdasarkan laporan, the reference to “respecting the referendum result” could have just meant not rejoining before the next election. But given that this was a manifesto red line, and that he had already spoken about respecting that, he seemed to imply something more.

Sebagaimana diketahui, and today burnham has announced three tests for his brexit reset. (See 9. 15am. ) Although these are only tests for the deal he is announcing on Friday, not for the Brexit policy he will announce at the next election, the focus on improving the Brexit deal and bringing it “closer to what people thought they were voting for in 2016” might be a sign of where his thinking is heading.

Sebagaimana diketahui, in interviews this morning, ed miliband, the foreign secretary, also focused on the government wanting to make brexit work better for the economy. He told Sky News:.

Sebagaimana diketahui, double quotation marklook, here’s my starting point. My constituents, people across the country, voted for a range of reasons for Brexit, but one of them was one of the biggest, certainly for my constituents, was to make our economy better, positive economic change. The economy has got worse. We haven’t had that. And nobody really thinks this Brexit deal is a good deal.

Berdasarkan laporan, on itv’s good morning britain, ed balls did not ask miliband about russell brand but he did ask him repeatedly if he wanted the uk to rejoin the eu. Berdasarkan laporan, the tories have pledged to halt “screen-based” exams and cut coursework in a bid to limit the use of ai by schoolchildren if the party returns to power, the press association reports. PA says:.

double quotation markNew guidelines for teachers would seek to ensure that laptops and tablets are not the default in classrooms, the party said.

Shadow education secretary Laura Trott said Britain had “sleepwalked into a situation where nearly a million children spend almost every lesson” on a device despite health professionals warning of the dangers of excessive screen time.

Sebagaimana diketahui, double quotation marki obey collective responsibility. Miatta Fahnbulleh [the energy secretary] will make the decision on this. So she looks at all the evidence, and then reaches a conclusion. I know it’s a quasi-judicial decision. I’m not going to second-guess [her].

Sebagaimana diketahui, good morning. There are two issues that will dominate the political news this week – the EU reset, and the Alan Milburn report on youth unemployment – and this morning there are new lines on both of these issues.

Diungkapkan bahwa andy burnham has set out “three tests” for the deal that he is due to agree with the eu at a summit on friday. double quotation markAhead of this week’s UK-EU Summit, the prime minister will set out three tests for any agreement:.

-Second, it must improve the Brexit deal and bring it closer to what people thought they were voting for in 2016, rather than the hard Brexit that no one ever seriously argued for in the referendum.

-Third, it must pass the Makerfield test by delivering real, tangible improvements in people’s everyday lives, particularly in communities that have felt neglected for too long.

double quotation markLet me first say, Russell Brand’s crimes are heinous and appalling, and all of my sympathies are with the victims of Russell Brand, who have shown incredible bravery.

double quotation markLet me just say one thing, because I do want to one thing you said.

Russell Brand was going around telling people not to vote in the general election.

Berdasarkan laporan, i was not endorsing russell brand. I was taking him on and saying he was completely wrong in saying that people shouldn’t vote, that democracy didn’t matter and all those things. But as I say, I deeply regret doing that interview.

#851. Mushroom lovers in UK told to avoid grow kits owing to invasive species risk

Mushroom lovers in UK told to avoid grow kits owing to invasive species risk

Tanggal: 16 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.theguardian.com/environment/2026/nov/16/mushroom-lovers-uk-told-to-avoid-grow-kits-invasive-species-golden-oyster

Popular edible golden oyster classed as high-risk invasive species because of negative impact on woodlands.

They have been viewed for years as the ideal Christmas gift for the culinary-minded, but experts have now warned that grow-your-own mushroom kits should be blacklisted from a spot under the tree.

An international group of mycologists, including experts from the Royal Horticultural Society, have said many of these kits, which allow people to easily grow mushrooms at home as a delicious addition to stir-fries and other dishes, contain invasive species.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the edible golden oyster mushroom, a favourite option, has been found growing in uk forests at breakneck speed. It has now been officially classed as a high-risk invasive species because of its negative impact on woodlands.

Scientists have said the golden oyster has established itself in the wild in at least two UK forests, with the most likely pathway of introduction being escape or release from grow kits.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, native to east asia, the mushroom species has been found to be invasive on other continents as it has wind-dispersed spores that can travel thousands of miles, making it impossible to stop its spread. It arrived in the US in 2012 and has spread across 25 states and approximately 772,200 sq miles (2m sq km). Because it establishes itself so successfully, the species has been shown to as much as halve the beneficial wood-inhabiting native fungi.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, despite its invasive nature, it is still legal to sell the golden oyster commercially, with grow kits widely available online and through large retailers. The RHS no longer exhibits the golden oyster at events, nor does it sell the mushroom in its shops, instead spotlighting native species that can be grown at home including lion’s mane.

Diungkapkan bahwa dr jassy drakulic, a senior plant pathologist at the rhs, said: “the growing public interest in fungi is something to celebrate, but as they become more widely grown and sold, we must also recognise the biosecurity risks that can accompany them. The escape of the golden oyster mushroom in the UK highlights a significant gap in how invasive fungi are managed.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, “fungi are difficult to track in the wild, living mostly unseen until they fruit, so we need stronger policies to prevent introducing species that can permanently alter native ecosystems. Developing a dedicated strategy for invasive fungi is essential if we are to safeguard biodiversity for the future. ”.

Sebagaimana diketahui, invasive species are one of the world’s leading causes of biodiversity loss. A famous example in Britain is the grey squirrel. It was imported from the US in the 1800s and spread a fatal disease known as squirrelpox to the native red squirrels. As a result, red squirrels have become extinct in many parts of Britain.

Diungkapkan bahwa aishwarya veerabahu, a mycologist at the university of wisconsin-madison in the us, said: “every golden oyster mushroom kit sold gives the golden oyster a chance to establish in nature and spread from there. Mushroom kits helped the golden oyster rapidly spread across the US and Canada; in less than a decade, it colonised vast areas of North America, and its full ecological impacts are still unfolding.

Sebagaimana diketahui, “fungi are the foundation of forests and we’re beginning to understand how invasive species are impacting local biodiversity and disrupting their complex relationships. Golden oysters haven’t spread too far in the UK yet, so there’s a fighting chance of preventing it from becoming invasive. We’re asking people to hold off on buying mushroom kits to protect the UK’s fungal biodiversity and favourite native edibles. ”.

The Ministry of Justice has launched an investigation into whether Russell Brand has broken prison rules after the jailed comedian shared a message claiming he was not guilty of sexual offences just days after his conviction.

Sebagaimana diketahui, brand’s wife, laura brand, read a message from her rapist husband in a video uploaded to their youtube channel in which he claimed: “i am not guilty of the offences i have been jailed for. ”.

It is understood a prisoner will be deemed to have broken the rules if they provide comments to a family member they know will be published.

Any inquiry could also examine whether the current rules need to be updated to stop comments from prisoners being broadcast via profit-making YouTube channels.

Sebagaimana diketahui, asked about the comments, the prime minister’s official spokesperson said: “this is clearly appalling and is being urgently investigated. We expect action to be taken if he is found to have broken the rules.

“Prisoners are strictly banned from making statements that cause distress to victims and speaking to the media is only permitted in exceptional circumstances.

Diungkapkan bahwa “prisoners cannot get around these rules by having someone else publish their comments … this is being urgently investigated. We expect action to be taken if the rules have been broken. ”.

Brand, 51, is serving a 10-and-a-half-year prison term after he was convicted of one count of rape and three sexual assaults at Southwark crown court on 5 November.

In his message, Brand said he had been moved from the category B Wandsworth prison in south-west London to the lower category C HMP Littlehey in Cambridgeshire – a prison for men convicted of sexual offences.

Berdasarkan laporan, “i am incarcerated in hmp littlehey, little as in small, and hey as in hey, i’m in the biggest sex offenders’ prison in europe. The good news is that I have already seen that the staff here are strong, they are kind, and they are dedicated. And as for my fellow prisoners, I now know that I am in no position to judge anyone.

Diungkapkan bahwa “i don’t know which other men here are not guilty, and the ones that are, they are people that christ died to save, like you and me, let us all love, pray for, and forgive one another as god forgave us. ”.

Berdasarkan laporan, prisoners are allowed to protest their innocence, meaning that no criminal offence has been committed in the release of the podcast. They are not, however, allowed to make statements from jail that cause distress to victims, and heavy restrictions apply to speaking to the media.

Sebagaimana diketahui, according to official guidance on prisoner access to the media, a prison governor must decide whether to permit it, and only if “serious distress to victims of the prisoner and/or outrage to public sensibilities is not likely to result from the broadcast. This is likely to occur if, for example, the prisoner’s crimes or conduct are recent, notorious or horrific”.

Mayor axes strategic response group that cracked down on protesters and announces new community safety division.

Zohran Mamdani, New York City’s mayor, announced Monday that he was disbanding a controversial city police unit that has faced criticism over the years from civil rights groups who have accused the unit of using excessive force and unduly aggressive tactics against protesters.

Berdasarkan laporan, in a video released monday morning, mamdani said the move stemmed from a campaign pledge he made to disband the new york city police department’s strategic response group (srg). “Today, we are keeping that promise,” Mamdani said in the video.

An accompanying joint statement from Mamdani and NYPD commissioner Jessica Tisch said the overhaul would “transform how the city prepares for and responds to protests, placing communication, de-escalation and civilian coordination at the center of our approach, while protecting New Yorkers’ constitutional right to protest”.

Along with eliminating the SRG, which was founded in 2015 ostensibly to focus on counter-terrorism, Mamdani and Tisch’s statement also said that the city planned to establish a “first-of-its-kind, civilian-led Community Dialogue and De-escalation Division (CDDD)” within the mayor’s office of community safety.

That division will not have weapons or arrest powers, unlike the SRG, according to the announcement.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the city will also establish what they described as a “specialized dialogue team” that will be known as the “first amendment support team” (fast) within the nypd’s community affairs bureau, mamdani and tisch’s statement said. The creation of Fast is meant to “improve the NYPD’s protest response,” and it will consist of 30 uniformed officers trained in communication and de-escalation, the mayor and police commissioner said.

Additionally, their statement said, the NYPD will create a new patrol support division (PSD) within its patrol services bureau.

Plans call for the unit to be staffed with vetted officers who will primarily perform patrol-related duties and receive specialized crowd management training to support responses to demonstrations.

Diungkapkan bahwa the reforms also introduce “significant new restrictions on the tactics and weapons” officers can use during protests and demonstrations – banning irritant gas, kettling and long guns. Responding officers will no longer be allowed to deploy pepper spray “as a crowd-management tool” – and “long-range acoustic devices” meant to affect protesters’ hearing “will be limited to 90 decibels,” Mamdani and Tisch said in their statement.

Under the new structure, the mayor said, the SRG’s counter-terrorism functions – “including heavy weapons deployments at critical infrastructure” – will be consolidated within the NYPD’s intelligence and counter-terrorism bureau.

The statement said that helped ensure a complete separation between the city’s counter-terrorism operations and protests protected by the rights to free speech and assembly guaranteed by the US constitution’s first amendment.

Tisch said that the new structure was “designed to consolidate our counterterrorism capabilities, provide greater support to our patrol officers and ensure we continue to respond to protests consistent with public safety and the first amendment”.

“These changes will make us a stronger, more effective department” she said.

The administration said that the SRG-related reforms come at “no additional cost and without increasing or reducing NYPD headcount”.

While civil rights groups hailed Monday’s announcement, the New York Police Benevolent Association’s president, Patrick Hendry, criticized it in a statement on social media.

Sebagaimana diketahui, “today is not a good day for new yorkers who just want a safe and orderly city,” said the statement from hendry, whose organization is a labor union representing more than 21,000 active nypd officers. “Mayor Mamdani is showing his true colors: he’s willing to put your safety and police officers’ safety at risk to appease his radical base.

Diungkapkan bahwa “so the next time your life is disrupted by demonstrators who are blocking bridges and roadways or causing chaos on our streets, remember: mayor mamdani is on their side, not yours. ”.

Mamdani in January had reiterated promises to disband the SRG after it arrested dozens of demonstrators occupying a hotel lobby in protests opposing Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE), the federal agency at the forefront of the mass deportation campaign which Donald Trump has pursued throughout his second presidency.

Furthermore, after 2020 protests over a Minneapolis police officer’s murder of George Floyd, New York City’s department of investigation recommended that the NYPD “reevaluate the central role” of the SRG “in response to large protests given their orientation to handle counterterrorism, riots, and other serious threats, and better calibrate their use to circumstances that require such specialized force”.

#861. Passing bill to speed up gas projects and datacenters would be ‘serious mistake’, Al Gore says

Tanggal: 16 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026/nov/16/al-gore-baaja-cop-31-climate

Former vice-president at Cop31 urges lawmakers to rethink contentious bipartisan Baaja bill advanced by the US Senate.

It would be a “serious mistake” to pass a contentious bipartisan bill to speed up energy projects and datacenters that has divided Democrats and environmentalists, Al Gore said.

The legislation, known as the Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act (Baaja), will make it easier to build large infrastructure projects in the US, from oil and gas pipelines and datacenters to crucial clean energy components such as solar and wind power and transmission lines, scaling back environmental protections and legal challenges in order to do so.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the permitting bill, devised by a group of republicans and democrats, passed a procedural vote in the us senate last week, but has split democrats and green groups over whether its trade-offs are worth supporting. Gore, the former US vice-president, said he is opposed to the bill and urged a rethink.

“I think it would be a serious mistake, particularly in the wake of the astonishing election results last week,” Gore, referencing Democrats’ sweeping midterm wins, said at the Cop31 climate summit in Antalya, Turkey.

Diungkapkan bahwa “the fact that president trump endorsed it enthusiastically is a clue, the fact that the american petroleum institute is giving out free tacos in washington to support it is also a clue. I hope they reconsider because I think it would be a very, very serious mistake. ”.

Trump, who has repeatedly attempted to halt clean energy projects in the US, said last week wind turbines are a “major loser” and that he will prevent any more being built, even as the bill to sweep away blockages to clean energy is being considered.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, this animosity, and the us president’s complicated relationship with federal laws, means baaja would end up aiding the fossil fuel industry, gore claimed. “Trump will implement any legislation given to him in a way that continues to redeem his unethical pledge to the fossil fuel industry during his campaign,” he said, referencing Trump’s promise to provide help to oil and gas executives in return for donations prior to the 2024 election.

Diungkapkan bahwa “the president of the united states is in charge of implementing whatever legislation is passed and he doesn’t play by the rules, he doesn’t respect the law and it’s not a mystery how he would try to implement this legislation,” gore said. “It would lock in a lot of new pipelines and fossil fuel facilities. And we will have a chance with the new Congress and the new balance of power in the US government to do a much better job. ”.

But while Democrats will be able to craft a far more renewables-friendly permitting bill when they gain control of Congress in January, proponents of Baaja point out that support from Trump and Republicans will likely wither, meaning there will be no legislation at all to help stop wind and solar projects being bogged down in lengthy reviews, with new generation struggling to bring clean electricity to Americans due to a lack of transmission lines across the country.

A final Senate vote is expected this week and if that passes it would move to the House.

Sheldon Whitehouse, a Democratic senator and longtime climate advocate who helped craft the bill, said he was working to improve the legislation but rejected Gore’s criticism.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, “mr gore neither spoke to senator (martin) heinrich or me or our teams before he reached that conclusion,” whitehouse, who is also at cop31, said. Whitehouse said he was working on “a variety of amendments to see what can be done to shore up potential holes in the bill” including provisions that would prevent Trump from arbitrarily blocking clean energy developments.

“There was a huge surge of misinformation that came kind of immediately after the text was released … we have had lots of exaggerated fears,” Whitehouse added about the criticism of the bill from some Democrats and green groups that environmental protections were being gutted for a modest reduction in greenhouse gas pollution.

Berdasarkan laporan, the bill could result in as much as 1. 5bn tons of emissions reductions by 2040, according to one analysis, and Whitehouse said he hoped amendments would increase this total.

Whether this is enough pollution reduction to justify environmental rollbacks has cut to the heart of tension in the broader green movement over whether to prioritize the climate crisis even if this means all sorts of new infrastructure that may impact ecosystems and communities.

“The prospect of losing tools to slow down and stop the cruelest projects should be haunting everyone,” said Abigail Dillen, president of Earthjustice, which opposes Baaja.

Diungkapkan bahwa for whitehouse, though, tackling the climate crisis is paramount. “Nothing is going to be more devastating to the environment than continuing on our pace of climate change, by like a factor of 100,” he said.

Berdasarkan laporan, “clean energy development is wildly outpacing fossil fuel development now. In the old days the developers were almost always the bad guys and a mindset developed around that pattern,” the senator added.

Diungkapkan bahwa “but that has now shifted and developers are 90% plus likely to be the good guys in the energy space,” whitehouse said. “I think if you have a gigaton scale decrease of emissions available, it’s important to grab it while you can. ”.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, when democrats take control of congress there will be “far bigger environmental and climate fish to fry than just this bill”, whitehouse added. We have to keep going because we are failing right now. We are failing to meet the obligations we have. “I think this is step one. ”.

What happens next in Yemen may send fresh shockwaves to the world economy.

The Iran-backed Houthi rebels who seized much of Yemen in 2014 have now forced the army of the internationally recognised government to withdraw from the Red Sea coast in order to defend their interim capital, Aden.

Their advance bodes ill for Yemen's legitimate, internationally recognised government, its Saudi backers and, by extension, much of the rest of the world.

Yemen, a mountainous, heavily armed, intensely tribal and largely impoverished nation, sits at the far south-west corner of the Arabian Peninsula.

The country has two coasts: One faces the Indian Ocean on which sits the once-prosperous trading port of Aden, the other faces the Red Sea and, most importantly, the narrow chokepoint at the southern exit of that waterway - the so-called Bab al-Mandab Strait or, in English, The Gate of Tears.

Whoever controls that strait can threaten any or all maritime traffic passing through from both the Mediterranean and the Red Sea to the Indian Ocean.

In normal times, it accounts for around 12% of global trade, with anywhere between 70 to 150 ships a day making the transit.

Diungkapkan bahwa but not any more. Although the Houthis say they are no threat to maritime traffic, they are currently at war with Saudi Arabia, making it extremely hazardous for the Saudis to send their oil tankers past the now rebel-controlled coast.

Watch: Why is the Bab al-Mandab Strait so important?.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, when the us and israel started a war with iran in february, tehran responded by choking off much of the oil trade flowing out of the gulf through another narrow chokepoint - the strait of hormuz. This sent oil prices soaring, boosted inflation and hurt economies everywhere.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the saudis had a plan b. Instead of exporting their oil past the dangerous coast of Iran, where their tankers risked being droned or mined by Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guards Corps, they started pumping it overland through their East-West Pipeline to an export terminal on the Red Sea at Yanbu. This worked for a while.

But then in July a cold truce between Saudi Arabia and the Houthis broke down, that pipeline got hit by drones and the rebels started firing missiles and drones at targets all over Saudi Arabia.

Berdasarkan laporan, on land, the houthis seized the initiative and made a lightning dash down the red sea coast, sending the yemeni army into headlong retreat. A brief counter-offensive appears to have failed and the Houthis are now reported to be in full control of the Bab al-Mandab Strait and the nearby offshore islands.

Sebagaimana diketahui, nicholas hopton, a former british ambassador to both yemen and iran and now director-general of the uk-based middle east association, says: "the decision by the legitimate government of yemen to prioritise the military defence of aden at the expense of withdrawing from other areas suggests that the war is not going well for the saudi-backed [yemeni] government. And the rest of the world should be worried. ".

Diungkapkan bahwa he warns that if the port of aden â a city of roughly 1. 25 million inhabitants â was to fall to the Houthis, it "would undoubtedly precipitate a further escalation in the regional crisis and further fragility in the global economy, catalysed by the US-Iran war".

But Mohammed al-Basha, the Yemeni founder of the US-based risk advisory firm Basha Report, believes the Houthis would struggle to capture the heavily fortified city of Aden.

Sebagaimana diketahui, "any attempt to seize a densely populated city like aden would come at a significant human cost," basha said. "Advancing across the flat coastal plains would also expose Houthi forces to air power. ".

Diungkapkan bahwa "for now, the houthis appear to be seeking a negotiated surrender, hoping to exploit infighting and divisions among southern factions to achieve their objectives without a costly urban offensive. ".

It is conceivable that the Yemen war will settle into a less dramatic but deeply unsatisfactory stasis - a situation where casualty figures subside yet the country remains split between areas controlled by the Houthis - Iran's Shia allies - and the disparate and often poorly motivated forces of the Saudi-backed Yemeni army.

The former British defence attachÃ© to Yemen, Col Iain Smailes, warned that the recent Houthi advance could trigger a spike in oil prices, as it did when they seized the Bab al-Mandab Strait in September.

He also warns this could have a knock-on effect to security well beyond Yemen's borders.

"By extending their control over the western coastline, the Houthis will increase their ability to smuggle weapons and ammunition from Iran, the Horn of Africa and elsewhere, posing additional threats to the region," Col Smailes said.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, "this control will enable both iran and the houthis to extend their influence in east africa and beyond. ".

#879. Forensic expert says his analysis of autopsy photos suggests Epstein was killed

📅 16 Nov 2026

Forensic expert says his analysis of autopsy photos suggests Epstein was killed

Tanggal: 16 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/c5n4exg1kkmyo?at_medium=RSS&at_campaign=rss

Watch: Forensic expert Michael Freeman speaks to Newsnight about Epstein's death.

This article contains distressing details and references to suicide.

A forensic expert has said he believes that convicted sex offender Jeffrey Epstein's death in prison was the result of a homicide, not suicide.

Speaking to BBC Newsnight, Professor Michael Freeman said that after reviewing the New York City medical examiner's file he believes Epstein was strangled, most likely from behind.

The medical examiner who carried out the autopsy concluded in 2019 that Epstein's injuries were consistent with suicide and there was no evidence of the defensive wounds expected if his death had been a homicide.

Epstein was found dead in prison on 10 August 2019 in New York as he awaited trial on sex trafficking charges.

Diungkapkan bahwa dr barbara sampson, chief medical examiner at the time of epstein's autopsy, who ruled that epstein's death was a suicide, has previously said: "i stand firmly behind our determination of the cause and manner of death for mr. Epstein. " The BBC has approached Sampson for further comment.

Freeman has served as a cause-of-death expert to attorneys-general in the US for death in police custody cases, including George Floyd in Minnesota.

He published his research and the New York City medical examiner's files after presenting his findings in London on Monday evening.

Freeman, who did not see the body, based his conclusions on the files and photographs from the examiner's report provided to him by Epstein's brother, Mark Epstein, who has always maintained that his brother was murdered.

Berdasarkan laporan, freeman said his analysis is independent and that he was not paid by mark epstein. His research has not been peer reviewed.

He told the BBC that he believed there are signs indicating an assault on Epstein, including a deep haemorrhage to his left shoulder and injuries that appear to be consistent to being struck in the face.

Freeman said he believed the evidence was most consistent with strangulation using a ligature and then that same ligature was probably used to suspend the body from the bunk bed.

Diungkapkan bahwa he said there appeared to be fingernail marks above the ligature mark on epstein's neck, which "would be consistent with strangulation, particularly from behind. And the attempt by the victim to try to remove the ligature from the neck".

Sebagaimana diketahui, he said "the injuries and the way the body was found don't match up. There's only one remaining explanation then, and that is that the death was as a result of a homicide. ".

The medical examiner who performed the autopsy at the time told the Department of Justice (DoJ) Office of the Inspector General , externalthat Epstein's injuries were more consistent with, and indicative of, a suicide by hanging rather than homicide by strangulation, adding there was no evidence of defensive wounds consistent with what is seen in victims of strangulation.

Epstein was awaiting trial on sex trafficking charges when he was found dead in his cell.

Freeman said he would have expected in an investigation of a death by hanging in custody for there to be a photograph before the body was taken down.

According to a DoJ investigation into Epstein's time in prison, the guard who found Epstein immediately called for a second colleague to help, lowered Epstein's body to the floor and began attempts to resuscitate him.

Epstein's death came a month after he was briefly placed on suicide watch, the DoJ report said.

When asked who might have killed Epstein if his interpretation of the evidence was correct, Freeman said he had "no idea".

Berdasarkan laporan, "that is not something i have an opinion about. That isn't any part of any investigation that I've done," he said.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, challenged on whether his views veered into conspiracy theory, freeman said: "i have the luxury of being able to say, don't take my word for it, let everybody look at it. ".

Berdasarkan laporan, "if you think i'm still a conspiracy theorist because i'm looking at something that looks like a strangulation and say, i think it is a strangulation and i don't think it could be a hanging, show me where i got it wrong. ".

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, "i'm wide open to that. I'm an academic. I'm quite happy to hear people's theories on things that are informed," he said.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, epstein was convicted in 2008 of soliciting prostitution from a minor, for which he was registered as a sex offender. He escaped a heavy jail sentence as a result of a plea deal.

Diungkapkan bahwa eleven years later, epstein was charged with running a network of underage girls for sex. He was awaiting trial in 2019 when he was found dead at the Metropolitan Correctional Center in New York City.

#881. Lindsay Clancy to face retrial next year for deaths of her three children

📅 16 Nov 2026

Lindsay Clancy to face retrial next year for deaths of her three children

Tanggal: 16 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/cw5y1v8de35go?at_medium=RSS&at_campaign=rss

Watch: Date announced for Lindsay Clancy retrial.

Warning: This story contains details some readers may find distressing.

Lindsay Clancy, the Massachusetts woman accused of murdering her three children, will face a retrial next year, a judge has said, after a jury deadlocked last time in a case that gripped the nation.

The judge set a trial date for 29 March 2027, though the district attorney did not explicitly say what charges Clancy would face.

Prosecutors said they wanted a jury trial, and the defence said they took that to mean Clancy, 36, would again face first-degree murder charges.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, five-year-old cora, dawson, three, and eight-month-old callan were strangled at the family home on 24 january 2023. The defence argues she had severe postpartum psychosis.

"I think you can read between the lines that when they say that the case is going to require a jury, that it's an indirect comment from the DA [district attorney] that they intend to proceed on first-degree murder indictments, so we will pick a trial date," defence lawyer Kevin Reddington said at Monday's hearing.

Diungkapkan bahwa prosecutors wanted a may trial date, but judge william sullivan decided on march instead. The judge is due to retire in June.

Clancy was charged in the first trial with three counts of first-degree-murder, which is the intentional and premeditated killing of another person.

Berdasarkan laporan, the district attorney has not yet officially said he will proceed with first-degree-murder charges. The BBC has contacted the district attorney's office for comment.

Clancy with her ex-husband and their children - five-year-old Cora, Dawson, three, and eight-month-old Callan.

The prosecution could choose to bring lesser charges against Clancy, such as second-degree-murder, which applies to unlawful killings committed with malice or extreme recklessness, but without planning.

A week ago, Judge Sullivan rejected a defence attempt to throw out the case on the grounds of double jeopardy.

Double jeopardy is a legal principle that protects someone from being prosecuted more than once for the same crime after an acquittal or conviction.

Diungkapkan bahwa the judge's decision cleared the way for a second trial. It was Judge Sullivan who declared the mistrial on 4 September because of the hung jury.

Afterwards, some of the 12 jurors said in media interviews that they had been ready to find Clancy not guilty by reason of insanity, but that one juror had held out.

It was not disputed at Clancy's first trial that she strangled the children with exercise bands in the basement of the family home in the Boston suburb of Duxbury.

She had asked her now-ex husband, Patrick Clancy, to leave the house to pick up takeout food and children's medicine shortly before the children were attacked.

The defence team wanted her found not guilty by reason of insanity, known in Massachusetts as lack of criminal responsibility.

The case sparked a debate over how postpartum mental illness is treated in the US.

Clancy is currently in a state-run psychiatric hospital and medical facility in Massachusetts.

#883. Airstrikes on Iran Missile Sites May Shed Light on Justification for Dams

Airstrikes on Iran Missile Sites May Shed Light on Justification for Dams

Tanggal: 16 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.nytimes.com/2026/11/16/world/middleeast/iran-dams-missile-sites-environmentalists.html

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, environmentalists have long puzzled over a wide network of water projects lacking any obvious justification. Then their areas were targeted in airstrikes.

Environmentalists have long been mystified by the significant proliferation of dams and water transfer projects like pipelines and tunnels across Iran, especially in regions that had no apparent need for them.

Diungkapkan bahwa some analysts think they now know the answer after u. and Israeli airstrikes on concealed Iranian missile sites this year targeted many of the same areas. S. These analysts have concluded that the water projects may have been developed to support the country’s military buildup.

Diungkapkan bahwa given the secrecy surrounding iran’s missile program, any connection between it and iran’s ambitious, decades-old initiative to develop water infrastructure remains speculative. But some experts find the evidence highly suggestive.

Nima Shokri, an expert on water security, and his team at the Hamburg University of Technology, in Germany, had for years tracked an unusually high number of dams across Iran — at least 533 of them, among the most of any country in the region.

Diungkapkan bahwa “it was always puzzling to me,” he said. “Why were they building so many dams?”.

Sebagaimana diketahui, in the spring, dr. Shokri was perusing news about the war in his home country when he came across a map plotting airstrikes that had targeted suspected military sites. The pattern — a semicircle of dots from north to south — nearly matched that of his own map marking the locations of dams.

His old question, he said, was superseded by a new one: “Why does it seem that wherever we have dams, there is a missile strike close by?”.

#885. Five EU states announce plans for immigration ‘return hubs’ in Rwanda

📅 17 Nov 2026

Five EU states announce plans for immigration ‘return hubs’ in Rwanda

Tanggal: 17 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/nov/16/eu-states-immigration-return-hubs-rwanda

Germany, Austria, Netherlands, Denmark and Greece likely to face challenges to policy criticised as ‘grave moral failing’.

Five EU member states have announced plans to set up an offshore centre in Rwanda for people with no legal right to stay in Europe, in a pilot scheme that is expected to face legal challenges and has been denounced as “a grave moral failing”.

The five countries – Germany, Austria, the Netherlands, Denmark and Greece – are the first to seek to use the EU’s newly agreed returns law that allows people who have exhausted all avenues of appeal against their removal from Europe to be sent to a third country.

In a statement released on Monday the five EU countries said “concrete negotiations with partner country Rwanda will begin for implementation”, saying the scheme would make “an important contribution to further curbing illegal migration, dismantling the business model of smugglers and relieving the burden on our population”.

Berdasarkan laporan, officials hope to send 100 people to rwanda from early next year to test the model. The scheme will apply to adults whose claims to asylum have been rejected or others with no legal right to live in the EU.

In theory, according to diplomatic sources, migrants would stay in a reception centre in Rwanda for a couple of months, before choosing to integrate into life in the Great Lakes country or return to their home nation.

Unlike the failed scheme pursued by the British Conservative government in Rwanda, or Italy’s agreement with Albania, it will not apply to people pursuing asylum claims.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the reception centre, which would be an open facility, was not intended to house people long term but to accommodate regular flows of people, the countries said. Diplomatic sources said the EU countries were not using British-funded facilities built in Kigali.

The governments involved argue it will protect the European asylum system while removing the incentive for irregular migrants to come to Europe.

Denmark’s immigration minister, Morten Bødskov, whose government has pioneered a tough line on migration widely emulated across the EU, said it was “a huge breakthrough”.

Berdasarkan laporan, the german interior minister, alexander dobrindt, said: “return hubs offer a positive approach for people without the right to stay and with no prospects in europe, whose countries of origin do not cooperate in the repatriation process. ”.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, andy burnham told reporters last week that the uk had not had direct discussions with european governments involved in return hubs but “we will watch that with interest, learning from what went on in the past. The public want us to do whatever we can to deal with illegal immigration. ”.

Critics have highlighted the ethical difficulties of striking an agreement with Rwanda’s repressive government, which was found in 2024 by the US state department to allow state security forces and civilian officials to commit human rights abuses with impunity, while also raising concerns about freedom of expression and forced labour.

Sebagaimana diketahui, spain’s socialist prime minister, pedro sanchez, said on monday the move had no “future or humanity”. “I don’t see any future or humanity in that. It’s not the solution,” Sanchez, an outspoken defender of immigration in a Europe that has tilted to the right in recent years, told Telecinco television.

Berdasarkan laporan, the french green mep mélissa camara denounced the agreement between the five countries and rwanda as “an agreement of shame” and “a grave moral failing”. She said: “Under this agreement, people will be deported thousands of kilometres away from the European Union, with no guarantees regarding the compliance with their rights. ”.

Berdasarkan laporan, alain berset, the secretary general of the council of europe, the continent’s human rights body, said it was not possible “to be so precise a priori” about what any return hubs proposal meant. Speaking to the Guardian before the announcement, he said all members of the Council of Europe were committed to the European convention on human rights “and this must be the lighthouse” for all discussions on return hubs.

Berdasarkan laporan, “on concrete cases, then we will have to see if this is compliant with the convention,” he said. He stressed that “all countries must be able to define their migration policy”.

Officials involved in setting up the migration centres expect legal challenges, but say the scheme is grounded in human rights law.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, rights organisations say the scheme is bound to fail. “Member states may call them ‘return hubs’ or even ‘welcome centres’, but no euphemism can hide the violence of uprooting people from the life they’ve been building in Europe, and sending them to a country they don’t even know, without family, networks or meaningful prospects,” said Chiara Catelli of Picum, a pan-European organisation that campaigns for the rights of undocumented migrants.

#889. Robert Pattinson: How the Twilight star became 007

📅 16 Nov 2026

Robert Pattinson: How the Twilight star became 007

Tanggal: 16 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/c574290jvk8wo?at_medium=RSS&at_campaign=rss

Robert Pattinson has starred in films including the Twilight franchise and The Batman.

Robert Pattinson's career is already flying high with roles in films including the Twilight series, The Batman and The Odyssey, so signing up to play James Bond will propel his profile into the stratosphere.

He's already established himself as a leading man, action star and character actor, which is clearly why he is about to play the suave, British secret agent 007.

At 40, he is slightly older than some of the other men reportedly lined up for the role, but he's also the most famous - something the new Bond studio Amazon-MGM may have favoured, with an eye on the box office.

His recent work has garnered both critical and box office success, including Christopher Nolan's summer blockbuster The Odyssey, in which he played the villainous Antinous.

Pattinson was also called "Oscar-worthy" by the Independent and "superb" by The Times, for his performance in November's Primetime, as the real-life host of US TV show To Catch a Predator.

Berdasarkan laporan, he also helped lead 2022's the batman to the second-biggest north american opening of the covid-19 pandemic behind spider-man: no way home. The Guardian said he played the "brooding" role with "appealing vulnerability, external".

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, meanwhile in dark romantic comedy the drama, he and his co-star gave a "career-highlight performance", external. It's one of three films he appeared in with Zendaya this year, along with The Odyssey and Dune: Part Three.

Robert Pattinson starred in 2022's The Batman, which was described by critics as a grim, gritty, and gripping super-noir.

Born in Barnes, south-west London, Pattinson grew up with his father, a classic car trader and mother, who worked at a modelling agency, and two elder sisters.

His interest in acting started while he was still at school, when he joined the Barnes Theatre Club.

"I wouldn't be acting if it wasn't for that little club," he told Your Local Guardian in 2008, external.

Sebagaimana diketahui, "i went originally because a lot of pretty girls went there," he said. "I worked backstage and I started acting when all the good people left and I was the only one tall enough to play the lead.

Sebagaimana diketahui, "in a weird sort of way, that stuff was probably the best i've done and the stuff i am most proud of. ".

Berdasarkan laporan, he landed his first big film role more than two decades ago, playing cedric diggory in 2005's harry potter and the goblet of fire. A relatively minor character, but it was enough to get him noticed.

Robert Pattinson and Kristen Stewart starred in five Twilight films from 2005 to 2012.

Three years later, he had a starring role in the first of five Twilight films, along with Kristen Stewart, in which they played star-crossed lovers - vampire Edward Cullen and mortal-turned vampire Kristen Stewart.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, based on stephanie meyer's hugely popular young adult books, the films globally grossed more than $3bn (â£2. 2bn) by 2012, and established Pattinson as a heartthrob.

He spoke in his early career of finding his often adoring, screaming fans hard to deal with.

Diungkapkan bahwa "although is part of the job, it feels like they have been paid to turn up and scream at me at 7. 30pm," he said.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, "nothing i don't think can prepare you for the fans. I don't know why I'm not getting used to it but I'm completely overwhelmed every time. ".

In 2010, Time included him in their list of 100 people who "most affect our world", external, saying perhaps prophetically that "we haven't seen a tenth of what he can do on screen".

After such mainstream success with the Twilight franchise, Pattinson was able to branch out.

He went on to work with several acclaimed independent film directors including David Cronenberg, starring in his film Cosmpopolis in 2012, as well as working with Werner Herzog in 2015's Queen of the Desert and The Lighthouse (2019), directed by Robert Eggers.

Diungkapkan bahwa pattinson told screen daily why he took the role in psychological horror film the lighthouse, external, saying he told eggers: "i just want to do something weird. ".

Pattinson and Zendaya have appeared in three films together this year - The Drama, The Odyssey and Dune: Part Three.

The following year though, he was back in big-studio territory, with Odyssey director Christopher Nolan, in sci-fi thriller Tenet, and again in 2022 with The Batman, directed by Matt Reeves and co-starring Zoe Kravitz and Paul Dano.

Berdasarkan laporan, pattinson told screen daily why he returned to big-budget films, explaining: "i guess i was trying to do the opposite of what i've been doing. I started thinking, 'I really want to do a big thing. '.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, "i hadn't done something with a massive budget for ages. But you approach it exactly the same way. ".

The Batman got generally positive reviews, re-establishing Pattinson with a broader range of fans.

By 2025, when he was on the red carpet for Parasite director Bong Joon Ho's sci-fi black comedy, Mickey 17, he said it was "quite strange" to have a fanbase that was now dominated by men, external.

"There's like a bunch of guys, which is a new one for me!" he told the Associated Press.

Pattinson's private life has often created interest in the press, not least his previous relationships with Stewart, and then the singer FKA Twigs.

Berdasarkan laporan, since 2018, he has been in a relationship with model suki waterhouse. They got engaged in December 2023 and had their first child, a daughter, in March.

Robert Pattinson and Suki Waterhouse have been a couple since 2018.

With his latest role as James Bond, Pattinson will be extremely busy, not least because the forthcoming Batman sequel is reportedly due out in 2028.

But the actor will have a head start as 007, having already worked with Bond 26 director Denis Villeneuve, who also helmed Dune: Part Three.

Pattinson was full of praise for him on their most recent film, despite the strain of working in the furnace-like heat of the desert.

"The scale of this stuff is just unbelievable, you're having your own Dune theme park, where the gimbal is going upside down and flying, and this is not like work at all," he told the New York Times, external.

Sebagaimana diketahui, "there are no negatives. Apart from having your sweat drained out of the top of your head, and getting like bulbous sweat bubbles. But even then, I didn't even really notice them.

Diungkapkan bahwa "he's so easy to work with, denis, it's never really a stress. ".

Diungkapkan bahwa sounds like pattinson will have the cool head needed to juggle his forthcoming roles - including james bond. You could even say he may end up being shaken, but not stirred.

From semiconductor dominance to new power grids, defense deals and K-pop, the region — beyond China — is becoming increasingly interconnected and self-reliant.

Damien covers global affairs from Vietnam.

President Trump’s trip to Asia this week will largely be seen as a test of American power in the main region where the United States and China compete for influence.

Diungkapkan bahwa his meetings in manila and shenzhen, china, will be scrutinized for shifts on trade and security. Deals he might strike with Beijing — plus a gathering with President Xi Jinping of China and President Vladimir V. Putin of Russia — will put the world’s great-power contest on display, as all three seek to show strength.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, but asia is not just a theater of competition. Many countries in the region have become wealthier, more technologically advanced and increasingly interconnected. Especially now, as China’s military becomes more threatening and the United States less reliable, they are hedging against greatness and relying more on neighbors.

Berdasarkan laporan, asian students and workers are moving to neighboring states. Countries with expanding defense industries are selling weapons to new partners. Nations that compete for high-tech investment are even making plans to cooperate on energy and cybersecurity.

Berdasarkan laporan, “they’re all looking at what more they can do together when the great powers are behaving so badly,” said ted osius, a former u. S. ambassador to Vietnam and adjunct professor of geopolitics at Fulbright University in Ho Chi Minh City. “If you’re a middle power, you’re thinking ‘I need more options. ’”.

Here are a few numbers that provide a sense of what the region contributes to the global economy, and how its nations are becoming more bound together to shape the world.
