#893. Is India rethinking its short-term military recruitment scheme?

📅 16 Nov 2026

Is India rethinking its short-term military recruitment scheme?

Tanggal: 16 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/c8ly0yr7wv1no?at_medium=RSS&at_campaign=rss

There are currently 300,000 Agniveers serving in India's defence forces.

For generations of young Indians, joining the armed forces offered something few other jobs did - a steady career, financial security, the promise of a pension after retirement and the pride of serving their country.

Diungkapkan bahwa in 2022, the government upended that arrangement, announcing a new reform scheme under which young men and women entering the military would serve for just four years. Only a quarter would be allowed to stay on permanently. The rest would return to civilian life with a lump-sum payment, but without the pension and other benefits that had long made military service an attractive career.

Now, as the first batch of recruits prepares to complete its four-year term, the government is offering them a chance to stay longer, in a significant shift in a policy that has been fiercely debated since its introduction.

Sebagaimana diketahui, on 4 november, chief of defence staff general ns raja subramani announced that recruits who failed to secure permanent positions under the agnipath, or "path of fire", programme would be offered another two years of service at higher pay. They would then get a second opportunity to join the regular forces, provided they met the selection criteria.

Gen Subramani said the decision followed feedback from the forces and insisted that Agnipath would continue.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, but the timing is significant. More than 18,300 recruits from the first batch are due to complete their initial tenure by the end of 2026. Officials say the new arrangement will be offered to more than 300,000 Agniveers - as recruits under the scheme are known - currently serving across the army, navy and air force.

Sebagaimana diketahui, whether future batches will also be covered remains unclear. The BBC has contacted the defence ministry for clarification.

Berdasarkan laporan, the ministry has defended , externalagnipath, saying internal assessments found the recruits to be physically fit, motivated and technologically adaptable. It also said the scheme had widened recruitment across districts and made the process more standardised.

But the extension has brought renewed attention to the trade-offs at the heart of the policy - and whether its original ambitions were realistic.

Those selected are trained for months before being inducted into regiments.

When the government introduced Agnipath, it argued the scheme would reduce the average age of the armed forces, lower long-term salary and pension costs and create a younger, more technologically adaptable fighting force.

But military experts and opposition leaders have questioned whether a four-year contract could replace what had traditionally been a coveted, long-term career in the armed forces.

"Being a soldier in the armed forces was a chance for these young men to make a life for themselves, to get their families out of poor or lower-middle-income conditions," says retired Maj Gen Yash Mor, a vocal critic of the scheme.

Diungkapkan bahwa these concerns were also amplified by the timing of agnipath's launch. Recruitment had been suspended for nearly two years during the Covid pandemic, leaving thousands of aspirants waiting for vacancies to reopen.

The changes were greeted by massive protests across the country, with many saying the career path they had spent years preparing for had fundamentally changed.

This sentiment was felt most in states and cities that have traditionally been major recruitment hubs, where military service has been a family tradition for generations.

Kulbeer Singh Chaudhary, who runs a recruitment training institute in Dehradun city, says interest in joining the armed forces fell sharply and he stopped conducting Agniveer training batches.

The latest announcement, he hopes, would reverse that trend.

"The possibility of a longer engagement and eventual absorption into the forces may offer young candidates greater assurance," he says.

Diungkapkan bahwa the changes also come at a time when the armed forces are facing personnel shortages. In November last year, The Indian Express reported, external that the army alone faced a shortfall of nearly 180,000 soldiers and was considering increasing recruitment.

Many young men from small towns spend months preparing for the selection process to join the defence forces.

Sebagaimana diketahui, but the debate over agnipath goes beyond what happens to recruits after four years. Critics also question whether that is enough time to turn them into experienced soldiers.

Sanjiv Krishan Sood, a former additional director general of the Border Security Force, has argued, external that the shorter training period is particularly problematic for technical roles requiring specialised skills.

Retired Maj Gen Mor says military effectiveness depends on experience and trust built over years.

"It takes eight-to-nine years to turn a raw recruit into a dependable, seasoned soldier - someone capable of handling a tank crew, an artillery gun crew or a small detachment," he says.

Berdasarkan laporan, "over those years, a soldier develops the ethos, camaraderie, brotherhood and fighting spirit that bind a unit together. These qualities cannot be built overnight. ".

Sood says the additional two years could help improve recruits' skills, particularly in handling specialised equipment.

Berdasarkan laporan, senior military leaders have also welcomed the extension. Air Vice Marshal Shekhar Yadav told news agency ANI, external it would allow the forces to retain trained personnel for longer.

But the change could create fresh challenges within military units.

Regular soldiers, Agniveers on four-year contracts and those serving an additional two years could find themselves working alongside one another despite differences in pay, promotion prospects and post-service benefits.

Experts warn that these disparities could affect unit cohesion.

Indian soldiers are deployed through the year at the country's borders with China and Pakistan.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, there is also the question of whether the changes will undermine one of the government's central objectives: reducing spending. Almost half of India's defence budget, external goes towards salaries and pensions, leaving less money for modernisation and new equipment.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, by limiting the number of personnel eligible for long-term benefits, agnipath was expected to ease that burden. But critics argue that savings should not come at the expense of military effectiveness.

"We are not against making changes, but there are ways and means to go about it," says Mor, adding that the government could instead reduce annual recruitment while retaining soldiers for longer periods.

He also points to India's tense borders with Pakistan and China, where troops remain deployed year-round, placing sustained demands on manpower and operational experience.

Retired Major-General Birender Singh Dhanoa, meanwhile, questions whether shorter service makes financial sense when the military is investing in training to operate increasingly sophisticated equipment.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, "the amount of time it takes to train, and the financial outlay for training, is much higher for modern equipment. So shouldn't you get the best bang for your buck?" he asks.

Many retired officers had proposed a different approach when the scheme was announced, he says.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, "we suggested that if you want to reduce your financial burden, you increase the terms and conditions of service. Take these guys for eight-or-nine years and retain a larger number after that. ".

Berdasarkan laporan, the announcement also comes at a politically sensitive time. Elections are due soon in Punjab, Uttar Pradesh and Uttarakhand - states that have traditionally supplied large numbers of soldiers and where military recruitment remains an important source of employment.

The opposition Congress party has called the revision a "u-turn", alleging that the government is responding to fears of losing votes.

Berdasarkan laporan, for young recruits approaching the end of their contracts, the changes offer some reassurance, but few guarantees. Two more years of service could mean more money, greater experience and another chance at a permanent career.

But for many, it also means putting their futures on hold, without knowing whether they will eventually be allowed to stay.

#897. Faisal Islam: What's in the Brexit reset food deal and are there trade-offs?

📅 16 Nov 2026

Faisal Islam: What's in the Brexit reset food deal and are there trade-offs?

Tanggal: 16 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/c6wy4l8nl42wo?at_medium=RSS&at_campaign=rss

Some British sausages have faced barriers to being exported to the EU.

In Boston, Lincolnshire, a supplier of ready meals to Marks & Spencer (M&S) manufactures thousands of portions of spaghetti bolognese to be sent to the retailer's shops in the Republic of Ireland.

Every plastic pallet is meticulously individually tagged with a green-grey label âEireâ.

Every truck full of food sent to European Union countries requires hundreds of pages of forms, checks by vets, expense and delays.

It has cost M&S millions of pounds and is part of that reason the British business shut down 11 French stores in 2021.

Berdasarkan laporan, many smaller exporters stopped sending their goods to the eu entirely. Some produce, including sausages and certain types of seafood, were entirely stopped.

All this was the predictable consequence of former Prime Minister Boris Johnsonâs 2020 deal prioritising regulatory freedom over freeflowing goods trade.

That will end with a Brexit "reset" that Prime Minister Andy Burnham is set to sign with the EU on Friday.

The government claims it could boost the economy to the tune of Â£5bn a year and cut the cost of food for households.

But will the agreement mean a return to frictionless trade for food with the EU or are there trade-offs and quid pro quos the UK will have to make?.

EU affairs minister Hamish Falconer, who is a key negotiator with the bloc, acknowledged a âchoiceâ is being made.

In exchange for being able to export produce such as Lincolnshire sausages to the 27 countries, the flipside is the extent to which the UK will be able to influence EU food policies.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the uk will have a "voice in the room", said falconer, but no vote. Critics have said a reset will make the UK "a rule taker", not a rule maker.

But Falconer said the UK will be involved in a process to shape the rules.

A Brexit reset would not involve any upfront payments, said Falconer, but made it clear there could well be an "exit clause" in case a future UK government reversed the closer alignment.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, he said this was "reasonable" to consider what would happen if a future conservative or reform government wanted to undo the new arrangements. Both parties have said they would if they were in power.

"The EU is worried about that and you can see why," he said.

The BBC understands that the clause is a result of EU concerns about the possible cost of having to rebuild facilities for border food safety checks which were put in place following Brexit.

The prime minister has said he believes there is a "win-win" deal to be had with the EU.

Speaking at a Marks & Spencer food court in central London, Falconer said reducing the cost of importing food "will mean less cost for supermarkets, and I hope that less cost then turns into cheaper produce on the shelves".

He said companies have to currently deal with "pages and pages" of form-filling.

Some exports are rejected for having the wrong colour of ink on forms, or an inaccurate Latin name for cooked meats.

The reset could also mean "tearing up" checks that were introduced on goods flowing from Great Britain to Northern Ireland, following Brexit, he said, as well as separate "Not for EU" labelling.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the whole deal to be signed on friday is calculated to add 0. 4% to UK GDP.

Minister for EU relations Hamish Falconer.

Tom Bradshaw, president of the National Farmers' Union, welcomed reduced border inspections and paperwork but said that for the NFU it was "a moment of opportunity and risk" with farmers waiting to see what carve-outs and transitional arrangements would be included.

Trade volumes in food exports to the EU had "fallen significantly - by over a third" since 2019, he said.

But the UK should take a "pragmatic" approach to implementing any new rules.

He raised pesticides and precision breeding - or gene edited crops - as areas where he hoped some compromise would be found.

UK firms are, for example, developing tomatoes engineered to contain extra vitamin D.

Historically the EU has had much stricter rules on gene-editing, but this year relaxed regulations.

Falconer said people would have to "wait and see the detail" in this area.

Another contentious area has been crisp flavourings, with concerns raised that stricter EU rules on certain ingredients might limit the sale of some popular snack flavours in the UK.

"I want to take this opportunity to absolutely stamp down on misinformation about smoky bacon crisps," Falconer said.

Post-Brexit the UK had stayed "pretty closely aligned" to European food safety standards, he said.

Two leading snack brands had already adapted their recipes to accommodate EU rules, an example of the kind of alignment that would happen whether or not there was a reset of UK-EU relations.

"The truth is, almost every business in this country that wants to export food or drink will be aligning with EU rules because it's our biggest market.

"Lots of people, like the good people at Walkers and Frazzles have made these changes already, so I would want to reassure people, particularly smoky bacon fans, it's okay," he said.

Could smoky bacon crisps really be banned?.

Ten years on, Brexit's economic impact is becoming clearer.

Reeves says UK's future should be inside the EU.

#898. Truck driver fired for ‘unsafe’ use of smartglasses in first reported sacking over device in Australia

📅 17 Nov 2026

Truck driver fired for ‘unsafe’ use of smartglasses in first reported sacking over device in Australia

Tanggal: 17 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.theguardian.com/technology/2026/nov/17/toll-truck-driver-fired-sacked-smartglasses-australia-ntwnfb

Toll employee Ricardo Martins Silva used smartglasses to take photos at an LPG terminal despite the risk of an explosion caused by an electrical spark, a court heard.

Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast.

A Toll truck driver was fired from work in Victoria after using smartglasses to snap photos at an LPG terminal, in what was described as an “intrinsically unsafe” incident.

It is the first reported case in Australia of a worker dismissed for using smartglasses in a workplace.

Diungkapkan bahwa the employee, ricardo martins silva, was fired from toll transport in july 2025, after eight months with the company as an lpg (liquefied petroleum gas) tanker driver, the federal circuit court heard. His role was to drive a loaded LPG tanker for Origin Energy from the Long Island Point terminal in Hastings, Victoria, for onward delivery.

A federal circuit court judgment last week stated that on 17 June 2025, Martins Silva raised concerns about a truck allocated to him, telling superiors the truck had too much vibration and was jumping excessively.

The judgment stated he was advised to take a different truck, and when he went to the terminal, he took photographs using his smartglasses, and sent them to a superior with a message stating: “I’m going to take the truck back to Dandenong and I’m leaving! There’s no more time for deliveries today!”.

The Esso worker at the terminal told Toll that any use of electrical equipment on-site is “intrinsically unsafe” due to the risk of an explosion caused by electrical spark.

Martins Silva was prevented from taking on additional work until an investigation into the incident had been completed, and Origin Energy later asked the employee be removed from work as soon as possible because “his attitude is poor” and “not doing planned deliveries because he is ‘tired and stressed’ is not acceptable”, the judgment read.

Sebagaimana diketahui, martins silva sent emails between 17 and 19 june raising concerns about his role, truck allocations and safety issues. The worker on 20 June submitted a complaint about his employment, including safety, and impact of working conditions on his health, among other things.

On 22 June, the employee was advised he was stood down, the judgment stated.

Berdasarkan laporan, at a meeting on 24 june, what toll termed as “the glasses incident” was raised with the employee. He was told it was regarded as a “critical safety breach” and that Toll had commenced an investigation process due to its seriousness.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, by 30 june, the company decided martins silva should be suspended from employment citing, among other reasons, the seriousness of the glasses incident. On 9 July, the employee was informed that taking a photograph with the smartglasses was in breach of Toll’s code of practice, and his contract of employment. His employment was terminated on 18 July, the judgment stated.

Martins Silva claimed the action was in breach of the Fair Work Act, arguing Toll’s actions were as a result of complaints he had made.

The federal circuit court found in the ruling last week that the glasses incident was “on any objective view a serious incident”.

“On the day he wore the smart glasses, Mr Martins Silva was plainly aware of the risks of what he was doing – he went so far as to seek to mitigate the risk by covering his smartglasses with safety glasses,” the ruling from federal circuit justice Karl Blake stated.

Sebagaimana diketahui, “the glasses incident was not concocted or made to look more serious than what it was. It was objectively very serious. ”.

Martins Silva had conceded in cross examination that he knew at the time he had done the wrong thing, Blake’s judgment stated, but had written to his employer at the time that his judgment had been affected by the unresolved trauma of a truck fire in which he had been injured in March 2025.

Sebagaimana diketahui, blake found martins silva was not dismissed because he made complaints but “because he wore smartglasses” at the terminal and his employer was of the view that it amounted to a serious safety incident. The application was dismissed.

While the case had focused on safety concerns, since the arrival of Meta’s Ray-Bans and cheaper alternatives such as the Kmart Anko brand glasses, governments have faced pressure to ban the devices over privacy concerns.

Councils across Australia have banned the glasses from some public spaces including gyms and pools, while the federal government is considering bans in government offices.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, germany, austria, the netherlands, greece and denmark are seeking to establish a hub for rejected asylum seekers. Here’s what to know about their effort.

Five European countries announced a plan on Monday that would send rejected asylum seekers to Rwanda, an experiment that comes as governments across the continent toughen their stances on migration.

The joint push from Germany, Austria, Denmark, the Netherlands and Greece was pitched as a way to handle migrants who had no right to stay in Europe but who, for one reason or another, could not or would not return to their home countries.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the project, which is not yet finalized, shows how european leaders’ stance on migration has hardened since the arrivals of 2015-16, when countries like germany admitted more than a million asylum seekers. With far-right groups like the Alternative for Germany rising in popularity, centrist leaders have gradually taken a less welcoming stance.

“For me, today marks a crucial step toward a new migration system,” Mette Frederiksen, the prime minister of Denmark, said at a news conference on Monday.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the pilot project is expected to start on a small scale, with perhaps 100 or 200 deportees. Critics are already worried both about the idea of sending people to a nation to which they have no connection, and about the risk that human rights will not be sufficiently protected in Rwanda.

The country has a history of courting migration-related deals.

Diungkapkan bahwa britain developed a plan to send asylum seekers there in 2022, though judges in london ultimately ruled the effort unlawful and it was later abandoned. The United States has recently deported people to Rwanda.

Number of people allowed to stay for third year on holidaymaker visa to be increased from 5,000 to 25,000 under revised plan.

Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast.

The federal government has backpedalled on its plan to cut backpacker numbers, arguing the change is the “best possible outcome” for regional industries who had criticised the crackdown because they rely on travellers for labour.

On Tuesday, the Albanese government announced it would lift the proposed cap on third-year working holiday visas, boost regional work requirements and delay the start of a new ballot system.

The home affairs minister, Tony Burke, had announced in a major speech in September plans to cap the number of third-year backpackers to 5,000 from the current level of about 31,000.

Sebagaimana diketahui, burke said on tuesday that the cap would now instead be set at 25,000 places. The home affairs minister claimed despite the increase, the net overseas migration (Nom) target would not change, due to a go-slow on approving UK backpacker visas.

“From the day after the [September] speech, myself, the assistant ministers and the department started consultation with industry to work through what’s the best landing place to deliver the total numbers we’re talking about, but to do it in a way that works best for industry,” Burke told reporters.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, “there was some slower processing generally happening before the announcement i made, and we have continued the slower processing with uk only since then. That’s provided the space that allowed me to go to the 5,000 to 25,000. ”.

The major reforms to working holiday visas unveiled in September included a ballot for backpackers seeking to stay a second or third year which would require them to work in the regions.

Under the original proposal, 45,000 backpackers would be allowed to remain for a second year and would be required to work at least three months in a regional area, and just 5,000 places would be allocated for workers for a third year.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the ballot, due to come into effect in november will now be delayed until early next year. From 1 March 2027, backpackers will be required to work in regional areas for four months, instead of three. (The changes won’t apply to travellers who finish their current regional work by the end of February. ).

Burke said the government would introduce a new “guarantee” for backpackers granted second- and third-year visas as part of the ballot process.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, “from december, people will be able to apply for the guarantee. “We’ll be issuing those every month. If you receive the guarantee and you do the regional work … then you’ve got the guarantee for the next year,” Burke said. And from January, every month we’ll be issuing these guarantees. ”.

The minister said the extra requirement was “the best possible outcome” for regional areas.

Making backpackers do 120 days of regional work instead of 88 meant that even with the reduction in visa numbers there was a boost in the overall workforce, Burke said.

The changes followed months of consultation with industry, regional and agricultural groups who warned of worker shortages.

The Nationals leader, Matt Canavan, said the initial policy announcement had done “massive damage” to small businesses and farmers in regional areas.

“The damage has been done to confidence in the sector and we still haven’t seen a cut to migration,” Canavan told reporters on Tuesday.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, “having slightly increased these backpacker number caps in this announcement today, the question has got to go to the government, surely the [net] overseas migration figure is now going up further. ”.

The government has set a net overseas migration target for 2026-27 of 245,000, and plabs to reduce that to 225,000 in 2027-28.

Sebagaimana diketahui, workers from the uk are exempt from the caps under a free trade agreement signed in 2021. Sources say the prime minister, Anthony Albanese, is in discussions with his UK counterpart, Andy Burnham, to force British backpackers to also do regional work going forward.

Burke said he was optimistic about negotiations.

Sebagaimana diketahui, “the conversations … have been going very well. But until every detail is landed on, I’m not going to get ahead of an announcement,” he said.

Sebagaimana diketahui, “the united kingdom have a good understanding of the issues that we need to resolve, so i’m not going to put a timeline on it. But I will say I’m very optimistic. ”.

The Accommodation Australia chief executive, James Goodwin, said Tuesday’s backflip showed the government had listened to concerns from the sector.

Sebagaimana diketahui, “these are sensible and welcome changes that recognise the important contribution working holidaymakers make,” goodwin said. “Minister Burke has listened to industry concerns and responded with changes that will make a meaningful difference. ”.

The government has felt pressure to reduce Nom which has become a contested debate.

Berdasarkan laporan, in september, ahead of the government’s original announcement, one nation proposed cutting migration numbers by 750,000 over three years by drastically reducing international student and family visas. That policy has since disappeared from One Nation’s website.

The Coalition has also flagged a reduction in net overseas migration.

The treasurer has come under growing pressure to sell the government’s economic strategy after five interest rate hikes, and amid rising unemployment and cost-of-living pressures.

Chalmers, speaking at the Australian Securities and Investment Commission conference in Sydney, said the mid-year economic and fiscal outlook (Myefo) “will strike some fine balances”.

“It will cut enough, but not too much,” he said.

Berdasarkan laporan, “it will help ease immediate capacity pressures without putting growth at risk, and make room for the responsible cost-of-living relief we’ve been rolling out without adding to price pressures. ”.

Diungkapkan bahwa “in contrast, rates are expected to continue climbing in every major advanced economy. ”.

“First, because of the intensifying spending pressures coming at us, including higher debt interest, rising costs of essential services, and other unavoidable spends and variations,” he said.

Sebagaimana diketahui, “second, because we take seriously and embrace our responsibilities in the fight against inflation. ”.

Berdasarkan laporan, despite the treasurer’s claim of $180bn in total savings since labor came to office in 2022, the budget papers project a deficit just shy of $10bn in 2024-25, $22. 3bn in 2025-26, and an expected shortfall of $31. 5bn this financial year.

The government has also come under pressure to redesign its changes to capital gains tax, including an alternative, business-backed model suggested by independent MP Allegra Spender.

That proposal would cut the CGT discount from 50% to 40% for “active” investments, such as shares and equity in small businesses, and leave the inflation-linked CGT model for property.

In his speech Chalmers also announced that the Australian Taxation Office would begin consulting with the business sector on “modernising Australia’s business tax system”, which he said could save companies and sole traders tens of millions of dollars a year.

“We’ll immediately begin consulting on two specific options,” he said.

Berdasarkan laporan, “first, reducing the burden on sole traders by pre-filling contractor income – saving an estimated 400,000 hours and $37m in costs each year. A third US aircraft carrier has arrived in the Middle East, US Central Command said in a social media post on Monday, making a dramatic show of military might as Donald Trump keeps his options open for next steps in the Iran war.

The USS Theodore Roosevelt brings thousands of additional troops to the Middle East as Trump has oscillated between threatening additional large-scale strikes on Iran and insisting that the more than eight-month-old war “militarily is effectively over”.

Berdasarkan laporan, the roosevelt, along with its accompanying strike force, left san diego in september. It joins the USS George HW Bush and the USS George Washington aircraft carriers, as well as smaller navy ships, which are in the region to maintain a naval blockade of Iranian shipping.

Berdasarkan laporan, the george hw bush arrived in the region in april, while the george washington arrived in august. The navy previously had three carrier strike groups in the Middle East in April, for the first time since 2003.

Diungkapkan bahwa in addition to the three aircraft carriers, the flotilla in the arabian sea now includes 13 destroyers, two cruisers and a littoral combat ship, according to the navy. Two more destroyers are in the Red Sea.

Diungkapkan bahwa the roosevelt had deployed along with the uss makin island amphibious readiness group, which includes the uss john p murtha and uss anchorage amphibious landing ships and around 2,000 marines. Those ships have yet to make it to the region.

Diungkapkan bahwa the third carrier arrived nearly two weeks after midterm elections that saw voters deliver major losses to trump’s republican party, driven in part by the unpopularity of the iran war and its economic effects. The results led JD Vance to publicly break with Trump over the conflict, posting on social media that “the reason we lost is the war”.

Trump has insisted it was the right thing to do and has not ruled out restarting the conflict, which has been locked in a stalemate for months.

Last week, Trump warned Iran that the US military is “locked and loaded” and that the US was keeping an eye on Pickaxe Mountain, a facility linked to Iran’s nuclear program, for signs of activity.

“If something does not work out, I would not hesitate” to act, Trump told conservative broadcaster Hugh Hewitt on Thursday.

Yet, Trump also told reporters last week that he believed it was highly unlikely he would need to order new major strikes on Iran, declaring that the war “militarily is effectively over” after meeting with Qatar’s prime minister.

Trump also declared that the US no longer needs a deal with Tehran and told Vance – who was a chief negotiator in earlier ceasefire talks – instead to focus on the administration’s domestic anti-fraud campaign targeting Democratic-controlled cities and states.

Diungkapkan bahwa negotiations have stalled due to differences over iran’s nuclear program, an issue that trump insists be part of any deal meant to end the war. Iran wants the US first to agree to several core conditions, including lifting the naval blockade that is stopping its oil from getting to world markets.

In the meantime, a focal point of the simmering conflict remains the strait of Hormuz, a critical waterway where a fifth of the world’s oil passed before the war.

Commercial ships are still coming under attack or facing other risks, while the US has carried out limited strikes on Iranian targets near the strait and is helping guide vessels through the contested waters.

Iranian state TV, quoting the naval arm of Iran’s revolutionary guard and the army, warned shipping companies Monday that a US-supported route through the waterway is dangerous because of mines.

Mines have damaged six oil tankers since Sunday, polluting the strait’s coastlines, according to the revolutionary guard’s navy.

Separately, a projectile struck a tanker trying to transit through the strait, starting an engine room fire, but no casualties were reported, the United Kingdom Maritime Trade Organization said.

US Central Command, which oversees military operations in the Middle East, said it has redirected 150 merchant vessels and disabled five since June under the blockade.

Independent assessments from Lloyd’s List, a maritime tracking and analysis firm, show that traffic through the strait remains at less than a third of prewar levels.

In 1990 Yemen had been divided in two, and many in the south want to return to a separated state.

Report on Britain’s youth jobs crisis calls for welfare, education, health and employment policy shake-up.

Andy Burnham is being urged to spend billions of pounds on a “new deal” for the next generation that would fund guaranteed jobs support for young people to offset a radical cut in benefits.

In a watershed report on Britain’s youth jobs crisis, Alan Milburn, the Tony Blair-era health secretary, said the country was at a “fork in the road” after a surge in the number of young people not in education, employment or training (Neet) to almost a million.

He said ministers had a choice to either carry on down a path of state and market failure or adopt a 10-year plan with an ambition to eradicate long-term youth unemployment.

Publishing a blueprint for change in a highly anticipated review, the report calls on the government to launch a sweeping shake-up of welfare, education, health and employment policy with the aim to ensure every young person has the chance to earn or learn.

If adopted by the government, Britain could halve the number of young people neither earning nor learning, helping about 600,000 more under-25s into education, employment or training each year by 2036, according to the review.

Sebagaimana diketahui, milburn’s report comes as britain’s young bear the brunt of rising joblessness as employers freeze their hiring plans amid the fallout from the war in the middle east. Coupled with the legacies of the Covid pandemic and austerity, and a rise in mental ill-health and as AI upends the jobs market, the UK’s Neet rate has reached 13% – the highest level since 2014. Milburn said that rate could be lowered to 5% by 2036.

However, central to his plan would be a controversial shake-up of Britain’s benefits system to approach the under-25s as wholly separate from the working-age population at large.

Urging the prime minister not to shy away from welfare reform – after Keir Starmer was forced into a humiliating climbdown over a plan to cut disability benefits amid pressure from Labour MPs – Milburn warned the future of the next generation depended on the government making changes.

Berdasarkan laporan, at a press conference in london on tuesday to mark the launch of his report, he is expected to say: “it is time for a new settlement that makes work not welfare the future for the next generation. ”.

Berdasarkan laporan, burnham pledged on sunday to intervene as early as childhood to tackle youth unemployment. Writing in the Guardian, he promised that changes to benefits he was considering in response to Milburn’s review would only be accompanied by a “root and branch rethink” of youth support.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, at the heart of milburn’s blueprint would be the creation of an entirely new welfare system for young people, involving tougher eligibility criteria than for older claimants. In exchange, however, there would be a drastic step-change in support to help young people find work.

Berdasarkan laporan, this would involve some young people with health conditions and disabilities losing access to current benefits, although they would be able to apply to a local fund for short-term expenses and equipment. Those with the most profound health conditions who would be unable ever to work would still get more generous financial support.

To counterbalance the changes, Milburn said upfront investment to create a new “youth opportunity service” in England should be created to deliver a drastic boost in support for young people.

Sebagaimana diketahui, accountable to regional mayors and local leaders, the service would combine employment, careers, health and practical support. Young people would receive a personalised participation plan and a named adviser, with access to support guaranteed by two new legal guarantees.

While education, skills and health policies are devolved in Scotland, Wales and Northern Ireland, Milburn will say at the report launch that the underlying principles in his report should also apply.

Berdasarkan laporan, analysis in milburn’s report shows that for every £1 spent on helping young people into work or education, the state spent £25 on youth benefits last year. Under his proposals that figure would be rebalanced to £2 to £1, bringing Britain closer into line with the ratios in other European countries.

The changes will, however, raise fears among some Labour MPs as well as charities and campaigners that slashing youth benefits could result in plunging more young people into poverty, particularly for those who require additional financial support to manage health conditions.

As Milburn prepared to launch his review, backbenchers from the left of the party – including Nadia Whittome, Bell Ribeiro-Addy, John McDonnell, Apsana Begum, Clive Lewis and Richard Burgon – warned in a letter that an entire generation risked becoming disconnected from work and wider society.

“What young people need is not more punishment, but more opportunity,” the signatories wrote, warning that an approach relying on benefit cuts “risks further disenfranchising young people who are already struggling”.

Diungkapkan bahwa they added: “placing young people under threat of losing essential financial support does not address the shortage of good-quality jobs, the barriers facing disabled young people, or the lack of meaningful routes into employment. ”.

In a bid to ease concerns among Labour MPs after last year’s welfare rebellion threatened to rupture the party and arguably began Starmer’s downfall, Milburn held meetings with MPs on Monday alongside the work and pensions secretary, Pat McFadden.

Diungkapkan bahwa mcfadden told backbenchers: “what is proposed is a new settlement for young people. This is not last year’s proposal with better PR. It’s about bringing together the help young people need in one place – treating them as a person not a departmental client. ”.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, milburn said britain had faced a neet problem for 25 years and had never made a plan to end it before. “We are at a fork in the road and half measures will not do. A complete system reset is needed. A work generation is possible. A lost generation is not inevitable. ”.

Labour has faced fierce criticism from business groups who say its decisions – including tax increases and a rising minimum wage – have added to Britain’s crisis in youth jobs, while the Conservatives and Reform have pushed for a tougher approach on benefits.

Helen Whately, the shadow work and pensions secretary, said Milburn’s review was “too cautious on reversing that damage and too often his answer is the big and expensive hand of the state”.

Sebagaimana diketahui, “overall, it fails to bring down the welfare bill, proposes billions more in government spending and won’t make the slightest difference for young people stuck on welfare now – because nothing will happen for at least three years,” she said. “Even so, there’s a long road ahead to see if it can get past welfare-loving Labour MPs. ”.

Tanggal: 16 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.theguardian.com/uk-news/2026/nov/16/failed-uk-asylum-seekers-to-lose-five-day-grace-period-and-face-immediate-removal

Home Office plans will cause unnecessary distress and anxiety, say refugee charities.

Asylum seekers who have exhausted the formal appeals process will be stripped of a five-day grace period and become eligible for immediate removal under Home Office plans condemned as “distressing” by refugee charities.

Shabana Mahmood, the home secretary, will amend a bill currently before parliament to allow immigration enforcement officers to detain and remove people who have unsuccessfully appealed against their asylum or immigration claim being rejected without further notice.

Currently, enforced returns for rejected claimants can only take place after a minimum notice period of five working days, which can allow people to launch other legal interventions or prepare themselves for removal.

Imran Hussain, the director of external affairs at the Refugee Council, condemned the change.

Diungkapkan bahwa “we must treat people with dignity. Removing people at such short notice will cause unnecessary distress and anxiety,” he said.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, “we also need to look at the evidence of what works. If you assist people to return with dignity, many will take that option, at far lower cost to the taxpayer. The reality is that voluntary removals are far more effective at removing people than enforced returns. ”.

Louise Calvey, the executive director at Asylum Matters, said: “People deserve a fair chance to make their claim for help and sanctuary, but forcibly removing people from the country so they don’t get a chance to make their claims won’t fix that.

Diungkapkan bahwa “right now, 63% of the population don’t have access to an asylum legal aid provider. What that means is people are attempting to navigate a horrendously complex and hostile system in a new country, often in a second language. In that environment, many people may not have had the proper advice in initial claims, so many who make further claims are found to have a genuine need for support.

Sebagaimana diketahui, “expelling people from the country to ensure we never get to hear their legitimate claims is nothing to be proud of – it will lead to real injustices. ”.

Mahmood has tabled an amendment to the immigration and asylum bill that will scrap the five-day timeframe.

Officials would instead be given a six-month period to remove refused asylum seekers and rejected migrants before further notice is required, the Home Office said.

The changes follow a similar approach to the system that Denmark successfully operates, the Home Office has said.

The number of migrants awaiting removal in Denmark was cut from more than 2,185 cases at the end of 2020 to fewer than 1,000 at the end of 2025.

Diungkapkan bahwa the uk has increased the number of removals since labour came to power, but faces huge backlogs in asylum applications. As of 30 June 2026, 40,168 people were waiting for an initial asylum decision in the UK. The number of refused applications hit more than 90,000 in the same month, breaking previous records.

Berdasarkan laporan, there are currently exceptions to the five-day notice period for removals, such as where the removal was disrupted by the individual or was cancelled due to bad weather. In these scenarios, removal can be attempted again without further notice for 21 days.

This timeframe will now be increased to six months under reforms in the bill, which returns to the House of Commons for report stage and third reading on 17 November.

The bill will also introduce a new immigration appeals authority with the aim of speeding up removals and changes to how human rights and modern slavery laws are applied to asylum applications to root out what the government described as “vexatious” claims.

Ministers hope the bill will bring into force proposals that will create a firm but fair asylum system, and which will reduce the pull factors driving illegal immigration.

Under other reforms, the responsibility to make modern slavery decisions for children will be devolved to local safeguarding partners.

This will ensure professionals who already support the child, and are closest to the child, are making the decisions for their future, the Home Office said.

Diungkapkan bahwa anna turley, the minister for border security and asylum, said: “this government is ramping up removals of those with no right to be here, with over 80,000 illegal migrants and foreign nationals returned since the general election. “Now we are ensuring those migrants who have exhausted their right to appeal can be removed promptly, rather than being given an opportunity to frustrate their legitimate removal from this country. ”.

The Department of Health and Social Care (DHSC) has decided to extend Palantir’s contract to provide the federated data platform (FDP) – the software that links different healthcare providers – for two more years rather than exercise a break clause that would have let them axe it next spring.

Campaign groups such as Amnesty International and Just Treatment have been urging ministers to activate the break clause in February in the contract that NHS England agreed with Palantir in 2023.

Berdasarkan laporan, many nhs care trusts have declined to use the fdp, amid widespread doubts in the service that it is as good as palantir insists. Diungkapkan bahwa “the current contract will remain for two years, before coming to an end,” frith told mps. The DHSC will soon invite British tech outfits to bid to be part of whoever replaces Palantir. “A process this important must command public trust as well as clinical confidence,” Frith added in a tacit admission that many hospital bosses and doctors are sceptical about Palantir’s claimed benefits.

Sebagaimana diketahui, ben coleman, a labour member of the commons health select committee, who last week urged ministers to replace palantir with a group of british firms, said: “i’m glad the government is ending reliance on a single supplier and shaking off the palantir albatross. This must be done without disrupting patient care or creating new dependence [on a new single supplier]”.

Amnesty International said the decision was “a victory for healthcare workers, patients and campaigners who refused to give up”.

“Doctors and nurses … should never have to work in a health service that partners with a company supporting a military committing genocide.

Diungkapkan bahwa “palantir has openly acknowledged supporting israel’s military in ‘war-related missions’, while israel is committing genocide against palestinians in gaza. ‘First, do no harm’ should apply not just to NHS staff, but to the companies the NHS contracts with,” said Tom Guha, its crisis campaigner.

Labour grandee seems to have assuaged MPs’ nerves on need for welfare reform to tackle youth unemployment crisis.

In a boxing gym in Peterborough almost a year ago, Alan Milburn, freshly appointed to run a government review into the nearly 1 million young people out of work and education, said he would be “unafraid to shine a light on uncomfortable truths”.

The Labour grandee, who held three cabinet jobs under Tony Blair, warned there was a “downward escalator” taking young people into a “world of benefits” and vowed to provide radical solutions.

Berdasarkan laporan, many labour mps bristled. Just six months earlier, they had mounted a successful rebellion to kill off the government’s planned £5bn cuts to health and disability benefits, significantly damaging Keir Starmer’s political authority by forcing him into a U-turn on his flagship welfare bill.

That day in the gym, Milburn knew he would have to win over a party suspicious of his motives and anxious about the impact of changes on vulnerable people, even if some acknowledged that the growing welfare bill was unsustainable.

On the eve of publishing his report on Tuesday, early signs are that he has assuaged backbench nerves, succeeding where Starmer failed in moving the Overton window within the Labour party on the welfare debate around young people.

Diungkapkan bahwa milburn’s strategy was clear from the off: make the moral argument for change, make it loudly and make it often. His favourite – and oft-repeated – statistic has been that the government spends 25 times as much on benefits for young people as it does on supporting them into work.

Sebagaimana diketahui, in a series of interviews and mp engagement sessions over the following months, he described the projections – that numbers could reach 1. 25 million by the early 2030s without major intervention – as a “national failure” that would result in a “catastrophic” generational fault line.

After his interim report in May, he gradually signalled that overhauling health and disability benefits for young people would be a central outcome of his review, suggesting the welfare system in its current form had failed them and was exacerbating inactivity.

Labour MPs were given time to get used to the idea and to air the arguments in public, with controversial elements of the report released early – the abolition of health benefits for under-25s, including existing claimants, among them.

Berdasarkan laporan, “alan didn’t want any nasty surprises,” said one government source. The government can’t move forward on this unless it’s able to bring people with them. “He wanted to engage fully with MPs and charities and anybody else with concerns. ”.

Sign up for the Breaking News UK email to get newsletter alerts direct to your inbox.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, he had several factors working in his favour. As his days in No 10 ran out, Starmer was so weakened that Milburn was able to “bulldoze” Downing Street into supporting his proposals, according to another source, especially as Pat McFadden, the welfare secretary, was already onboard.

Secondly, several of the leading figures in the welfare rebellion were now inside government – most notably Louise Haigh, who is now Andy Burnham’s number two, and Anneliese Midgley, the chief whip.

Meg Hillier, the moderate chair of the Treasury select committee who had fronted that rebellion, last week indicated the proposals should get a “fair wind”, although she also acknowledged the difficulty of the choices ahead.

Thirdly, the drip-drip of pitch-rolling came alongside a wider sense of alarm in the UK over the prospects of the next generation, amid concerns over rising mental ill health, social media and AI upending the jobs market.

Burnham has said he wants to cut the welfare bill “as soon as we possibly can” but has warned against “crude cuts” (which the government would struggle to get past Labour MPs anyway) in the push for “sustainable” employment.

His approach has echoes of Tony Blair, who talked of “a hand up, not a hand out”, actively pursuing a policy of reforming and investing in welfare specifically to bring down what he termed the “bills of social failure”.

The big difference now is that the fiscal backdrop is more challenging, though Milburn will recommend that ministers spend hundreds of millions on back-to-work support in the short term in return for welfare savings, increased tax receipts and a fairer, happier country over the long term.

Diungkapkan bahwa the rather clunky symbolism of choosing a boxing gym for his first promotional visit last year wasn’t lost on anybody. Since then, Milburn – a former chair of the Social Mobility Commission – has been clear this is a fight he thinks the government needs to have.

His recommendations, along with those from the Timms review into health and disability benefits, which will be published in the coming weeks, will form the basis of a white paper next spring that will then become a new welfare bill, voted on by Labour MPs.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, so, for now, the campaign to win them over continues. Standing alongside Milburn at a meeting of the parliamentary party on Monday night, McFadden said: “What is proposed is a new settlement for young people. This is not last year’s proposal with better PR. ”.

Hatchlings emerge after discovery in September of first sea turtle nests ever to have been recorded on US west coast.

Two months after the discovery of the first sea turtle nests ever to have been recorded on the US west coast, the eggs have hatched – and California’s first group of 75 native-born olive ridley sea turtles have been released into the Pacific.

The eggs incubated at the Aquarium of the Pacific in Long Beach after the historic discovery of two separate nests in September at southern California beaches, a shift likely driven by this year’s El Niño conditions.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, on saturday, the aquarium of the pacific announced the turtles’ first emergence in a social media post: “the hatchlings are here! we are excited to share that some of the olive ridley sea turtle eggs from seal beach successfully hatched after a 58-day incubation period. Working with our partners, we carefully released them from the beach in the dark early hours of this morning. ”.

Sebagaimana diketahui, a day later, the aquarium added: “even more egg-citing news! a second group of olive ridley sea turtle hatchlings, this time from the huntington beach nest, was released into the ocean early sunday morning. ”.

In total, 54 turtles were released from the Seal Beach nest and 21 from the Huntington Beach nest.

Sebagaimana diketahui, on 16 september, an olive ridley sea turtle was observed digging a nest and laying eggs on seal beach in the first-recorded instance of any sea turtle nesting on the west coast. Three days later, a second turtle was spotted nesting on Huntington Beach.

Typically a tropical species, the olive ridley sea turtle normally resides in the Pacific, Indian and Atlantic oceans, but has been known to nest on the southern tip of Baja California.

“It is not known why these turtles chose southern California beaches as nesting sites, but it indicates an important historical change that could have long-term implications for the species and for local sea turtle management and protection,” the Aquarium of the Pacific said in a social media post.

Sebagaimana diketahui, “the behavior of these turtles was probably influenced, at least in part, by the incoming el niño, along with the recent tropical storm, range expansion, or perhaps navigational mistakes. The species is also known for its behavioral flexibility. ”.

As Hurricane Polo began to form in late September, researchers with the aquarium and its federal and local partners relocated the 204 eggs from the two nests to incubate in the safety of the aquarium’s animal care facility.

“As animals adapt in unexpected ways to changes in their natural world, humans will need to adapt and make space to ensure endangered and threatened species are given a fighting chance,” said Jeffrey Flocken, president and CEO of the Aquarium of the Pacific.

Diungkapkan bahwa “if they successfully hatch, these baby turtles will likely one day return to nest to carry on future generations on these very same beaches, giving us a remarkable opportunity to help a species expand its range and thrive. ”.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, even as the huntington beach and seal beach turtles have begun hatching and returned to the ocean, researchers are continuing to advise the public to be on the lookout for more nests. On 1 November, a third nest was recorded in Ventura county although those eggs were swept away by unusually high tides – likely also caused by El Niño.

#940. European-made pesticides named in 1,605 poisoning reports in Brazil last year

📅 17 Nov 2026

European-made pesticides named in 1,605 poisoning reports in Brazil last year

Tanggal: 17 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.theguardian.com/environment/2026/nov/17/european-made-pesticides-named-1605-brazil-poisoning-reports

About a third of cases involved chemicals banned for use on EU farms, according to investigation by Unearthed and Public Eye.

Pesticides sold by European chemical companies were named in more than 1,600 poisoning reports in Brazil last year, an investigation has found.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, about a third of the cases involved chemicals banned from use on farms in the eu because of the risks they pose to people and the environment. But European companies are not banned from manufacturing these chemicals, as long as they export them overseas to countries where they are legally allowed to be used.

Analysis of Brazilian health ministry data by Unearthed and Public Eye in a report published on Tuesday found that of 2,857 poisoning reports that named an identifiable agricultural product, 1,605 named brands sold by European pesticide companies.

Sebagaimana diketahui, farm workers in brazil have described their flesh rotting, skin burning, difficulty breathing and vomiting after using the chemicals at work, according to the report. A small number have died accidentally or killed themselves by drinking the pesticides.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, under brazilian law, reports must be submitted by healthcare professionals to brazil’s national disease notification system in all suspected pesticide poisoning cases. These reports can be marked “confirmed” poisoning or “exposure” only by the doctor or nurse who saw the patient.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, clinicians sometimes record cases as exposure when they lack the training or support to confirm a diagnosis, but are presented with a patient who says they have been exposed to pesticides or present symptoms of pesticide poisoning. Laboratory confirmation is rare, so recording a diagnosis of “confirmed” poisoning usually depends on clinical judgment.

Sebagaimana diketahui, experts say clinicians can be reluctant to confirm cases because of a lack of training or support. A brand being named in a poisoning report is not proof that it caused poisoning or death.

“The insufficient training of healthcare professionals to recognise and manage these cases is a major limiting factor,” said Vanda Garibotti, a public health biologist at the State Centre for Health Surveillance in Rio Grande do Sul, southern Brazil.

High staff turnover and a lack of institutional support meant poisoning cases were rarely confirmed through laboratory tests and often relied on clinical judgment, Garibotti added.

Diungkapkan bahwa in more than 6,700 medical reports involving agricultural pesticides last year, 2,857 named an identifiable product. Of those, 1,420 were classified as confirmed poisonings. A further 1,108 were classified as exposures; for the remainder the classification was unknown or other diagnoses.

Berdasarkan laporan, some of the products are made in britain. It contains diquat, a chemical that was banned in the UK in 2020 after experts concluded it posed a high risk to people living near fields where it was sprayed. Reglone is the most frequently cited UK-made weedkiller. Diquat is also found in other pesticides.

Despite the usage ban, Reglone is still manufactured by the Swiss-headquartered pesticides company Syngenta at its factory in Huddersfield for export to countries with more permissive regulations, including Brazil.

Diungkapkan bahwa nelson castoldi died last year after accidentally ingesting reglone on his family farm in rio grande do sul. To save money, his family had bought the weedkiller in bulk, decanting a single litre into an empty cola bottle to avoid hauling a heavy 20-litre canister into the fields.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, working under the scorching sun, castoldi mistook the black chemical for a soft drink and took a sip. Though he spat it out immediately, the chemical caused his kidneys to fail before attacking his lungs. He died two days later.

Sebagaimana diketahui, “we fell apart,” ivan castoldi said of his father’s death. She became depressive and had a stroke. “Four months after our father passed away, our mother also passed away. She cried day and night. She was left alone.

Berdasarkan laporan, “that poison, reglone, should be banned in brazil,” he added. “Not because of what happened to us, but because of its toxicity. ”.

The Brazilian health ministry recorded 75 cases involving diquat last year, compared with 36 over the five years from 2018 to 2022.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the investigation found reglone was specifically named in 44 reports, including four deaths. Of those cases, 26 were classified as confirmed poisonings and the rest were classified as exposure, unknown, or adverse reaction.

Dormex, a pesticide manufactured in Germany by Alzchem and distributed in Brazil by the German chemical company BASF, is another product workers said injured them or made them ill.

Sebagaimana diketahui, sidnei souza de oliveira, 49, suffered a severe injury after a jug of dormex spilled on his leg while he was filling a sprayer. The handle broke as he was transferring the chemical into the tank. At first, his leg turned red, and he continued spraying.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, he carried on working for four days before going to hospital. “After 15 days, my leg was black. Chunks of flesh were falling off,” Oliveira said. A doctor said the injury was serious and had to remove dead tissue to stop it spreading towards the bone.

Diungkapkan bahwa oliveira said the protective trousers supplied by his employer were thin and allowed the chemical to seep through. He said he had been afraid of losing his job if he stayed away from work for too long.

Berdasarkan laporan, dormex contains cyanamide, which was banned from use in the eu in 2008 because of concerns about its effects on human health, particularly among farm workers spraying the chemical. Analysis shows the Brazilian health ministry database recorded 17 confirmed poisonings involving Dormex last year.

Berdasarkan laporan, finale, a basf product identified in the investigation, contains glufosinate, which was banned in the eu in 2018. Roundup – a glyphosate-based weedkiller manufactured by the German chemical company Bayer – was frequently cited in Brazilian poisoning reports, including 12 deaths.

Sebagaimana diketahui, across all the poisoning reports identified by the investigation as involving products sold by european companies, there were 32 reported deaths. Of these cases, 31 were classified as confirmed poisonings, and 26 were recorded as suicides.

Berdasarkan laporan, syngenta products were cited 425 times in the poisoning reports, and basf 179 times. The company figures are not mutually exclusive: some poisoning reports named products sold by more than one manufacturer.

Nina Schrank, a senior campaigner at Greenpeace UK, said the findings were a “deadly double standard”.

Diungkapkan bahwa “if a pesticide is too dangerous to use in britain, it should be too dangerous to export. Ministers must stop allowing Britain to be part of a production line for toxic chemicals that are putting lives at risk overseas. ”.

Diungkapkan bahwa the eu’s pesticide approval system requires chemicals to meet strict standards for human and animal health and the environment. Cyanamide was withdrawn after an assessment found exposure among agricultural operators could exceed safe levels. Diquat has been banned on EU and UK farms since 2019 and 2020 respectively, after experts concluded it posed a high risk to workers, people living nearby and birds. Glufosinate, meanwhile, is classified in the EU as toxic to reproduction, meaning it can harm fertility or the development of unborn children.

Berdasarkan laporan, suicide prevention is also a factor. A 2020 study found national bans on highly hazardous pesticides could be a cost-effective intervention for reducing the number of people who kill themselves in countries with a high burden of suicides attributable to pesticides.

Diungkapkan bahwa a syngenta spokesperson said almost half the brazilian cases attributed to the company were not classified as confirmed poisonings, adding: “public eye and unearthed are aware of this but have explicitly chosen to disregard the dataset’s final classification. ” The company accused the investigation of disregarding the dataset’s final classifications and identified “numerous other inconsistencies” that it said raised “serious concerns” that the evidence was “being selectively interpreted to support a predetermined conclusion”.

Berdasarkan laporan, “there are real people behind these statistics. Every genuine case of poisoning matters, and every family affected deserves our concern,” the spokesperson added.

Sebagaimana diketahui, syngenta said brazil had its own “robust regulatory system” and that products banned in europe could still be independently assessed and legally registered in the country, citing differences in crops, growing conditions and pest pressures. It said it trained 95,000 people in Brazil in the safe use of its products in 2025, including through free online courses.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, bayer said its products were safe when used according to label instructions, citing what it described as rigorous testing and assessments by global health authorities. The company said it took pesticide poisoning seriously but questioned the reliability of the data, arguing that products and circumstances of exposure had not been independently verified, some chemicals may have been incorrectly identified and symptoms such as headaches and skin irritation could have other causes.

It said “Roundup” was “widely used as a generic term” that could refer to weedkillers made by other manufacturers or counterfeit products.

Berdasarkan laporan, the company said it provided training on the safe handling and use of pesticides, including protective equipment, and that its programmes reached more than 4 million people globally in 2025. It also argued that a pesticide being banned in the EU did not necessarily mean it was unsafe, saying other countries had robust regulatory systems that took account of local agricultural conditions.

Sebagaimana diketahui, it added: “while the data presented helps to provide information on broad trends of exposure, the data has limitations and warrants caution when drawing conclusions, particularly when looking at individual cases. ”.

BASF said it was deeply concerned by reports of poisoning that might be linked to its products, adding that it took all such incidents seriously.

A spokesperson said publicly available information suggested some incidents might have involved the intentional ingestion of crop protection products, describing such acts as “deliberate misuse” of products intended exclusively for agricultural use.

Sebagaimana diketahui, basf said it had global and local procedures to assess and investigate incidents potentially involving its products, and worked with authorities and experts where appropriate to understand cases and identify ways to prevent similar incidents. It said it invested in education and training to promote the safe handling and use of its products, with initiatives in Brazil reaching more than 14,475 participants in 2025.

The company said it was confident in the safety of its products when used in accordance with label instructions and applicable regulatory standards.

It added that Brazilian law required crop protection products to be handled and applied only by authorised and properly trained individuals, and said it took its responsibility for ensuring their safe use seriously.

Footage shows Ukrainian missile approach Crimea bridge.

Ukraine has severely damaged a critical bridge linking Russia to occupied Crimea, in what President Volodymyr Zelensky says was an "unprecedented operation" weeks in the making.

Images shared by Ukrainian officials show a section of the Crimean Bridge has collapsed into the water, dealing a logistical and symbolic blow to Moscow's war effort.

The Kremlin said it would rebuild the bridge "better than before" and that Russian President Vladimir Putin had been briefed on the overnight attack.

The bridge was built by Russia after it invaded and illegally annexed Ukraine's southern peninsula in 2014, and was personally opened by Putin in 2018.

Ukraine has long targeted the Crimean Bridge, which provides a road and rail route for Russian soldiers heading towards the front line, but has struggled to close it for good.

While Kyiv has been trying to increase the cost to Russia of waging war economically, by hitting oil refineries and depots, striking the bridge is an attempt to increase the political cost on Putin.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the timing of the strike comes at a significant moment, ahead of putin meeting the leaders of china and the us. This could cloud his moment back in the spotlight.

The damage after the overnight attack, involving missiles and drones, appeared to be far more severe than during previous strikes on the bridge, with a large arched section of the bridge apparently destroyed.

Video footage appeared to show critical damage to the road section, with remnants of the support arch and road deck seen protruding from the water below.

Zelensky said the strike was the result of a seven-stage operation by the military and security services, which saw Ukrainian forces "gradually destroy air defence systems, radars, electronic warfare equipment, and other designated targets on the way to the final objective".

He said several types of Ukrainian drones as well as the country's Flamingo and Neptune cruise missiles were fired overnight during a "pivotal stage".

The Ukrainian president also said the rail section parallel to the bridge's road had also been hit by a wave of drones, though images showed its supporting arch was still standing and a Russian-backed official said some rail services were operating.

Ukraine's state security service SBU said operations had "systematically suppressed enemy air defence systems" over a month, and said it showed "no Russian defence systems can guarantee the safety of illegal objects occupied by the invaders".

Meanwhile, Ukraine's military said the roadway on the bridge is "out of action", with no vehicle able to cross it, and the railway section is still standing, but with a damaged arch.

Berdasarkan laporan, russia's investigative committee confirmed structural damage and said it had opened a "criminal case. on terrorism charges" after attacks by "Ukraine's armed formations".

For the second day in a row, Russia recorded the biggest Ukrainian drone attack since the war began, with 2,256 drones downed, according to the defence ministry.

Zelensky had warned of major attacks in the days leading up to a meeting between Putin, Donald Trump and Xi Jinping in China's Shenzhen on Thursday.

There was heavy traffic in Kyiv on Tuesday after two major crossings were closed after strikes.

Elsewhere, Kyiv Mayor Vitaliy Klitschko said the Pivnichnyi (Northern) and Pivdennyi (Southern) bridges - key crossings over the Dnipro River - were closed after Russia hit Ukraine's capital overnight.

Loud explosions were heard in Kyiv just before midnight on Tuesday, with Klitschko saying shortly after that the city had suffered "damage to critical infrastructure systems" and disruption to heating and water supplies.

Eight major bridges span the Dnipro River connecting the western and eastern parts of Kyiv, and an estimated three million residents rely on the bridges to travel across the city.

Strikes on the busy Northern and Southern Bridges will cause major disruption to people's daily lives.

Elsewhere, three people have been injured in a Russian missile attack in the central Cherkasy region, according to local officials.

The long-term impact of the Crimean Bridge strike is still not fully clear though the risk of a serious transport and logistics crisis for the Russian military has increased significantly.

The collapse of the arched section has cut off the peninsula's direct road and rail links with Russia â at least until the crossing can be repaired.

However, there is still a land corridor running through the occupied parts of Ukraine's southern Zaporizhzhia and Kherson regions - though Kyiv has been systematically striking transport routes across northern Crimea, as well as bridges and other crossings in the area around Chongar.

This has already caused problems with the delivery of fuel and other supplies, including military cargo.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, there is a ferry crossing across the kerch strait, which connects the black sea with the sea of azov. It could partly compensate for the loss of the bridge, but its capacity is very limited and it is also vulnerable to attack.

Russia could also supply Crimea by sea, but this route is also risky, as Ukrainian naval and aerial drones operate extensively in the area.

In addition, debris from the Crimean Bridge â particularly its enormous arch â may have blocked the shipping channel.

This would make it harder for larger vessels to pass through and create further problems for the Russian-occupied ports in the Sea of Azov, including Mariupol and Berdiansk.

#946. Ukraine accuses Russia of targeting rescue operation after 'double-tap' strike kills 72

📅 17 Nov 2026

Ukraine accuses Russia of targeting rescue operation after 'double-tap' strike kills 72

Tanggal: 17 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/c30rk8x5g80qo?at_medium=RSS&at_campaign=rss

Ukrainian officials have accused Russia of targeting rescue and recovery operations two weeks after a deadly "double-tap" strike at a village close to the front line killed at least 72 people.

Ukraine says Russia carried out two attacks in succession on a humanitarian aid centre in the village of Komyshuvakha on 2 November - including the use of what it said was a 3,000kg (6,600lb) aerial bomb on a shelter where residents had fled for safety.

Verified images posted in the days after the attack show damage to emergency vehicles and excavation equipment at the site.

The State Emergency Service of Ukraine (DSNS) told BBC Verify there were multiple Russian strikes during the rescue.

The DSNS said three police officers, four workers and two rescue dogs were injured while five vehicles were damaged during the operation, which has now concluded.

With the DSNS saying the death toll had risen to at least 72 people, the attack on Komyshuvakha has become the second deadliest single incident of the Ukraine war.

Emergency service vehicles have also been targeted.

Oleksiy, an intelligence officer investigating the incident for Ukraine's SBU security service, who asked to be identified only by his first name, said rescue vehicles were "clearly marked" and accused Russia of "deliberately destroying humanitarian equipment".

Sebagaimana diketahui, he added the village's infrastructure and the people still living in komyshuvakha are also being systematically targeted by drones and bombs. Oleksiy accused Russian forces of "outright terror against civilians, against peaceful residents" to make life on the front line impossible.

Diungkapkan bahwa bbc verify has confirmed videos being shared by ukrainian police that show rescue workers at the scene shouting "drone, drone" and running for cover on the day after the 2 november attack. A group can also be seen treating a victim.

Sebagaimana diketahui, oleksiy said rescue crews operated under a constant threat of attack. "The enemy knows perfectly well that what is being carried out there is essentially a humanitarian operation to search for the dead," he said.

BBC Verify has asked the Russian Ministry of Defence for comment specifically about the Komyshuvakha attacks but has not received a response.

A general statement released on 2 November by the Russian MoD said it had targeted energy and transport infrastructure used by the Ukrainian military across the country.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, while there are no military or industrial facilities in komyshuvakha it is close to a key route used for ukrainian troop movements, supplies and evacuations. The village was previously reported to have been struck by the Russians on 28 October.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, local people headed to the shelter area on 2 november after being told by a local telegram group that aid would be distributed between 10:00 and 12:00 local time (08:00-10:00 gmt). Ukrainian authorities said an initial strike, at 09:45 local time, hit buildings above ground killing one woman.

Video shows moments between deadly Russian attacks on village in Ukraine.

Bodycam footage, released by Ukrainian police in edited segments and analysed by BBC Verify, shows people trying to free a casualty from the rubble before declaring she had died.

Throughout the footage, warnings of an impending second strike can be heard on police radios with increasing urgency until people are instructed to run to the underground shelter.

Berdasarkan laporan, the same footage, which was taken around an hour after the first attack, goes on to show people in a shelter. As they wait in silence a large explosion can be heard and the video goes dark.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, aftermath video filmed later shows bodies being recovered from a large crater immediately above the shelter. Twisted iron and rubble from the structure below can be seen beneath the surface.

Funerals have been held almost daily for the victims of the attack, including locals working to administer aid distribution, those seeking to collect it and soldiers who officials say arrived to assist with rescue efforts.

Trevor Ball, bomb disposal expert at intelligence firm at Armament Research Services, said a crater seen in the footage was consistent with the damage and depth left by a FAB-3000, a 3,000kg Russian bomb which can destroy underground structures.

His comments were echoed by Chris Proops, an ex-UK National Crime Agency investigator, who said the scale of the damage at the scene matched the size of the FAB-3000.

The remnants of the wing from a glide bomb guidance kit.

Ball and Proops both confirmed verified photos of munition fragments obtained by BBC Verify from Ukrainian authorities show part of a guidance kit that is compatible with the FAB-3000, which increases the weapon's accuracy and allows it to be fired from a greater distance from the target.

International law experts told BBC Verify that Russia had committed a war crime if it knowingly attacked rescue workers.

Ben Saul, professor of international law at the University of Sydney, said this "appears to be either a deliberate attack on civilians or civilian objects - a war crime - or an indiscriminate attack - also a war crime".

Diungkapkan bahwa prof samuel moyn of yale university said "directly targeting rescuers or their equipment is a gross violation of international humanitarian law". Precautions have to be taken to ensure that strikes target combatants rather than others, he added.

Additional reporting by Margaryta Maliukova, BBC Monitoring.
