#988. Ukraine hails attack on vital Kerch bridge linking Russia and Crimea – Europe live

📅 17 Nov 2026

Ukraine hails attack on vital Kerch bridge linking Russia and Crimea – Europe live

Tanggal: 17 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.theguardian.com/world/live/2026/nov/17/europe-ukraine-russia-crimea-kerch-bridge-attack-latest-news-updates

Zelenskyy praises ‘unprecedented attack’ as the Kremlin says bridge will be restored and will be ‘better than ever’ following strike.

Ukraine has critically damaged the Kerch bridge linking occupied Crimea with Russia in an overnight missile attack, in what Ukrainian officials say is a symbolic blow to the Kremlin.

Diungkapkan bahwa photos suggest that a 227-metre road arch span has fallen into the kerch strait, which connects the sea of azov with the black sea. The adjacent railway arch span has also sustained damage.

Diungkapkan bahwa ukrainian commentators say the massive steel arch cannot easily be replaced. The closure of the bridge means that traffic from Crimea can travel out of the peninsula only via a land corridor through occupied southern Ukraine, vulnerable to Ukrainian drones.

But Russian officials, quoted by Reuters, insisted that damage was only minor, and would be quick to sort out.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, “we have already gathered together the resources, designers, and builders ‌for repair work. We are sorting out logistics issues with the regional leadership,” Russian deputy prime minister Marat Khusnullin wrote on Telegram.

The bridge has in the past been a key supply route for Russian forces in Ukraine ​and is widely viewed as one of Russian president Vladimir Putin’s signature infrastructure projects.

The overnight strike followed ‌an intensification of ​Russian attacks in the ​past few months on bridges in Ukraine, including in the capital Kyiv.

Elsewhere, EU defence ministers are meeting in Brussels this morning for their latest discussions on Ukraine, followed by the Ukraine defence contact group.

Meanwhile, Germany’s chancellor Friedrich Merz is hosting Finland’s influential Alexander Stubb, two days before a major meeting of the coalition of the willing in Berlin.

Diungkapkan bahwa they will no doubt offer their reaction to today’s events in ukraine. I will bring you all the latest.

It’s Tuesday, 17 November 2026, it’s Jakub Krupa here, and this is Europe Live.

The Speaker of the Riksdag, Andreas Norlén, has said granted Ulf Kristersson’s request for more time for coalition talks (15:50) but that he wants to have clarity for the Swedish public by Christmas.

He said he would give parties one more week before he calls in the party leaders to decide what will happen next, but that he is determined to get to the end of this process soon so that by Christmas, Sweden will either have a new government or can prepare to go back to the polls with a second election.

Diungkapkan bahwa “my opinion is that this formation of government needs to come to an end in good time before christmas. I want that when the Swedish people celebrate Christmas they will know that Sweden either has a new government or are preparing themselves for another election. ”.

Sticking to the Swedish theme for a moment, Sweden’s defence minister Pål Jonson is the latest leader to stop by the journalists upon his arrival at today’s Ukraine Defence Contact Group in Brussels.

Diungkapkan bahwa in his comments, he said the meeting was “timely” as “the situation in ukraine is very challenging due to the fact that russia scaled up its production, both of ballistic missiles and also drones and glide bombs. ”.

Sweden will spend €4bn on helping Ukraine in 2027, Jonson said, noting cross-party backing across the parliament.

The minister also said that Sweden signed a letter of intent with Ukraine and the UK on the upcoming delivery of Gripen fighter jets for Ukraine.

Responding to questions from reporters, Jonson also said that the US undersecretary of defence Colby did not say “specific” information on the ongoing review of the US posture in Europe.

Berdasarkan laporan, “we are expecting it to come by the end of the year,” he said, adding that “the message is clear that europe is going to shouldering the lion’s share of conventional deterrence by 2028. ”.

Asked about the peace negotiations with Russia, the Swedish minister said he “has not seen any serious intent from the Russian side” on ending the war in Ukraine, stressing the need to keep supporting Kyiv in the meantime.

Jonson pointedly disagreed with Finland’s president, Alexander Stubb, who has repeatedly called for direct talks with Russia’s Vladimir Putin.

Diungkapkan bahwa asked if he sees any merit in that approach, he said:“not quite, because we do not see any serious commitment from the russian side to making any kind of compromise. ”.

Berdasarkan laporan, “i know there’s all kinds of ideas drifting around that we should also have a discussion about the european security architecture. We do not welcome that. ”.

In other news, after 65 days without a government, Moderates leader Ulf Kristersson has asked for more time before parliament votes on whether they want him as prime minister.

Two weeks after he was given the task to attempt to form a “middle” coalition government by the Speaker, he said on Tuesday afternoon that he had requested a few more days.

The Speaker will hold a press conference later this afternoon when he is expected to respond to the former prime minister’s request.

His announcement comes after the Centre party leader, Elisabeth Thand Ringqvist, asked Kristersson and the Social Democrats leader Magdalena Andersson to present a “total package” for her party to choose between after talks between the left-leaning parties failed to produce a result.

Berdasarkan laporan, she has already said yes to andersson’s proposal of a coalition between the social democrats, green party and the centre party with cooperation with the left party. But the Left party has since continued to demand ministerial posts, which the Centre party has refused to accept.

Sebagaimana diketahui, “a majority government that cannot agree does not work, so nothing would get done. A few more days are needed before a vote takes place, so that the Centre party can have a complete basis for decision making which is needed to take a position. ”.

If the vote on Kristersson does not lead to a government, parties have just one more attempt before another election will be automatically called.

Kristersson said he does not want another election, but is “totally prepared” for one and already has a team of people preparing in case.

Berdasarkan laporan, meanwhile, ukraine’s volodymyr zelenskyy has said kyiv is working on a prisoner of war exchange with russia, “one of the most important agreements reached at the trilateral meeting in abu dhabi. ”.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, he said ukraine would submit its proposals to the us, and could “deliver results in the coming weeks. ”.

“The timeline for implementing this agreement depends on how quickly the Russian side acts and on the American team’s communication with them,” he said.

Acting on the success of the humanitarian operations in Oleshky, Ukraine will also propose 10 other areas in the occupied parts of Kherson and Zaporizhzhia regions where similar actions are needed, Zelenskyy said.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, arriving earlier, uk defence secretary wes streeting – who co-chairs the group - said the meeting comes “at a critical time for the war in ukraine” in what he argued “has been a terrible year for vladimir putin. ”.

Sebagaimana diketahui, “russian casualties are [at] intolerably high levels as a direct result of his illegal and unnecessary war. The frontline isn’t moving, and Ukraine continues to show extraordinary resilience, courage and ingenuity. The economic costs on his economy and his own people have been catastrophic. And all of those lives and all of those, economic costs are coming with little to no gain. ”.

Berdasarkan laporan, streeting said the meeting was focused on “mobilising the support for allies … to see ukraine through what will inevitably be a challenging winter. ”.

Sebagaimana diketahui, “we’re all invested in the, attempt to negotiate a peace, and an end to this conflict that has to be on terms that are acceptable to ukraine. There can be no decision about Ukraine without Ukraine. ”.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, “i think we’ve just seen another example of ukrainian ingenuity and ukraine’s absolute determination to defend itself against russian aggression. We stand with Ukraine, as they do that. ”.

Just like Rutte, he said he expected “a number” of announcements from Ukraine’s allies to help Kyiv in the coming months today.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, over in brussels, the ukraine defence contact group is about to meet for their latest talks on ukraine, including the us undersecretary of defence, elbridge a. Colby.

Diungkapkan bahwa nato’s secretary general mark rutte just arrived and chatted with reporters, telling them he is “relatively optimistic” ahead of the meeting, hoping for “some good announcements this afternoon. ”.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, “a lot of people are working very hard to bring peace to ukraine. But in the meantime, we have to make sure that they have what they need to get through winter, that they have what they need to be as strong as possible in the peace negotiations. ”.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, on the kerch bridge, rutte said that “it’s important that ukraine defends itself. ”.

Berdasarkan laporan, “and that means also hitting out at logistical nodes; it’s unavoidable that they do that. … We have to see, of course, what exactly happened but at least [from] the media footage, it seems that they were successful. ”.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, rutte declined to comment on the peace negotiations, saying merely that “the us is playing a crucial part here. ”.

Diungkapkan bahwa “i think it’s good that europe is now at a table – that was one of the outcomes of abu dhabi – i think the europeans have organised themselves now quite well. ”.

Diungkapkan bahwa asked about the renewed starshield restrictions affecting ukraine, he said that “relevant parties are working very hard to make sure that as soon as possible, things are back to normal. ”.

Berdasarkan laporan, “i know that anyone who can be helpful here is working on this. ”.

Back to Ukraine, the Swedish armed forces have taken to social media with a post that appears to mock Russia following the overnight attack on the Kerch Bridge.

Sebagaimana diketahui, “bridges enable military mobility. Equally important is the protection of these important land corridors to avoid having to take the long way round. A strategic necessity in all operations, creating the preconditions for logistics, reinforcement and sustainment of forces. ”.

North Macedonia’s security agency said it had foiled a “terrorist” assassination plot targeting a person in neighbouring Greece and dismantled an Iranian-linked network, AFP reported.

The National Security Agency (ANB) said it had busted “a wide network of proxy actors” linked to Iranian Edris Jahangiri Mavaneh, who was a “collaborator of the Iranian security and intelligence services”.

The network, “under the direct instructions of the Iranian national, undertook preparatory logistical activities to carry out a terrorist act/assassination against a person in Greece”, the agency said.

The operation was led in cooperation with the Greek national intelligence agency, it added.

Four suspects have been remanded in custody and another placed under house arrest, interior ministry official Aleksandar Janev told local media.

Meanwhile, Slovakia looks set to host another round of governmental ⁠consultations with Russia in 2027, foreign ministry documents scrutinised by Reuters showed, ⁠continuing the ⁠direct talks ​held last month for the first time since Moscow’s invasion of Ukraine.

The latest round of talks in October centred on discussions over Russian energy supplies, as ⁠well as culture and agriculture, and resumed ​a process suspended ‌in 2022, Reuters noted.

Slovakia’s prime minister Robert Fico is a fairly regular guest in Moscow and has often faced criticism for his pro-Russian views and repeated call for engagement with Moscow, despite the continuing invasion of Ukraine.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the 140 successful candidates from serbia’s student list have just been sworn in as mps at the national assembly in belgrade. They took the oath en masse, alongside members of the long-governing Serbian Progressive Party (SNS), which now finds itself in opposition for the first time in 14 years.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, it follows the spectacular triumph of the student list in last month’s parliamentary elections. It comfortably defeated the SNS and its populist leader Aleksandar Vučić with a slate of candidates drawn from academia, athletics and economics, among other disciplines. None of the new MPs have any political experience.

Berdasarkan laporan, before the parliamentary session, student list supporters gathered outside the national assembly to cheer their representatives. Some of them performed the traditional kolo circle dance in celebration.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, meanwhile, there were jeers and whistles for arrivals from vučić’s party. A woman in the crowd poured a bottle of drinking yoghurt over the head of SNS candidate Lidija Vukićević, who said she felt “very bad” about the “primitivism and vulgarity” of Student List supporters.

Berdasarkan laporan, now the mps have been sworn in, the next task is to elect a parliamentary speaker. Whoever it is become the acting president of Serbia – because Vučić resigned as head of state to make his unsuccessful attempt to become prime minister.

Separately, former US president Joe Biden’s memoir, Promise Me, America, got published today, and it features some interesting lines on European affairs.

Just skimming the book for now, there is a bit of interesting background on the US response to the Russian invasion of Ukraine, and his secret visit to Kyiv in February 2023, as well as some of Biden’s unfiltered views on Ukraine’s Volodymyr Zelenskyy.

Diungkapkan bahwa “but i must admit that it could be difficult to work with zelensky[y]. As brave as he and the Ukrainians were, they tested our patience on many occasions, demanding more armaments and money. ….

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, zelensky[y] could be moody and stubborn in our private conversations, and not as grateful as i would have expected. That could be frustrating, and I let him know that in no uncertain terms. Still, I refused to cut and run on the Ukrainians, who possessed a tremendous fighting spirit. And so did Zelensky[y]. ”.

Berdasarkan laporan, in longer paragraphs on ukraine, biden writes he was “not blind to ukraine’s faults,” including “too much corruption” in the country’s judicial system, “where the rich and powerful were often free to buy their way out of accountability. ” “Ukraine would have to deal with these challenges if they wanted genuine integration with Europe and the West. ”.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, “but i had also seen the inner strength of the ukrainian people. If they could create a real democracy, with checks and balances, and fair elections, they could be a bulwark in the region, and an inspiration to peoples everywhere who were trying to claw their way out of a history of repression. They deserved a fighting chance. ”.

He also reveals that Donald Trump’s transition team after the 2024 elections wanted to get a permission to immediately start negotiations with Russia’s Vladimir Putin.

Sebagaimana diketahui, “during the transition, donald trump’s team had asked me to sign a letter empowering them to negotiate directly with putin, even before he took office. But I refused, unwilling to give them carte blanche for what I expected would be a kind of surrender, at Ukraine’s expense. ”.

Elsewhere, Biden also writes about his relationships with other leaders, including first foreign trip as president, to attend a G7 summit in Cornwall in 2021, noting his “bittersweet” feelings about “saying goodbye to an old friend, Angela Merkel,” while remarking how “impressed” he was by France’s Emmanuel Macron.

Sebagaimana diketahui, “[he] enthusiastically welcomed me into the group, but he asked hard questions about the rise of populism in the united states and how it might affect our long-term foreign policy. ”.

double quotation mark“When I said, ‘America’s back,’ he responded, ‘For how long?’”.

Diungkapkan bahwa writing about brexit, biden – who is of irish heritage on his mother’s side – expresses his frustration that the withdrawal from the eu was “threatening to undermine the good friday agreement of 1998, which had done so much good in bringing peace to northern ireland. ”.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, “i also disapproved of brexit for its ultranationalist claims, and for making many promises that could not possibly be kept. I believed that the populist leaders and opportunists who backed Brexit had sold the British people a false bill of goods. ”.

Finland’s Alexander Stubb just addressed reporters in Berlin, after meeting Germany’s president Frank-Walter Steinmeier.

Stubb said the upcoming meeting of the coalition of the willing in Berlin on Thursday will be “very important” for the peace process.

Sebagaimana diketahui, “i think it’s important that we get a structure and order in the negotiations, which basically means that there’s a clear timetable and that there’s a clear agenda. ”.

Diungkapkan bahwa “the process is not going to be fast, but i think it should be well structured. You cannot speak about security without Europe. … I think the key here is that you cannot speak about territory without Ukraine. ”.

Stubb also explained his approach to engagement with Russia, rooted in three key issues: geography, diplomacy and military.

Diungkapkan bahwa “we need diplomacy. If you don’t talk about peace, you will never get peace. And in order to be able to get peace, you need to have dialogue and conversation and diplomacy. … We believe that in order for you to have a diplomatic say in the geographic situation that you are in, you have to back it up with something. ”.

In Kyiv, Russian ballistic missiles hit the Northern and Southern bridges – two major transport arteries that cross the Dnipro river.

Traffic was also suspended, causing gridlock early on Tuesday morning.

Russia’s army confirmed it had hit both bridges in a “massive attack” on Ukraine’s infrastructure, AFP reported.

Hungary will suspend rail traffic between Hungary and Ukraine for two days after a Russian drone struck just hundreds of meters from a railway station in western Ukraine, Hungarian prime minister Péter Magyar said.

“Recently, in Transcarpathia, a Russian drone struck 300 meters from the Mukachevo railway station.

The Hungarian crew of the train arriving from Hungary has been taken off the train.

Sebagaimana diketahui, we are suspending rail traffic between hungary and ukraine for today and tomorrow. ”.

Mukachevo is just across the Hungarian-Ukrainian border on the Ukrainian side, in an area inhabited by many ethnic Hungarians.

Hungary’s foreign minister Anita Orbán – no link with that Orbán – offered a bit more detail on the incident.

“At around 10am Hungarian time, Russian Geran-2 drones attacked Transcarpathia in three waves, primarily targeting the areas around Mukachevo and Uzhhorod.

Sebagaimana diketahui, ukrainian air defence forces responded effectively and shot down several of the attacking drones. Unfortunately, reports have also come in of multiple drone strikes, and the extent of the damage is currently being assessed.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, this is not the first air attack against transcarpathia, and unfortunately it is unlikely to be the last. As Russia intensifies its attacks against Ukraine’s civilian population, we can expect further attacks of this kind against Transcarpathia as well, which until now has been relatively protected due to its geographical location.

Sebagaimana diketahui, ukraine’s civilian population is likely to face the most difficult winter of the war so far. The electricity grid and district heating systems are already in critical condition, particularly in Kyiv, Kharkiv and southern Ukraine. Russia is expected to intensify its attacks on power generation. Without electricity, water supplies in cities are also disrupted, millions of people are left without heating and power, and everyday life becomes increasingly difficult.

Berdasarkan laporan, i express my solidarity with the hungarian community in transcarpathia and with the entire ukrainian people, who have now had to face the horrors of war every day for nearly five years and are making extraordinary efforts simply to get through daily life. ”.

Let’s quickly go back to Ukraine for some news from Hungary’s prime minister, Péter Magyar.

#997. How new US chip restrictions on South East Asia will hit China

📅 17 Nov 2026

How new US chip restrictions on South East Asia will hit China

Tanggal: 17 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/cwq6e2qgvmlgo?at_medium=RSS&at_campaign=rss

Xi and Trump when they met in Beijing in May.

As US President Donald Trump heads to China, his administration has renewed efforts to curb Beijing's access to advanced semiconductors.

On Monday, Washington announced new interim rules that will increase scrutiny of data centre operators in Singapore, Malaysia, Thailand, Indonesia and Brazil.

The move not only restricts the export of advanced chips, but also access to their computing power, which Chinese firms currently rent abroad to train artificial intelligence (AI) models.

South East Asian countries in particular have invested heavily in data centres to power their AI ambitions - and Chinese firms seeking computing power overseas have been a key market.

Diungkapkan bahwa but now these firms will need a us government licence to buy advanced chips from nvidia or other american chipmakers. This allows Washington to monitor if those chips are being used to serve Chinese companies, or being smuggled to China.

Berdasarkan laporan, this poses a fresh challenge for beijing, which has become deeply dependent on compute from abroad in the wake of us export restrictions. At least 30% of China's advanced AI computing power is projected to come from renting overseas or smuggling in 2027, according to research by the Institute for Progress, external, a US-based think-tank.

China's foreign ministry called the new rules "economic coercion" and said Beijing "will take necessary measures to firmly safeguard its own legitimate rights and interests".

Diungkapkan bahwa this is also a problem for south east asian economies where large numbers of data centres have sprung up recently. Some of the firms behind them are accused of helping China evade US export controls on advanced chips.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, one of those is singaporean data centre firm megaspeed, whose former director alice huang is suspected of being a chinese spy. Calls for tighter export controls have grown after Nvidia's Jensen Huang admited to an affair with her and resigned as CEO.

Megaspeed, the biggest buyer of Nvidia's chips in South East Asia, is accused of illegally smuggling chips to Chinese companies after purchasing them for use in data centres in Malaysia, Indonesia and Thailand.

Berdasarkan laporan, the company has denied these allegations, defended its business as "legitimate and lawful", and said it has "retained external legal counsel to conduct a thorough internal investigation". It also said Alice Huang stepped down from her role as director in late 2023 and left the firm last year.

The US Commerce Department's Bureau of Industry and Security, however, has said Brazil and the four South East Asian nations "present a higher-than-normal risk of diversion" of the chips that Washington wants to keep out of China's hands.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the new measures are aimed at ensuring sensitive us technology "cannot be circumvented through remote computing arrangements involving data centers in third countries," the bureau added. Licences will be issued on a "case-by-case basis", it said.

Batam in Indonesia is emerging as a major regional data centre hub.

Countries like Malaysia and Thailand whose data centre roll out has been heavily driven by Chinese buyers could be hit hardest, says international trade expert Naoise McDonagh from Australia's Edith Cowan University.

But the new rules are unlikely to derail the data centre boom as a whole, says Reema Bhattacharya from advisory firm Verisk Maplecroft, adding that investment backed by major tech firms and clearly identifiable customers should "remain relatively resilient".

Diungkapkan bahwa singapore was an early adopter of data centres but when it began limiting new construction, investment flowed to neighbours malaysia and thailand. Johor in Malaysia and Batam in Indonesia have also approved billions of dollars worth of data centres to catch the spillover demand.

These countries have been offering incentives such as cheaper land to attract foreign investment, including from Chinese tech giants Alibaba and Tencent.

But now, the region could find it harder to get hold of advanced chips.

The BBC has contacted Indonesia, Malaysia and Thailand for comment.

Singapore said it is "engaging relevant US authorities" to understand the new rules better, and is "exploring how to facilitate trusted access" for local firms.

A spokesperson for Brazil's Ministry of Development, Industry, Trade and Services said it is aware of the US announcement and it "is closely monitoring any potential developments regarding this measure".

Malaysia previously said it welcomes data centre investment but "will not allow itself to be used to get around export controls".

The new rules also come just ahead of Trump's meeting with Chinese leader Xi Jinping in Shenzhen this week.

Beijing has made self-sufficiency in tech a national priority and needs the best chips to build powerful AI models.

Berdasarkan laporan, chinese firms deepseek and moonshot have come close to us rivals like anthropic and openai. So much so that The Institute for Progress estimates top US AI models lead the best Chinese platforms by only about six and half months.

"This is despite US AI companies having significantly better compute access and financing," it said.

Still, China needs advanced US chips to ensure its best AI models are competitive, experts tell the BBC.

The new restrictions on South East Asia and Brazil have taken away "one of the more practical routes Chinese AI developers had to accessing frontier computing power," Bhattacharya said.

But tighter restrictions could also push Chinese firms towards domestic semiconductors and further drive advancement at home.

That has been a longstanding dilemma for Washington, McDonagh said: whether to keep selling chips to China to retain its reliance on the US, or restrict access and risk further spurring Chinese innovation.

International investigation using trove of leaked internal data allegedly shows German bank overlooked compliance concerns to safeguard profits.

Deutsche Bank reportedly dismissed warnings about its dealings with risky clients, including high-profile Russian oligarchs, to protect profits, the findings of an investigation into a trove of leaked bank documents indicate.

A leak of 15m internal files is reported to show that the troubled German bank repeatedly ignored concerns by its compliance officers about its risk-taking, despite having already been caught being used to launder billions of dollars for Russian criminals, spies and oligarchs between 2010 and 2015.

The investigations, which were published by media outlets including Der Spiegel, the Financial Times, the New York Times and Le Monde, will represent a fresh blow for Deutsche Bank, which has struggled to repair its reputation after a number of scandals and dealings with controversial clients including the US president, Donald Trump, and the sex offender Jeffrey Epstein.

Berdasarkan laporan, deutsche bank said on tuesday that the issues raised in the investigations “date back many years, in some cases as much as two decades” and had been addressed by its leadership. “Where relevant, we reviewed these matters at the time and worked closely with regulators. ”.

However, the reports suggested Deutsche Bank prioritised profit ahead of internal controls, and continued to expand its Russian business until 2021, despite warnings from internal compliance officers and growing geopolitical tensions between Nato allies and Moscow.

Deutsche Bank allegedly resisted pulling out of Russia even after the Kremlin launched a full-scale invasion of Ukraine in February 2022, before the bank did a U-turn and exiting the country in March that year.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the investigations suggested deutsche bank was driven by competitive pressure, including from american banks, and that its chief executive, christian sewing, pursued a growth strategy that involved doing business with a list of customers known as its “most sensitive clients”. That covered roughly 50 corporate clients ranked by how close they were to the Kremlin, and other potential risks including financial crime, according to the Financial Times.

Some names allegedly on that list included: Russia’s state-owned gas company Gazprom; petrochemicals group Sibur; and oligarchs including the aluminium magnate Oleg Deripaska, the report said.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, outside its russian dealings, the german lender is facing fresh scrutiny for allegedly processing almost $600m (£454m) of suspicious payments linked to epstein, much higher than previously known. Deutsche said it “regrets [its] historical relationship” with Epstein and that it had made “considerable investments in strengthening controls”.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the lender is also accused of accidentally leaking trump’s tax documents to another client during his first term in office, which deutsche bank allegedly kept secret from the white house. Deutsche Bank said it did not comment on former or existing client relationships. Deutsche Bank cut ties with Trump in 2021.

The reports prompted a 4% drop in Deutsche Bank’s German-listed shares on Tuesday.

Deutsche Bank issued a public statement in response to the investigation on Tuesday, saying it had “gone through a fundamental transformation” under Sewing.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, “we made substantial investments in our control environment while restoring sustainable profitability, as evidenced by record profits in 2025 as well as in recent quarters. This involved €7bn of direct investments in our control environment between 2019 and 2025. ”.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the bank added: “we remain committed to ensuring continuous enhancements of our control environment and a culture of integrity and completing any outstanding remediation. ”.

Diungkapkan bahwa “regardless of how the information was obtained, it includes confidential information about clients, employees and other third parties, which remains legally protected. We have acted, and will continue to act, decisively to protect this,” the bank said.

#1000. Pretending to be in New Zealand, booking leave and buying consoles - the lengths fans are going to for GTA 6

📅 17 Nov 2026

Pretending to be in New Zealand, booking leave and buying consoles - the lengths fans are going to for GTA 6

Tanggal: 17 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/cm4gn9xnn1ppo?at_medium=RSS&at_campaign=rss

Grand Theft Auto 6 will feature a playable female character for the first time since the 2D games.

Grand Theft Auto fans have waited 13 long years for the latest edition of the game to be released - and going to extreme lengths to be ready for its launch.

GTA 6 will be released at midnight on Thursday - and Victoria Evans, from West Sussex, is not leaving anything to chance.

Diungkapkan bahwa she has her alarm set for 05:00 gmt, and has a day off booked. She says she put the game's release on her leave request form which was approved, she told BBC News, despite the fact her boss "doesn't know what GTA 6 is".

Sebagaimana diketahui, she's far from the only one. For the game's launch day, HR software company BrightHR, external looked at absence data from more than 1. 2 million employees from 70,000 businesses across the UK.

Diungkapkan bahwa it found gta was mentioned in 4. 6% of time-off requests by employees. Throughout November and December, it said an estimated 83,000 days had been booked off for the game.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, and booking leave is only one of the ways fans are making sure for the big day. Others are buying a new console to play it on or even pretending they're halfway around the world to get early access.

Berdasarkan laporan, market intelligence firm sensor tower estimates, external gta 6 has already generated $1. 18bn (Â£894m) from 12 million pre-orders - although Rockstar has not confirmed this.

Despite the option to preload the 212GB game, Jennifer Holmes, chief executive of the London Internet Exchange, said several UK internet providers including BT and Virgin Media had "increased capacity in anticipation of higher demand" ahead of launch.

GTA 6 - all you need to know about Rockstar's blockbuster game.

Gamers have long been known to book time off work for major releases.

When Red Dead Redemption 2 launched in October 2018, social media users were sharing plans to take the day off, with one analytics firm reportedly finding, external more people talking about calling in sick for it than any other game that year.

Similar conversations took place ahead of Cyberpunk 2077's release in December 2020, with fans discussing, external taking several days off to play.

GTA 6 is set in a fictional state inspired by Florida, which has featured heavily in the game's marketing, including this promotional blimp.

Some places have decided to lean into the trend for GTA 6 by offering incentives around the game - including the US Army's 3rd Infantry Division based at Fort Stewart, Georgia.

It gave some active-duty soldiers a four-day pass to play the game when it is released in November, as long as they sign a reenlistment contract for a minimum of two years between 1 August and 12 November.

"The idea was to have a unique incentives programme that connects to what soldiers are interested in," public affairs officer for the division, Lieutenant Colonel Angel Tomko confirmed to the BBC in August.

"There are 130 soldiers eligible within the battalion, and 20 have selected this incentive as part of their reenlistment," she said at the time.

Aside from taking time off, some gamers have also been discussing a technical loophole which could give them valuable extra hours of play before it officially unlocks in their country.

Because GTA 6 will release at midnight local time in all regions, New Zealand will become one of the first places where it is available, due to it reaching midnight earliest because of its position near the international date line.

This has led to some investigating ways to "trick" their consoles into thinking they're based in the island country when they are in fact thousands of miles away.

According to Google Trends, searches for the "GTA 6 New Zealand trick" have surged by more than 5,000% in the UK over the past month.

Games journalist Vic Hood said many gamers would be looking to play earlier to "get in on the action as soon as possible", as well as to prevent spoilers.

"As New Zealand is 13 hours ahead of the UK, that's 13 hours of gameplay that has time to spread across the internet and potentially spoil some key story beats and in-game surprises," she said.

"Took an extra day of paid time off when I found this out," one fan posted on Reddit on the trick.

It also means gamers would be playing the game at the much nicer time of 11:00 GMT, rather than having to stay up all night.

But another Xbox user shared caution on Reddit, noting that while the loophole had been exploited for many years for other game releases, GTA 6 "might be the game where Microsoft finally does something about this 'exploit'" - which could include banning players.

GTA 6's developers Rockstar and publishers Take Two Interactive have not commented on the loophole, and neither have Sony nor Microsoft.

Louise Wooldridge from Ampere Analysis said both Microsoft and Sony had "rules governing regional accounts and purchases" for the Xbox and PlayStation, adding that Sony's were "slightly more restrictive".

Players who choose to use the workaround could therefore risk breaching those terms and conditions and potentially face restrictions on their accounts or lose access to their digital games.

The hype for the game has taken over locations across the world, including Selfridges in London.

Some gamers will have to wait even longer than their console-playing counterparts to get their hands on GTA 6, as the game will not be available on PC at launch, similar to previous GTA releases.

"Spare a thought for the PC users who will have to live vicariously through others' YouTube videos and Twitch streams," gamer Stephen Finn told the BBC.

A PS5 now costs from Â£520, while the more powerful PS5 Pro is nearly Â£790.

Despite the hefty price tag, for some the temptation to join the community in playing what many have called the biggest game launch of the year, if not decade, has been too great.

Reddit posts and videos, such as one by US YouTuber isoish, external, show fans buying consoles specifically to play the game.

"So, the only game I'm going to have on here is GTA," the content creator said in the video.

After more than a decade of waiting, it seems some fans are determined not to waste a single minute of GTA 6's release - no matter the cost or extra effort.

Ukraine has critically damaged the Kerch bridge linking occupied Crimea with Russia in an overnight missile attack, in what Volodymyr Zelenskyy hailed as an “unprecedented” military operation.

Diungkapkan bahwa footage showed a ukrainian flamingo cruise missile seconds before it hit the road and railway crossing, followed by an explosion. The strike follows an earlier attack on Monday that targeted an arch across its central section.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, writing on social media, the ukrainian president described the attack as “a response to russian strikes on our infrastructure”. He said it was the culmination of a long and complex campaign to demolish the bridge, involving domestically produced drones and ballistic missiles. Palianytsia drones hit the road section of the bridge, while Neptune and other missiles targeted the adjacent rail section, he added.

Berdasarkan laporan, the ukrainian general staff said an arch and a span of the bridge’s road section had collapsed, severing the road link, while the railway line was still standing but its arch was damaged. Train travel across the bridge resumed on Tuesday after a brief pause.

Earlier, Russian forces struck ⁠two major bridges in Kyiv that straddle the Dnipro River late on Monday, along with some other critical infrastructure, amid drone ⁠and missile attacks ​across Ukraine.

Sebagaimana diketahui, ukraine has declared that the kerch bridge, built eight years ago after vladimir putin’s 2014 annexation of crimea and known officially as the crimean bridge, is illegal. It has repeatedly attempted to destroy it, using a truck bomb in 2022 and a sea drone strike the following year.

The latest drone and missile barrage appears to have succeeded after months in which Ukrainian unmanned systems forces have systematically knocked out the peninsula’s multi-layered air defences.

Berdasarkan laporan, the kremlin-appointed governor of crimea, sergey aksyonov, confirmed that road traffic on the bridge had been suspended. “We ask residents and visitors in Crimea to refrain from travelling toward the bridge and to take these restrictions into account when planning their routes,” he posted on Telegram.

Sebagaimana diketahui, photos on tuesday suggest that a 227-metre road arch span has fallen into the kerch strait, which connects the sea of azov with the black sea. The adjacent railway arch span has also sustained damage.

Sebagaimana diketahui, ukrainian commentators say the massive steel arch cannot easily be replaced. The closure of the bridge means traffic from Crimea can travel out of the peninsula only via a land corridor through occupied southern Ukraine, vulnerable to Ukrainian drones.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the debris appears to have blocked the main navigable route beneath the bridge, used by maritime traffic from the sea of azov and the ports of berdiansk and mariupol. But pro-war Russian commentators acknowledged that repairing the bridge would be very difficult, warning that, unlike in 2022 and 2023, Ukraine now had the capability to strike floating cranes and repair crews.

Diungkapkan bahwa ukrainian observers were gleeful at the bridge’s long-awaited destruction. They also pointed out that Ukraine’s armed forces could hit the bridge again to prevent repair work from being carried out. ”.

Diungkapkan bahwa the ukrainian blogger anton gerashchenko pointed out that putin personally opened the bridge in 2018, driving across it in a kamaz truck. “The Kerch bridge stands as the primary symbol of the Russian occupation of Ukrainian Crimea and the embodiment of its illegal annexation. It is Putin’s flagship project,” he wrote.

Sebagaimana diketahui, he added: “for years, russian authorities claimed the bridge was ‘the most protected facility in the world’. Consequently, every successful strike shatters the myth of the invincibility of Russian air defences – as well as the notion that Ukraine is incapable of reaching key targets deep behind enemy lines. ”.

Berdasarkan laporan, ukrainians celebrated on tuesday with memes. The company Fire Point, which manufactures the Flamingo missile, posted a popcorn emoji. Other social media users shared video of “Kerch Bridge on Fire”, a popular song by Saint Javelin which has become an anti-Moscow anthem.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, russian military bloggers were gloomy. One, Russian Engineer, acknowledged the Ukrainian military operation to paralyse the bridge had been “perfect”. Hundreds of unmanned aerial vehicles distracted Russian air defences, he said, before a clinical strike by ballistic missiles.

Sebagaimana diketahui, russia had already sharply restricted traffic across the crimean bridge. Moscow has largely stopped using the crossing for rail fuel shipments since the 2022 Ukrainian attack damaged the bridge and set a fuel train ablaze.

Sebagaimana diketahui, rybar wrote that the latest strike would force moscow to “completely overhaul” its supply routes to crimea, shifting more traffic to the novorossiya highway. Russia would also have to step up the installation of protective netting along the route, Rybar added, lamenting that the measure had not been introduced in the spring.

Diungkapkan bahwa meanwhile in kyiv, loud explosions could be heard as russian forces struck two bridges over the dnipro river. The mayor of the Ukrainian capital, Vitali Klitschko, wrote on Telegram that according to “preliminary information, there have been hits on the north and south bridges in ⁠the capital”. There were water and power cuts in parts of the city, he added later.

Russian forces launched a ​series of attacks on bridges crossing ‌the river earlier this ‌month and in October.

A Russian missile attack injured three people ‌in the region of Cherkasy and also targeted Kharkiv, Ukraine’s second biggest city, local officials said on Telegram.

Russia’s defence ministry claimed ⁠on ⁠Tuesday its ​forces had ⁠carried out a massive ⁠overnight strike ​on ‌Ukrainian ‌military-industrial facilities, ‌transport infrastructure in Kyiv and Zaporizhzhia and the ‌Cherkasy and Dnipropetrovsk regions.

The ministry ​said the strikes also ⁠targeted energy facilities, ​port infrastructure ​and ​vessels ​used ‌by ​Ukraine’s armed ​forces.

Russian defence ministry data from Monday showed that an overnight Ukrainian drone barrage was the biggest since the start of full-scale war in 2022.

Zelenskyy also said on Monday ⁠that Ukraine had held new online talks with the US presidential envoys ​Steve Witkoff and ​Jared Kushner, as well as European ​representatives, on the prospects of ending the war with Russia.

Berdasarkan laporan, kushner ​said progress had been ‌made towards an ​agreement, though important ​challenges remain to end the war, which russia started by invading ukraine in february 2022. Moscow annexed the Black Sea Crimea peninsula in 2014.

#1003. Ukraine Attacks Kerch Bridge Linking Russia to Occupied Crimea

Ukraine Attacks Kerch Bridge Linking Russia to Occupied Crimea

Tanggal: 17 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.nytimes.com/2026/11/17/world/europe/ukraine-kyiv-russia-kerch-bridge-crimea.html

Destroying the structure, the only one connecting Russia to the occupied Crimean Peninsula, has long been a top objective for Kyiv.

Marc Santora, who has covered the war in Ukraine since 2022, has written about each Ukrainian attempt to bring down the Kerch Strait Bridge.

For years, Ukraine has had a bull’s-eye on the only bridge linking the occupied Crimean Peninsula to Russia.

Berdasarkan laporan, after moscow used crimea as a springboard to launch its all-out invasion of ukraine in 2022, kyiv bombed the bridge that year with explosives hidden in a truck. The next year, Ukraine attacked it with unmanned naval vessels. Two years after that, it dispatched covert operatives to try to bring the bridge down by planting explosives on undersea support pillars.

Berdasarkan laporan, the 12-mile-long structure, the kerch strait bridge, survived it all, a powerful if scarred symbol of moscow’s control of crimea, which russia illegally annexed in 2014. But before dawn on Tuesday, Ukraine struck probably its biggest blow yet, sending a significant section of the bridge into the sea after a series of drone and missile attacks.

Sebagaimana diketahui, in a statement about the bridge, the ukrainian military command said, “russia built a myth around it as a symbol of crimea being ‘russian forever. ’”.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, “now,” the statement added, “part of the structure lies in the water. ”.

Diungkapkan bahwa the ukrainian government released photographs and video documenting the attack and aftermath. The New York Times also verified social media video showing the collapse of a central span of the bridge used for vehicle traffic.

#1005. Trump says Alaska voters chose the wrong Dan Sullivan. What does the data show?

📅 17 Nov 2026

Trump says Alaska voters chose the wrong Dan Sullivan. What does the data show?

Tanggal: 17 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/cxnv4jlr269eo?at_medium=RSS&at_campaign=rss

Almost two weeks after the Democrats swept to victory in the midterm elections, votes are still being counted in the race to elect a senator in Alaska, with Democratic candidate Mary Peltola ahead of her Republican rival - Senator Dan S Sullivan.

This Senate contest has drawn scrutiny after another Dan Sullivan entered the race earlier this year - with ballot papers listing both the incumbent Dan S Sullivan and a Daniel J Sullivan Jr.

Republicans have said this could have confused voters, prompting an unsuccessful legal challenge and President Donald Trump claiming votes for "the fake Dan Sullivan" were supposed to be for "the real Dan Sullivan".

US media has not forecasted a winner in the race - the last Senate seat still without a winner after the 3 November election.

But with 98% of the vote counted, even if Senator Dan S Sullivan's votes were combined with Daniel J Sullivan Jr's votes, this would still not overcome Peltola's lead.

Berdasarkan laporan, alaska uses a ranked-choice voting system, which means voters can vote for five candidates in order of preference. If no candidate reaches more than 50% of the first preference votes, then voters' other choices will be used to decide who wins.

Diungkapkan bahwa bbc verify has analysed voting data showing voters' second choices. It shows that over a third of voters who put Daniel J Sullivan Jr first left their second choice blank.

The next highest second-choice preference was for the Democratic candidate Mary Peltola - receiving nearly twice as many second-choice votes as the Republican Dan S Sullivan.

This calls into question claims that Republican voters may have been confused about which Sullivan they were voting for.

Why midterm vote-counting is taking so long in America's largest state.

Republican Dan S Sullivan has held the US Senate seat in Alaska since 2015 and was running for his third term.

Daniel J Sullivan Jr - a retired school teacher from a remote fishing village in Alaska - entered the race in May and has run a low-key campaign.

A New York Times story, external published the week before Election Day claimed that Democratic operatives with links to the Peltola campaign had tried to recruit "spoiler" candidates in the Senate race, including Daniel J Sullivan Jr.

Berdasarkan laporan, the report said it had seen text messages and interviewed 12 people who participated in or were told of the plan, or were would-be candidates who the team also tried to recruit. The BBC has not independently verified the reporting.

Peltola has denied all knowledge of the alleged "scheme" and Sullivan Jr has denied any links with the Peltola campaign.

President Trump has posted multiple times on Truth Social since the election, claiming that the race has been "rigged".

But experts note it's not an illegal tactic, if it was employed.

"There is nothing to prevent a campaign from recruiting someone else to run, even if for political reasons," said Joshua Douglas, an election law expert at the University of Kentucky.

Alaska Senate candidate denies knowing about alleged plot to put two Dan Sullivans on ballot.

Senator Sullivan was joined by President Trump at a campaign rally ahead of the vote.

Voters in Alaska select their first choice candidate, followed by options to rank up to four other candidates in order of preference.

Berdasarkan laporan, "there is no specific law preventing people with the same name running, but many states have laws or regulations about how names appear on the ballot. One of those regulations was used in Alaska" said Ruth Greenwood, director of the election law clinic at Harvard Law School.

On Alaskans' ballots the two Sullivans were listed as:.

Sebagaimana diketahui, - sullivan, dan s. (Registered Republican) Incumbent.

There was a second registered Republican candidate, Gerald Heikes - who was also allegedly recruited into the race according to The New York Times.

A sample ballot for the US Senate election in Alaska.

Diungkapkan bahwa as of tuesday, peltola holds 49. 98% of the vote.

Berdasarkan laporan, in the event that peltola were not to clear 50%, officials eliminate the candidate in last place and reallocate those ballots to the voters' next choices. This process continues until two candidates remain, with one clearing the 50% hurdle.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, daniel j sullivan jr is the listed candidate in last place with 1. 65% of the vote.

Democrat Mary Peltola's said on Saturday she will "decisively be elected" as Alaska's next senator.

Senator Dan S Sullivan and his allies have accused the Democrats of trying to confuse voters.

Trump said last week: "Anybody that voted for that second Dan Sullivan, the fake Dan Sullivan, was supposed to be a vote for the real Dan Sullivan".

Of the ballots analysed by BBC Verify that ranked Daniel J Sullivan Jr first, 38% of them recorded no valid second choice.

We do not know how many of these voters may have thought they had voted for the Senator Dan S Sullivan and then not ranked any other candidates.

A further 29% of Daniel J Sullivan Jr voters ranked the Democratic candidate Mary Peltola second, almost double the 15% that ranked the incumbent Republican Senator Sullivan as second.

Sebagaimana diketahui, "the likelihood that any confusion might play a significant role is diminished in alaska," richard pildes, a professor of constitutional law at new york university, argues, "because any voter who was unsure which dan sullivan candidate they meant to vote for could rank them first and second. ".

Additional reporting by Daniel Wainwright.

#1006. Serbia’s Student List candidates sworn in as MPs after election triumph

📅 17 Nov 2026

Serbia’s Student List candidates sworn in as MPs after election triumph

Tanggal: 17 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/nov/17/serbia-student-list-mps-sworn-in-election-triumph

Inaugural parliamentary session comes as ousted populist Aleksandar Vučić threatens mass protests of his own.

Candidates for Serbia’s Student List, the grassroots movement of political outsiders that pulled off a spectacular victory in last month’s elections over the party of the populist leader Aleksandar Vučić, have been sworn in as MPs as they begin the process of forming a government.

The 140 candidates – among them academics, lawyers, scientists and the odd actor – were sworn in on Tuesday during the inaugural session of the new parliament, bringing 14 years of rule by Vučić and his Serbian Progressive party (SNS) to an end.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, before the parliamentary session, student list supporters gathered outside the national assembly to cheer their representatives. Some of them performed the traditional kolo circle dance in celebration.

Berdasarkan laporan, meanwhile, there were jeers and whistles for arrivals from vučić’s party. A woman in the crowd poured a bottle of drinking yoghurt over the head of the SNS candidate Lidija Vukićević.

Sebagaimana diketahui, a caretaker government under the outgoing prime minister, ðjuro macut, will remain in office until mps approve the student list’s choice of a cabinet. For now, its makeup – including the identity of a future prime minister – remains unclear.

Diungkapkan bahwa sarah el sarag, a human rights lawyer and mp-elect, said the wider student movement continued to be active in the process of selecting the cabinet, along with the candidates themselves. “All the time, we are doing it together. “We are there because of them,” she said of the students. ”.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, parliamentary planning sessions had helped prepare the candidates, she said. We are lawyers, doctors, professors – and it is the first time for us to do this kind of job. “We have been having meetings and exercises for the parliament almost every day, because none of us are professional politicians. ”.

Diungkapkan bahwa the sessions reflect the student list’s efforts to pre-empt sceptics who question whether a group of candidates with no political experience is equipped to govern. Members of the movement that selected El Sarag and her fellow MPs have reiterated that all are experts in their professional or academic fields and are better qualified than many of the people who served as ministers or MPs under Vučić.

Sebagaimana diketahui, el sarag said her colleagues had a good idea of what to expect from tuesday’s opening session. “People who have had some experience of politics have been making some simulated exercises for us,” she said.

She would not divulge the identity of the candidate for speaker – who will become Serbia’s acting president – let alone the name of the next prime minister.

The most pressing stories and debates for Europeans – from identity to economics to the environment.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, vučić is not accepting his new role as leader of the opposition meekly. Since the election, he has accused the Student List of instituting a regime of “naked terror” by directing “submissive prosecutors and police” to carry out unlawful detentions.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, police and prosecutors have made a series of arrests of people with links to the sns. Last week, prosecutors targeted the owners of a well-connected construction company over a project on the site of the once-famous Hotel Jugoslavija, which was hit during the 1999 Nato airstrikes on Belgrade.

Sebagaimana diketahui, that followed the arrest of the owner of alta bank, which held the concession for processing bill payments on behalf of serbia’s state-owned electricity company. Others facing charges include senior police officers accused of abuse of office, and people suspected of vote rigging and violence during the elections.

After the two years of protests which culminated in the SNS’s defeat at the ballot box, Vučić is threatening major protests of his own.

Raša Nedeljkov, the programme director of the Serbian election and democracy monitor CRTA, said the first disruptions could come during parliament’s inaugural session.

Diungkapkan bahwa “we can expect a lot of sabotage, a lot of obstruction, a lot of circus-creating atmosphere,” he said. “If we see such scenes in parliament – including some kind of physical obstruction – that’s something which would not surprise me. ”.

Berdasarkan laporan, in such an atmosphere, speed may be of the essence, he said. MPs must approve a new cabinet within 90 days of the national assembly’s inaugural session but will be motivated to name a PM well before that deadline.

#1007. BBC launches programme for children forced from school by bandits and poverty in West Africa

📅 17 Nov 2026

BBC launches programme for children forced from school by bandits and poverty in West Africa

Tanggal: 17 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/c3pw450ndyjqo?at_medium=RSS&at_campaign=rss

Hadiza left school at 13 to get married and now spends her time doing housework.

Diungkapkan bahwa as she pounds millet, 15-year-old hadiza sings the english alphabet. It is a reminder of something that she desperately misses - going to school.

"Sometimes I write on the ground to practise and see if I'm still writing correctly," she says.

One night, about two years ago, a group of armed men raided her village.

Sebagaimana diketahui, "they scared our cattle away and abducted a girl. We had to run away. We walked barefoot all the way here," she says.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, since then she has lived in a displaced persons camp in goronyo, a few kilometres from her home. For a short while she went to school here, but soon met a young man and, at the age of 13, stopped going to classes and got married.

"It's tradition here that once a girl is married, her education ends," she explains.

Now she lives with her in-laws and helps look after the home.

Although Nigerian law prohibits marriage under the age of 18, it is not always enforced.

Hadiza practises writing on the ground to make sure she doesn't forget the English alphabet.

Diungkapkan bahwa hadiza is one of nearly 19 million children in nigeria who are missing out on an education, according to estimates shared by unesco in 2024. That's about one in four of the country's school-age children.

Against this backdrop, the BBC World Service has launched Dars Hausa, an educational programme in the main language spoken in northern Nigeria, as well as neighbouring Niger, Cameroon and elsewhere in West Africa.

Diungkapkan bahwa it brings english, maths and science lessons to children across west africa, via social media, local television partnerships and radio. Many people in the region get their news from the radio and nearly half of households in Nigeria have one, according to the charity Save the Children.

Sebagaimana diketahui, dars means "lesson" in pashto and dari, and it was first launched in those languages in 2023 for afghan children barred from attending school. An Arabic version followed in February 2025.

Diungkapkan bahwa the reasons why so many nigerian children are out of school are numerous and complex. Like Hadiza, 12-year-old Rukayya also lives in the displacement camp in Goronyo.

After Rukayya's father was killed, she gave up school to earn money instead.

"It pains me to see other children studying and going to school while I cannot," she says.

As the eldest child, each day Rukayya goes out to gather firewood to sell and to beg so that her younger siblings can have something to eat.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, "if my father was alive, i wouldn't have to go out and beg," she explains, saying some people mock her "but it doesn't stop me because it is our only way to survive. ".

Bandits killed her father about a year ago in front of her, she says, and her family fled from their home to the camp.

She and Hadiza are among 670,000 people in north-west and central Nigeria who have been forced from their homes by armed robbery and kidnappings, according to the International Organization for Migration.

Three Girls: Lessons in Limbo features the stories of Hadiza and Rukayya - you can watch the full film on YouTube, external.

Some attacks have been carried out by militant Islamist groups, but the majority in this region are by criminal gangs, known in Nigeria as bandits, who steal, kill and kidnap.

The school that Hadiza once attended in Goronyo is the only one serving children in the camp and typically has about 50 students in each class.

One of the teachers, Kamilu Sulaiman Jakada, says that even though lessons are free, only a tiny portion of the children attend, and even then sporadically, because parents tell him that "it is the children that are the breadwinners" and they need to earn money to eat.

Armed gangs, poverty and lack of funding all have a huge impact on children's education, says teacher Kamilu Sulaiman Jakada.

He says the school does not have enough teachers or classrooms, explaining that funding is inconsistent and often comes from individuals or organisations rather than the government.

Berdasarkan laporan, the other challenge is the bandits. A gang once came to the school on motorbikes, shooting in the air, he says, and although no-one was hurt, many parents were scared and withdrew their children. That has been parents' reaction to attacks in some other parts of the country too.

Diungkapkan bahwa every nigerian child is meant to get nine years of free, compulsory education - six in primary and three in secondary school. Responsibility is shared between federal, state and local governments.

But many schools are facing shortages and poorer families who cannot afford private education can struggle to pay for uniforms, books and transport.

The crisis has built up over decades, with successive governments struggling to address chronic underfunding and poor oversight of resources.

In addition, many children in the traditional Almajiri system, which provides Islamic education, are not taught subjects such as maths and science, and are considered by Unicef to be out of school.

Many of Nigeria's schools face shortages of teachers, classrooms and learning materials after years of underfunding and lack of oversight.

Minister of State for Education Prof Suwaiba Sa'id believes the number of children out of school is lower than has been reported, but admits that with Nigeria's growing population "the proper investment, the proper oversight, has not been doneâ¦ I will not mention the names, but we know of two states that did not recruit a single teacher for eight years".

Berdasarkan laporan, she says that education is the government's "number-one priority" and initiatives such as lumina are designed to help address "decades of neglect". Lumina aims to support one million girls by 2030, providing an accelerated learning programme for older girls who have missed years of formal education.

She also says that "the government is doing everything possible" to deal with bandits and that "we have seen children that should be at school but are engaged in this banditry".

Sebagaimana diketahui, in the meantime, it is children like hadiza and rukayya that the bbc world service dars hausa programmes aim to help. Hadiza says she still has a dream to one day become a doctor "to help my fellow women".

Sebagaimana diketahui, dars hausa will air on bbc news hausa radio on sundays at 06:45 west africa time, with a repeat at 20:45. The programme will also be available via BBC News Hausa's digital platforms, including YouTube, Facebook, X and Instagram.

#1008. Asylum seekers on final ‘one in, one out’ UK-France flight feel they are being ‘punished’

📅 17 Nov 2026

Asylum seekers on final ‘one in, one out’ UK-France flight feel they are being ‘punished’

Tanggal: 17 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.theguardian.com/uk-news/2026/nov/17/asylum-seekers-one-in-one-out-uk-france-smugglers

Many of those onboard are being deported for second time after fleeing threats from people smugglers in France.

Many of the asylum seekers on Tuesday’s final “one in, one out” deportation flight are people who returned to the UK fleeing threats from smugglers after they were already forcibly returned to France.

Hundreds of asylum seekers who were sent back to France are thought to have returned to the UK, citing threats from smugglers who said their families still owed them money for the Channel crossing.

Berdasarkan laporan, asylum seekers who spoke to the guardian described being punched, beaten or raped by the smugglers. Some said smugglers had caught them while they slept on the streets and forced them to work for them in conditions of modern slavery in a migrant camp in Calais, cleaning the smugglers’ tents and carrying water or firewood.

The charity Medical Justice, which has provided support to people detained for one in, one out, called the pilot scheme “a disaster”.

The one in, one out scheme involved forcibly returning hundreds of people who had travelled to the UK on small boats to France in exchange for bringing a similar number from northern France to the UK to claim asylum.

Diungkapkan bahwa one asylum seeker with a ticket for tuesday’s flight said he was captured by the smugglers after being returned to france by the home office earlier this year. He said he was a political dissident in Iran, and believed he would be executed if he was returned there.

Sebagaimana diketahui, “i came back to the uk a second time because the smugglers caught me in france,” he said. “I was sleeping on the streets in Paris because France did not accept my asylum case.

Berdasarkan laporan, “many of the people who have tickets for tuesday’s flight are people like me, who came back to the uk a second time. I believe that 100%. I believe those of us who came back to the UK a second time are being punished by being sent back to France a second time. ”.

He said that although the Home Office stated that sufficient lawyers were available for asylum seekers detained for France, he and others had struggled to access good quality legal advice.

Sebagaimana diketahui, “friends paid privately for a lawyer for me. The lawyer promised me that 24 hours before the flight, they would challenge my removal, but he has done nothing,” he said. “They do not even answer the phone although I have tried to call them 10 times.

Berdasarkan laporan, “my mind is broken. I am scared that when I am returned to France on Tuesday, the smugglers will catch me and kill me.

Berdasarkan laporan, “when the guards came to take me to the plane for france last time, three or four of them surrounded me and made me feel like a criminal. I have committed no crime apart from coming to UK to claim asylum.

Sebagaimana diketahui, “when i slept on the street last time the weather was warmer in france. Now it is too cold to sleep outside. I don’t know what I’m going to do. ”.

Sign up for the Breaking News UK email to get newsletter alerts direct to your inbox.

A second asylum seeker with a ticket for the flight, who also returned to the UK after being sent back to France, said he knew of dozens of people due to fly on Tuesday.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, “all of us have bad solicitors who are not helping us,” he said. “One in, one out finished on 1 October. I do not understand why the Home Office wants to continue sending us to France. ”.

John Tuckett, the independent chief inspector of borders and immigration, said in a report published last week that it was not known how the Home Office would measure the success or failure of the one in, one out scheme, despite it being given the highest operational priority, with regular updates supplied to ministers and 10 Downing Street.

Berdasarkan laporan, he cited a ministerial submission which stated that the aim of the scheme was to demonstrate that dangerous journeys on small boats were not a viable option for entry into the uk, with the aim of undermining the organised immigration crime model. Since the scheme ended on 1 October, 4,786 people have crossed the Channel in 69 small boats, according to government data.

A Medical Justice spokesperson said: “One in, one out has been a disaster, causing avoidable suffering to a vulnerable group and it has failed in the Home Office’s stated objective.

Sebagaimana diketahui, “the home office must start to learn lessons and put an end to dangerous detention conditions. ”.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, seema syeda, of the joint council for the welfare of immigrants, said: “the uk government has forced people fleeing war, climate breakdown and persecution to take murderous and traumatising journeys across the channel, only to treat them with brutality once they have arrived here, retraumatising them with detention and deportation. ”.

A Home Office spokesperson said: “We welcome the inspector’s recognition of the strong operational delivery of the UK-France pilot, which successfully demonstrated that a returns arrangement of this kind can work.

“The message was clear: if you returned to the UK after being transferred to France under the pilot, you would be sent back.

Diungkapkan bahwa “the pilot has now concluded and we are taking forward lessons learned as part of wider efforts to strengthen returns. Any future operational decisions, including on evaluation and reporting, will be considered in the usual way. ”.
