#1009. Taking Korea's toughest exam from behind bars

📅 16 Nov 2026

Taking Korea's toughest exam from behind bars

Tanggal: 16 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/cmewvxg855yno?at_medium=RSS&at_campaign=rss

The boys in Mandela have been convicted of serious offences.

Students intently focus on maths formulas written on a board before lowering their heads and taking notes as the teacher works through a sum.

The teacher's voice and the scratch of pens fill the room.

At first glance, this could be any classroom in South Korea.

But thick metal bars cover the windows and the students are wearing blue prison uniforms and rubber shoes emblazoned with the words "Korea Correctional Service".

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, this is mandela boys' school, an education facility for young prisoners inside the seoul southern correctional institution in guro, south-west seoul. In South Korea, young people who are sentenced to imprisonment by a criminal court must serve their time in prison.

"The boys here have committed serious offences and received criminal sentences," Jeong Yeo-gyeong, a correctional officer in the Korea Correctional Service's social reintegration division, told the BBC.

Diungkapkan bahwa "as well as theft, there is a high proportion of serious offences, including violence, bodily injury, sexual violence and robbery. ".

But by opening educational institutes like Mandela, authorities are hoping to give these young offenders a chance to better their lives after they serve out their sentences.

Opened by the justice ministry in March 2023, it allows boys who were aged 17 and under when their sentences became final to prepare for school equivalency exams as well as the Suneung - the country's notoriously difficult university entrance examination - while still serving their sentences.

Held every November, the Suneung is an infamous eight-hour marathon of back-to-back exams.

Students attempt about 200 questions across various subjects, which include Korean, maths, English, social and natural sciences, among others.

The country itself comes to a standstill - construction work halts, planes are grounded and military training gets suspended to facilitate an optimal testing environment.

A total of 551,864 people have applied to take this year's Suneung on 19 November.

Around 30 prisoners are enrolled in the Suneung preparation class at Mandela Boys' School, and 11 of them have applied to take this year's exam.

Several boys are sitting the Suneung exam this year and are taking intensive preparation classes.

Park Soo-young (not his real name), a 17-year-old inmate, has been at the Mandela Boys' Suneung preparation class for two months and hopes to study social welfare.

He tells the BBC that he had dreams of becoming a police officer before committing the crime that landed him behind bars.

Diungkapkan bahwa he says he could not bring himself to look properly at his mother during his trial. When he turned towards her after his sentence was announced, she was crying.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, "seeing her like that, i broke down too. I wondered how I was going to live from then on, and how I could look after my mother, who was on her own. I think I kept crying for about a week while I was in the detention centre. ".

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, looking back on his offence, he says he feels "very ashamed that i couldn't control that impulse". If you do, everything will be different. If he could meet his younger self, he would tell him: "Control that impulse. ".

Sebagaimana diketahui, "i'd grab myself by the collar and shake myself as i said it. ".

He hopes the Suneung and university will offer him a chance to start again.

Sebagaimana diketahui, "once i'm out, i need to cut ties with the friends and people i used to know and start a new life. Going to university would let me leave the area where I used to live, move somewhere else and start something new. That's why I began studying again. I think university is the only way to do that. ".

But he describes beginning Suneung preparation as "a struggle every day".

Berdasarkan laporan, "but the teachers don't let anything slip past. They keep helping us until we understand. If I don't understand something, I put my hand up and they come over and explain it.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, sometimes, if i've missed something, i keep working at it on my own. If I still can't get it, I ask the students next to me to explain," he said.

Sebagaimana diketahui, park's day begins at 06:30 with a morning check by prison officers. He starts memorising English vocabulary and working through Korean reading passages early in the morning.

Diungkapkan bahwa "i learn english words whenever i can, even before breakfast. We have to come down to the classroom at 08:00, so we have another check and then come down for lessons. From 07:00, I work through a Korean passage, something like literature or speech. ".

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, during breaks, students make calls to their families or leave the classroom for scheduled visits. In the evening, they return for supervised study. Once the day's activities are over, they must go back to their cells together.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, park says he studies until 22:00 before finishing for the day. If he wants to study longer hours, he needs permission from a prison officer.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, but even if gets a good result this year, park will not be allowed to leave prison and attend university straight away. He is only due to be released in 2028, but plans to use this exam as experience and continue studying next year.

Berdasarkan laporan, "this time, i want to experience how the suneung works and how competitive it is. Then, next year, I'll work hard from the start so I can get in the year after that. ".

By opening educational institutes like Mandela, authorities are hoping to give young offenders a chance to better their lives.

Some former students from Mandela Boys' School have managed to get into university, according to the justice ministry.

Others have continued their studies after leaving prison, including by enrolling in residential exam preparation academies.

Berdasarkan laporan, the inmates are taught by a team of seven prison officers, all of whom hold teaching certificates. Each is responsible for a subject.

Sebagaimana diketahui, visiting instructors provide classes in the humanities, arts and sport, while university student volunteers help with learning. Professional psychological counselling is also available.

Berdasarkan laporan, park min-yong, who applied to work here in 2023, teaches science. And alongside Suneung lessons, he works with the students' to change their habits and behaviour.

One thing he often tells them is that they need to "learn how to become adults".

He believes that while studying in itself does not necessarily turn inmates away from a life of crime, the experience of having worked hard at something: staying with a concept that makes little sense, revisiting a wrong answer and continuing even when grades do not improve straight away, is valuable in itself.

"Studying properly means pushing yourself to your limits, and that takes considerable stamina and patience," he says.

Berdasarkan laporan, "whether they chose to do it or not, the experience of persevering, enduring and not giving up easily may help them to some extent when they face the difficulties of life after release. ".

He says the material they encounter while preparing for the Suneung also gives them new things to think about.

Diungkapkan bahwa korean reading passages cover literature, society, science and philosophy. Students have to consider a character's perspective, examine the evidence behind an argument and understand unfamiliar concepts. They also encounter explanations that differ from their own and have to reconsider what they think.

"They gradually learn that it's not just about their own personal view - that these concepts and relationships have been developed through a shared understanding among many people," Park said.

Park says students sometimes cheat in classroom tests even while he is watching.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, "they cheat as if it's nothing. They give each other answers, even when I'm watching them. There may be an element of doing it deliberately, but often they haven't thought it through. Some repeat it after being told off. They don't think about the impact their actions or words could have on others. ".

The boys also have a strong desire for recognition, he says.

Sebagaimana diketahui, "it's all the time. 'Look how much I've done. I've done this much - haven't I done well?' They're always like that. Look how much my grades have improved. They're hungry for it. ".

Park Min-yong teaches science to the boys in Mandela.

Not everyone agrees with this initiative though.

One criticism is that young people who have not committed crimes also face fierce competition for university places: so there is some anger that the state provides offenders with separate education and opportunities to prepare for this exam.

Father Jeong Min-ha, of the Archdiocese of Seoul's correctional ministry committee, worked with Seoul Southern Correctional Institution from September 2023 until last year.

Diungkapkan bahwa "studying gives them a sense of achievement and time to look seriously at their own lives. I think that is the most important part of rehabilitation. That's why I think it matters. ".

Park recalls a student who had done well at the school but later returned to prison.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, "he was doing well when he left, but in the end he came back. I'd hoped he would carry on with what he'd been doing here, but he couldn't. That's disappointing. So something went wrong. ".

Berdasarkan laporan, according to the justice ministry's 2026 corrections statistical yearbook, 35. 7 times the overall rate of 21. That was about 1. 5% of prisoners aged under 20 who were released in 2021 were imprisoned again within three years. 2%, and the highest of any age group.

Diungkapkan bahwa but park hopes the students will continue learning after they leave prison. "We don't know what the outcome will be," he says.

Berdasarkan laporan, "they say the way to clear a glass of dirty water is to keep pouring clean water into it, rather than trying to remove each bit of dirt. I hope they fill their minds with good things, learn to use their energy and intellect in the right way, and put that learning into practice at the right time and place. ".

#1010. Ed Miliband announces first sanctions on Israeli firms working in West Bank

📅 17 Nov 2026

Ed Miliband announces first sanctions on Israeli firms working in West Bank

Tanggal: 17 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/nov/17/ed-miliband-israel-west-bank-settlements-sanctions

Move is designed to hinder building of more illegal settlements, which Foreign Office says Israel has ‘refused to clamp down on’.

Ed Miliband has announced the first set of sanctions against Israeli companies planning to build illegal settlements in the West Bank, after he pledged to try to prevent settlements that destroy the chances of a two-state solution.

The UK foreign secretary also announced he was placing sanctions on a rightwing activist Israeli group involved in trying to block aid into Gaza as recently as last month.

Miliband announced the measures just before tenders for the large E1 West Bank settlement were due to be allocated by the Israeli government, while saying he wanted to work with a new Israeli government in a more cooperative way.

Israel’s possible new prime minister, Gadi Eisenkot has said that, if appointed, he will take a tougher approach than Benjamin Netanyahu to settler violence.

The sanctions are designed to stop the flow of finance to eight identified construction firms, although in practice the extent to which any of the firms are dependent on British finance is yet to be tested.

Diungkapkan bahwa on 8 september, miliband announced an expansion of its global human rights sanctions regime, as well as a complex set of measures, yet to be implemented, designed to ban the trade in goods from illegal settlements. The Foreign Office said that it welcomed and encouraged trade with “green line Israel” and firmly distinguished this with activity in settlements.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the foreign office said the current israeli government had “not only refused to clamp down on illegal settlement, but has facilitated and encouraged them”. More settlements had been approved under the four years of this Israeli government than in the previous 20 years.

The entities targeted by sanctions are Israeli construction, property development and architectural businesses that have helped to plan, build, supply or market housing and public infrastructure in Israeli settlements in the occupied West Bank.

Miliband – who was criticised by some for broadening the sanctions criteria and planning a ban on trade with illegal settlement – said: “Protecting the two-state solution is the north star of this government’s approach.

Sebagaimana diketahui, “that is why my message on e1 is clear: do not bid, do not build, and do not profit from the destruction of the two-state solution. The status quo in the West Bank and Gaza is unacceptable. And we will not stand by while those blocking desperately needed aid deepen the intolerable suffering of civilians in Gaza. ”.

Sebagaimana diketahui, but he added in a potential olive branch: “we are committed to working productively with a new israeli government and the palestinian authority to advance lasting peace and security for israelis and palestinians alike. ”.

Diungkapkan bahwa miliband and his middle east minister, stephen doughty, have repeatedly highlighted the israeli government’s refusal to let a variety of dual-use goods into gaza. The Foreign Office said civilians in Gaza were in desperate need of winter supplies, with catastrophic floods leaving nearly 4,000 households without shelter and 1. 4 million people living in tents or makeshift shelters.

Sebagaimana diketahui, according to the un, more than 150,000 tents and 300,000 tarpaulins bought by humanitarian partners and donors are outside gaza ready to go in, but are being held by the israeli authorities. The Israeli authorities also continue to block timber from entering, leaving no emergency shelter kits available in Gaza.

Diungkapkan bahwa the israeli government claims the blockage of some goods is necessary to prevent hamas obtaining items that could be used to attack israel. The dispute over dual-use goods and closed entry points into Gaza has lasted for more than two years.

These Ukrainians Aren’t in Combat. But They Deal With War Every Day.

Tanggal: 17 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.nytimes.com/2026/11/17/world/europe/ukraine-war-civilians.html

This Ukrainian doctor works near the front, trying to save wounded soldiers.

This man has buried more than 1,200 soldiers.

This therapist tries to help damaged veterans heal.

Diungkapkan bahwa this forensic pathologist once helped to solve crimes. Now he identifies fallen soldiers.

Diungkapkan bahwa mykhailo biliak has spent most of his life in the funeral business, and he no longer remembers how many graves he has dug. “The worst day was six funerals,” said Mr. But he knows he has buried more than 1,200 soldiers in Lviv, in western Ukraine, since Russia started its full-scale war in 2022. Biliak, 62.

Diungkapkan bahwa hundreds of miles to the east, in a basement near the front line, daryna boiko, a 32-year-old anesthesiologist, prepared to attach an iv drip to a soldier wounded by a drone. “It was scary out there,” he replied. “It won’t be scary,” she assured him. “It’s fine here. ”.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, in kyiv, the capital, hanna buraho, a 53-year-old psychotherapist, made tea after a session with a group of soldiers. “When the war started, everyone rushed to help each other, and every person wanted to do something of their own, so this is my contribution,” Ms. More than 5,000 service members have been through her rehabilitation program, which uses horses. Buraho said.

Berdasarkan laporan, in odesa, in southern ukraine, two morgue workers pushed open the heavy, rusted doors of a refrigerated rail carriage that contained the remains of dozens of soldiers killed in battle. A white bag was placed on an autopsy table, and Ruslan Fedoniuk, 61, a forensic pathologist, turned to his work.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, none of these people carry weapons. But like Ukrainians across the country, they deal with the war and its consequences every day.

Diungkapkan bahwa lychakiv cemetery, the oldest in lviv, has been a place of sorrow for countless families. Biliak, it is a workplace. For Mr. He is the first to arrive at a gravesite, and one of the last to leave after he and his colleagues shape the mound of earth over it.

#1012. India has been named a ‘destination of the year’ for 2027 – here are insiders’ tips on travelling beyond the tropes

📅 17 Nov 2026

India has been named a ‘destination of the year’ for 2027 – here are insiders’ tips on travelling beyond the tropes

Tanggal: 17 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/nov/16/is-is-india-travel-boom-travel-and-leisure-women

As tourism booms, three experienced female travellers give their take on how to make the most of travelling here.

Don’t get This is India delivered to your inbox? Sign up here.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the 13th-century persian scholar zakariyya al-qazwini never travelled to india. But he catalogued it in his famous work The Wonders of Creation and Rarities of Existence, which drew on accounts of a distant land filled with “rarities par excellence”. For al-Qazwini, as Helen Pfeifer writes in the London Review of Books, wonder was not an emotion but an intellectual method of making sense of the world and acquiring knowledge.

Sebagaimana diketahui, india has long occupied such a space in the global imagination, as a land of extraordinary riches; spirituality, customs, chaos and contradictions. This has shaped how the country is perceived from afar, but it can often flatten its complexities.

Berdasarkan laporan, so when, last week, travel + leisure named india its destination of the year for 2027, i found myself considering what it means that the country holds such multitudes. The magazine’s recognition will undoubtedly add to its growing appeal as a travel destination. But expectations built around India can differ from the experience of being there, particularly for women.

Berdasarkan laporan, my own experiences of travelling in india largely surround my work as a journalist, often visiting places that would never make it into a travel guide. I remember the towering chinar tree outside the home of a woman in Kashmir whose son had been killed in an encounter with the security forces; the rolling hills of Odisha, where we travelled to meet a guerrilla fighter; the tiny hut in Chhattisgarh where, after a 13-hour journey, our team found a meal of rice and lentils. These scenes have stayed in my mind, for their landscapes as much as for the stories and circumstances.

Diungkapkan bahwa ultimately, such experiences were far more illuminating than those from a conventional travel itinerary, and taught me to navigate uncertainty and embrace discomfort. For this week’s newsletter, I spoke to three women about the journeys in India that stayed with them and what travelling here has meant to them.

One of the most memorable journeys for travel writer Shivya Nath was a trek through the Tirthan Valley in Himachal Pradesh, with a crew of local women.

Diungkapkan bahwa trekking has always been a male-dominated industry and nath, author of the book rootless and restless, was struck by the personal journeys of the women leading the expedition. (She travelled with an organisation which trains women to become guides, overcoming social and family restrictions. ) “For some of the women, spending even two nights away from home required negotiating with their families,” she told me.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the route wound through dense forests in the great himalayan national park, across ancient bridges, over gushing, undammed rivers, accompanied by the soundtrack of birdsong. “The only sounds you hear are of nature,” she recalled. Along the way, they stopped to forage lingri, a seasonal wild fern used in regional cooking, which they later prepared at a riverside camp they set up for the night.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the following morning, the group hiked to a waterfall, standing together on a large rock in the middle of the cascading water. Being with “just a group of women who love being in the outdoors, was a really powerful feeling for me”, she said.

Diungkapkan bahwa for afsha sethi, a corporate leadership professional from bengaluru who has travelled extensively in india, one of her most cherished travel experiences is an unlikely one. As part of an extracurricular project when she was in high school, students were paired with a local community through an NGO. She spent a week shadowing a farming family growing rice and areca nut in Karkolli, in northern Karnataka.

Diungkapkan bahwa walks through lush forests with waterfalls were a daily routine. “We would come back with leeches on our legs, and then put salt to get rid of them,” she recalled.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the trip also brought her into contact with something she had not encountered before. When her roommate told the host family about getting her period, their sleeping arrangements were shifted to the courtyard. “It turned out to be a great experience, because the weather was very nice and [we were] looking at the stars and just chatting late into the night,” she said. It reminded her that travelling through India can mean encountering different social conventions.

‘The moment somebody puts up something on Instagram, everyone throngs to it’.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the travel boom in india is led by domestic travellers. 95bn domestic tourist visits in 2024, a jump of 17. The country recorded almost 2. 5% from the previous year, according to recent government data. Overall, India ranks 31st in the World Economic Forum’s Travel and Tourism Development Index 2026, up eight spots since 2024.

Women accounted for 43% of foreign arrivals, an interesting counterpoint to India’s reputation as a challenging destination for female travellers.

Sebagaimana diketahui, but the boom raises questions about what happens to the places being discovered. “I think one of the most basic things travellers can do is to avoid geotagging locations. “Social media has definitely accelerated the over-tourism problem,” says Nath. ” She suggests choosing community-owned tourism initiatives that allow local people to benefit directly from visitors.

Sebagaimana diketahui, nayanika gaffino, a mother and recreational athlete who has also clocked up the miles around the country, has seen this happen first-hand in goa, where she lives. “The moment somebody puts up something on Instagram, everyone throngs to it … even though it doesn’t have the capacity to handle so many people,” she says, adding there are beaches her family now avoids because of this.

Berdasarkan laporan, travelling with girls, gaffino also has to consider practicalities such as hygiene and access to clean public toilets and safety. As such, she gravitates towards boutique properties that are accustomed to hosting families with children.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, nath acknowledges that solo travel can require extra vigilance. On solo trips, she prefers family-run homestays or guesthouses where someone is aware that she is on her own and can watch out for her. At the same time, she adds, India can be an intensely hospitable place where people generously invite you for tea or a meal.

Sebagaimana diketahui, discovering a place, she says, should also include finding ways to preserve the very qualities that led you to it in the first place. The journeys the women described involved seeing a side of India that differed from their own expectations. This is what makes al-Qazwini’s understanding of wonder relevant for me. To approach something with wonder is not to be impressed by just beauty or uniqueness but to have a curiosity about what it might show us – its possibilities and its limitations.

Niha Masih takes a look at the stories, ideas and news makers of modern India.

Diungkapkan bahwa politics | more than one-third of the international delegates – about 115 people – expected to attend the congress party’s bharat summit over the weekend were denied entry to india or had their visas cancelled, according to the wire. Congress described this as an attempt to stifle voices of criticism, while the foreign ministry said that visa-related decisions are “sovereign functions” but did not share further details.

Diungkapkan bahwa lawsuit | the us state department has served summons in a civil lawsuit brought by khalistani separatist leader gurpatwant singh pannu against national security adviser ajit doval and former research and analysis wing, samant goel, according to the hindu. The foreign ministry described the lawsuit as “frivolous”.

Berdasarkan laporan, culture | a 50-year-old navaratri festival at wesleyan university, in connecticut, has made it an unlikely home for carnatic music and dance traditions. Although such festivals take place at cities around the world, few institutions have become as significant a platform for Indian music and dance.

A recommendation from someone with great taste.

Sebagaimana diketahui, shaunak sen, director of the academy award-nominated all that breathes, recommends: “if you find yourself in the oft-trodden window of wanting to watch something for an hour after dinner, but feel drowned in the mediocre flotsam of the big streamers, i have a suggestion watch the strangely inventive short films of the artist-bureaucrat sns sastry from the 1960s and 70s [on youtube]. I Am 20, which interviewed young adults born in the year of India’s independence, is an inquiry into a certain national zeitgeist. Between the candour of the participants and the sharpness of their complaints, one can scarcely believe this was made under the aegis of the government. Unlike the regular pedantic state films of the time, Sastry somehow created avant garde, surreal, even funny films, funded by the Films Division of India. ”.

Diungkapkan bahwa firecrackers were responsible for most of delhi’s fine particulate matter of pm 2. 5 – about 71% – in the hours after Diwali celebrations, according to a first-of-its-kind assessment by the Indian Institute of Tropical Meteorology. The national capital reported its most-polluted Diwali since 2021, data from the Central Pollution Control Board showed.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, ai anxiety is everywhere. The situation becomes more complicated when one of their children takes a job at an AI company. Bhasin’s mockumentary is about three retired men in a small Indian town who, persuaded that artificial intelligence is taking over human jobs, fight back by impersonating household appliances. Pranav Bhasin’s comedy We Were Here has brought that to screens in a short film that is making an impression internationally. One becomes a dish antenna, another a vehicle’s reverse camera and a third a microwave. “Do you want artificial intelligence?” “No, I have real one,” goes one caustic exchange.

The New Yorker released the film on YouTube and it’s eligible for Oscars consideration after winning at the Palm Springs International ShortFest.

#1014. Ministers vow to create new welfare system for young people as they back Milburn report

Ministers vow to create new welfare system for young people as they back Milburn report

Tanggal: 17 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.theguardian.com/society/2026/nov/17/alan-milburn-report-young-people-work-neets-job-support-savingsalan-milburn-plan-young-people-work-neets-savings-200m-a-year

Author of long-awaited report says money saved in benefit cuts will mostly be used to fund new job support system.

Alan Milburn has said his plan to get more young people into work will save the government only £200m a year as the cost of job support swallows up almost all of the anticipated cuts to benefits.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the former health secretary unveiled his long-awaited report into youth unemployment on tuesday morning, urging ministers to cut disability and sickness payments for under-25s and invest the money in back-to-work schemes. Figures contained in the report show that his plan will not deliver significant overall savings.

The figures are likely to be seized on by the Conservatives as evidence that Labour is not serious about reducing the welfare bill – something the opposition party has put at the heart of its economic policy.

Diungkapkan bahwa but they will bolster the arguments of milburn and the prime minister, andy burnham, that the year-long review has not been motivated by cuts. “The system I propose will spend less on compensating for economic inactivity, more on creating routes out of it; less on the consequences of failure and more on avoiding it,” Milburn said in the report.

Sebagaimana diketahui, he told labour mps at a meeting on monday night: “the tories will say it’s too expensive, you can cut faster. But you can’t – or you’d drive young people into destitution with poor housing and ill health. ”.

Milburn’s report, the outlines of which have been widely trailed over the past few weeks, sets out in detail what he thinks should be done to reduce the number of young people not in education, employment or training (Neet).

The plan would involve the government spending nearly £2bn a year on a new youth opportunity service, which would provide support and advice to give every young person a guaranteed route into education, training or work.

It would involve spending just over £2bn to create more vocational training courses and apprenticeships, and a further £1bn in direct payments and tax breaks for companies that hire young people.

The new system would be paid for largely by taking disability and sickness benefits away from young people and replacing them with a single youth allowance, which would be considerably below what some people can claim currently.

People aged 18-24 would no longer be able to claim personal independence payments, which would be replaced by a new allowance available only to those whose conditions are “well established, significant and ongoing”.

Diungkapkan bahwa the benefits cuts would be expected to save £3. 4bn being generated by higher tax receipts. That money would be almost entirely swallowed by the £5. 6bn by 2036-37, with an additional £2. 8bn cost of the new system, Milburn said.

Sebagaimana diketahui, milburn began his review last year amid concern at the top of government over the rising numbers of young neets. That figure reached 1m earlier this year, equating to 13% of young people – a higher rate than in any European country except Romania.

Diungkapkan bahwa in his report, he argues: “our country is at a fork in the road. Or change course and make the difficult changes that can shift the trajectory. Go on as we are and see the Neet crisis grow. ”.

He says his proposals constitute a wholesale rethinking of how the benefits and education system works for young people, and should not be cherrypicked by ministers looking to impose only the ones they like.

Berdasarkan laporan, he has received public backing from the governments of burnham and his predecessor, keir starmer. When he addressed Labour MPs on Monday he was accompanied by the work and pensions secretary, Pat McFadden. McFadden and Burnham will speak to the parliamentary party about the plans again on Tuesday morning.

Diungkapkan bahwa ministers are hoping they can avoid a repeat of last year’s bruising welfare rebellion, when labour mps forced starmer to drop his plan to cut benefits by about £5bn a year. That humiliation arguably spelled the beginning of the end of Starmer’s time in office. Several of the architects of the rebellion now have government jobs, including the de facto deputy prime minister, Louise Haigh, and the chief whip, Anneliese Midgley.

Sebagaimana diketahui, at deutsche bank, a longtime bank of russian industry titans and oligarchs, officials scrambled to get ahead of the damage. “Russian Sanctions Urgent Request” read the subject line of an email sent by one of Deutsche’s anti-financial crime specialists to her colleagues.

Sebagaimana diketahui, this email exchange was the beginning of a frenzied reckoning within the scandal-plagued bank over its long resistance to breaking with russia’s most important business titans under vladimir v. Deripaska and Viktor F. Putin, the Russian president. The bank’s clients included the Russian billionaires Oleg V. Vekselberg. Time and again over many years, records show, Deutsche Bank’s risk managers warned that such relationships were perilous.

But profits associated with maintaining its Russian clients won out every time.

Diungkapkan bahwa russia’s war in ukraine swept up deutsche bank in a larger shift. For decades, German politicians and business leaders believed that working with Russia and deepening economic ties between the two countries would discourage Russian aggression. That strategy collapsed after the invasion.

Migrant workers who are financially exploited can now be considered victims of modern slavery, after a legal challenge by a care worker who was scammed out of £22,000 to pay an agent for a job in the UK that did not exist.

Diungkapkan bahwa the care worker, ali*, from pakistan, was put in contact with an agent who told him he could organise a certificate of sponsorship for him to work in a uk care home. The agent was recommended by a friend who said he had been helped to secure a UK care job.

After handing over £22,000 and obtaining what he thought was a genuine certificate of sponsorship and a health and care skilled worker visa from the Home Office, he, his wife and their two young children moved to the UK in October 2023, excited about their new start.

He was keen to begin work as soon as possible as he had incurred heavy debts owed to family members from whom he had borrowed money to cover the cost of obtaining the documents.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, after he arrived in the uk, he kept calling the number he had been given to find out when he could start work. “There is a worrying disconnect between those experiencing modern slavery and those getting help,” Piper said.

Diungkapkan bahwa ali was referred to the national referral mechanism for potential victims of trafficking and modern slavery and was initially found not to qualify as a potential victim of modern slavery. Supported by Work Rights Centre and Central England Law Centre, he challenged the home secretary for not including financial exploitation in the list of forms of modern slavery.

A judicial review was issued earlier this year and the decision was then reversed so that the Home Office will consider his case as one of potential human trafficking.

The Home Office has admitted in a court order that it previously “adopted an unduly narrow approach to the concept of exploitation” and said it would recognise financial exploitation as a form of modern slavery and trafficking.

Sebagaimana diketahui, tessa burwood, the solicitor at central england law centre who represented ali, said: “home office compliance checks for the health and care visa scheme are meant to ensure that vulnerable migrant care workers are only employed by genuine agencies and to prevent the forms of exploitation that are so commonplace in the sector. Sebagaimana diketahui, “the fact that financial exploitation will hopefully now be recognised as a form of modern slavery is a small step in the right direction but it is not the end of the nightmare for migrant care workers, who may still face years of uncertainty and instability due to the impact of this poorly conceived visa scheme. ”.

Tanggal: 17 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.theguardian.com/politics/2026/nov/17/chloe-moffat-policy-parents-treasury-worker-employers

Exclusive: Parents of Chloe Moffat urge employers to treat staff facing allegations in a kinder, more human way.

The parents of a Treasury worker who took her own life last year have launched a policy that directs employers to treat staff in a kinder and more commonsense way, and are asking HR departments across the country to adopt it.

Chloe Moffat’s parents also said the government department plans to plant a memorial garden in her honour at its Horse Guards Road offices.

Sebagaimana diketahui, moffat, a 26-year-old personal assistant, took her own life the day after she was called into a surprise disciplinary meeting about anonymous complaints alleging she had disclosed sensitive information at work, which she denied. A coroner found in August that the Treasury had “materially contributed” to her death.

Berdasarkan laporan, she had been convinced she would lose her job, the coroner heard, despite that not being a likely outcome. Moffat’s managers declined to allow her to bring a colleague to the “informal” meeting, did not give her any advance notice of it and refused to tell her whether she was likely to lose her job. They also removed access to her director’s email and changed her work responsibilities.

She had worked at the Treasury for almost three years, loved her job and had an exemplary employment record, the coroner heard.

Berdasarkan laporan, her parents, anne and david moffat, have been working with the global kindness institute, an ngo, to come up with “chloe’s policy” for hr departments to adopt to prevent such tragic incidents from happening in future. They are calling on organisations across the country to help develop and take on the policy.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, “all we want is for nobody else to go through this,” anne moffat said. “If it goes through HR departments, even people considering making allegations, everybody can hopefully follow the Chloe policy and ask if this is really necessary.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, “so many people are so policy driven and so into disciplinaries and making people accountable when it may not be necessary. People aren’t being treated in a commonsense, human way. ”.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the policy calls on hr departments to consider the harms of disciplinary processes to those subjected to them, particularly when complaints are anonymous or unverified. It emphasises prioritising psychological safety and supporting those going through any disciplinary process, as well as minimising these processes in the first place by considering alternatives. It also calls on HR departments to provide clarity to those going through disciplinary processes, including letting people know if their role is safe.

Sebagaimana diketahui, david moffat said: “it’s a powerful leadership standard. If it raises the profile of the process that Chloe went through and avoids it happening to anyone else, that is good enough for me. ”.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the treasury’s response to the coroner’s prevention of future deaths report acknowledged the department’s role in her death and committed to safeguards. A review of the civil service by the Cabinet Office found that the conditions to which Moffat was subjected had been replicated in other disciplinary meetings.

Anne Moffat said: “If you think about what happened to Chloe, if HR had thought ‘we know that she was very well thought of, nothing else had ever happened, these were the first ever allegations, they were anonymous,’ was this process necessary?”.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the prevention of future deaths report issued by the coroner last month found there was still a risk at the civil service due to its disciplinary procedures. The civil service has put in place multiple safeguards to address these issues. This guidance includes allowing staff to have a supporter in disciplinary meetings, giving proper notice of any such meeting, and informing staff if a dismissal is not likely. The Treasury is also hiring an on-site occupational therapist to support staff wellbeing.

Berdasarkan laporan, the moffats met james bowler, the permanent secretary at the treasury, at the end of last month. David said: “We felt listened to, and as part of their response to the coroner as well we felt reassured that change was being implemented. It was a very emotional meeting. If the changes they have put forward to the coroner had already been in place, we certainly feel that Chloe would be with us today. ”.

Diungkapkan bahwa anne added: “it is the first time we felt that the treasury had been compassionate to us and it wasn’t defensive or legal speak. They are looking at how to remember Chloe, and looking at the possibility of a memorial garden within the building and marking the garden with a plaque. ”.

Berdasarkan laporan, david said: “we feel that chloe is finally being acknowledged and remembered. ”.

A Treasury spokesperson said: “The Treasury’s deepest sympathies continue to be with Chloe’s friends and family, and the department continues to mourn our colleague.

Sebagaimana diketahui, “our response to the coroner’s prevention of future deaths report sets out the action we have taken following this tragic case. An independent review found staff acted in good faith and with a duty of care throughout. ”.

Debt Problems of the Richest Countries Are Trickling Down to the Poorest

Tanggal: 17 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.nytimes.com/2026/11/17/business/economy/global-debt-economy-world-bank.html

Sebagaimana diketahui, the debt load of developing countries jumped to $9. 4 trillion as high interest rates and other global shocks batter their economies.

Patricia Cohen covers the global economy and reported this story from Bangkok and London.

It’s hard to find a government these days that is not struggling with crushing public debt.

Berdasarkan laporan, the financial problems of wealthier nations have been monopolizing the spotlight. The United States, Britain, France, Italy, China and Japan are all facing record or near-record debt levels. The fallout has been painfully visible in France, where anger at rising costs and crumbling public facilities and services helped provoke violent protests and a general strike in recent weeks.

But rich countries’ fiscal problems do not just pool at home; they trickle down to amplify the financial pressures on low and middle-income countries.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the result is that less-well off nations are borrowing more and paying more for their loans. Their combined debt surged last year to $9. 4 trillion, according to a World Bank report this month.

The poorest of the poor countries fare the worst: They are facing interest rates not seen since the late 1980s.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, many of the causes are beyond their control. A series of crises, beginning with the Covid-19 pandemic, and continuing with energy shocks, supply chain disruptions and rising prices stemming from the wars in Ukraine and Iran have strained national budgets and pumped up debts.
